snippets.notes: The list is empty by default, which changes nothing. Add category slugs; posts from other categories still appear in their archives, search and feeds.

snippets.title: Skip Category and Tag Pages With Only One Post
snippets.description: Sends visitors straight to the post when a category or tag archive contains just one post, saving them a pointless extra click.
snippets.notes: Uses a temporary redirect, so the archive works normally again as soon as a second post is added.

snippets.title: Return 404 for Empty Category and Tag Pages
snippets.description: Shows your "not found" page with a 404 status for categories, tags and other terms that have no published posts, instead of an empty archive.

snippets.title: Hide Subcategory Posts From Parent Categories
snippets.description: Makes a category archive list only the posts assigned directly to that category, not the posts from its child categories.

snippets.title: Subcategory Links at the Top of Category Archives
snippets.description: Shows a row of links to the child categories at the top of a category archive, helping visitors drill down into large sections.
snippets.notes: Only categories with posts are listed. The position depends on where your theme starts the post loop.

snippets.title: Post Count in Archive Titles
snippets.description: Adds the number of posts to category, tag, author and date archive headings, for example "Recipes (42)".

snippets.title: Show Category Descriptions on the First Page Only
snippets.description: Hides category, tag and taxonomy descriptions on page 2 and beyond of an archive, so long intro texts are not repeated on every page.

snippets.title: Archives List Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds an [archives] shortcode that lists your posts by month or year, as a list or a dropdown, anywhere in content or widgets.
snippets.notes: Example: [archives type="yearly" show_count="yes"] or [archives type="monthly" limit="12" dropdown="yes"].

snippets.title: Category List Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [category_list] shortcode that prints a linked list of your categories, optionally with post counts and nested subcategories.
snippets.notes: Example: [category_list show_count="yes" exclude="1,7" taxonomy="category"].

snippets.title: Tag Cloud Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [tag_cloud] shortcode to show a tag cloud inside a page or post, with control over how many tags appear and how large they get.
snippets.notes: Example: [tag_cloud number="30" smallest="0.8" largest="1.6" taxonomy="post_tag"]. Sizes are in em.

snippets.title: Include Custom Post Types on Author Archives
snippets.description: Lists an author's portfolio items, recipes or other custom post type entries on their author page, not just their blog posts.
snippets.notes: Set the post types to include. They must support authors.

snippets.title: Include Custom Post Types on Category and Tag Archives
snippets.description: Makes category and tag archives list custom post type entries that use those categories and tags, not only regular posts.
snippets.notes: The custom post type must be registered with the category or post_tag taxonomy.

snippets.title: Disable Tag Archives
snippets.description: Redirects tag archive pages to the homepage and removes tags from the XML sitemap, for sites that use tags only internally.
snippets.notes: Your theme may still print tag links on posts; they will redirect to the homepage.

snippets.title: Disable Post Format Archives
snippets.description: Redirects the automatic archives for post formats (such as /type/gallery/) to the homepage and removes them from the sitemap.

snippets.title: Different Number of Posts on the First Blog Page
snippets.description: Shows a different number of posts on the first page of the blog than on the following pages, for example 3 featured posts up front and 10 per page after that, with pagination still correct.
snippets.notes: Later pages use the "Blog pages show at most" setting. Sticky posts are added on top of the first-page count by WordPress.

snippets.title: Stop Sticky Posts Jumping to the Top
snippets.description: Keeps sticky posts in normal date order on the blog page, so you can still mark posts as sticky for other uses without changing the main feed.

snippets.title: Sticky Posts First in Category Archives
snippets.description: Puts sticky posts at the top of the category archives they belong to, the same way WordPress already does on the blog page.
snippets.notes: Only the first page of each category archive is affected.

snippets.title: Page Number in Archive Headings
snippets.description: Adds "Page 2 of 7" to archive headings on paginated pages, so visitors and search engines can tell the pages apart.

snippets.title: Posts per Page on Author and Date Archives
snippets.description: Sets how many posts appear on author and date (year, month, day) archives, independent of the main blog setting.

snippets.title: Card Style for Query Loop Posts (SCSS)
snippets.description: Turns each post in Query Loop blocks into a card with padding, rounded corners, a soft shadow and a lift on hover, for blog and archive templates in block themes.
snippets.notes: Change the variables at the top to match your design. Works with list and grid layouts.

snippets.title: Newsletter Box After the Third Post in Lists
snippets.description: Inserts a newsletter sign-up box after the third post on the blog page, archives and search results, where browsing readers will see it.
snippets.code:
Get new posts by email

One short email when something new is published. Unsubscribe any time.

Subscribe
snippets.notes: Change the post number in the snippet settings and the link to your sign-up page or form.

snippets.title: Button-Style Pagination (SCSS)
snippets.description: Turns the page numbers under the blog, archives and Query Loop blocks into evenly sized rounded buttons with a clear current-page state.
snippets.notes: Covers classic theme pagination (.nav-links) and the Query Pagination block.

snippets.title: Featured Image Hover Zoom on Archives (SCSS)
snippets.description: Adds a gentle zoom to featured images on the blog page, archives and Query Loop blocks when visitors hover over a post, making lists feel more interactive.
snippets.notes: Motion is switched off for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

snippets.title: Allow Font, eBook and Data File Uploads for Administrators
snippets.description: Lets administrators upload web fonts (WOFF, WOFF2, TTF, OTF), EPUB eBooks, JSON and GPX files to the Media Library, which WordPress blocks by default.
snippets.notes: Other roles keep the default list. Add or remove extensions in $wpide_extra_mimes.

snippets.title: Tidy Image Titles on Upload
snippets.description: Turns file-name titles like "IMG_2041-sunset_beach-final" into readable ones like "Sunset beach final" when images are uploaded, so the Media Library is easier to search.
snippets.notes: Only titles that contain dashes or underscores are changed; titles read from the photo's own metadata stay as they are.

snippets.title: Minimum and Maximum Image Dimensions for Uploads
snippets.description: Rejects image uploads that are smaller or larger than the pixel sizes you set, so blurry thumbnails and oversized camera originals never reach the Media Library.
snippets.notes: Set any limit to 0 to switch it off. SVG files are not checked.

snippets.title: Change the Big Image Size Limit
snippets.description: Sets the size above which WordPress scales down very large uploaded images (2560 pixels by default), for example to 1920 pixels to save disk space and bandwidth.
snippets.notes: The original file is kept on the server; WordPress uses the scaled copy everywhere. To turn scaling off completely use the Disable Big Image Scaling snippet instead.

snippets.title: Save JPEG and PNG Uploads as WebP
snippets.description: Makes WordPress generate WebP versions instead of JPEG and PNG for every image size it creates on upload, which usually cuts image weight by a quarter or more.
snippets.notes: Needs a server whose GD or Imagick supports WebP; otherwise nothing changes. The original upload stays in its first format. Set the format to image/avif for AVIF.

snippets.title: "Uploaded By" Column in the Media Library
snippets.description: Adds a column to the Media Library list view showing who uploaded each file, with a link to see everything that person uploaded.

snippets.title: Default Featured Image
snippets.description: Uses an image of your choice as the featured image for posts that do not have one, so archive grids, related posts and social shares never show a gap.
snippets.notes: Upload the fallback image, copy its attachment ID from the Media Library and put it in $wpide_default_thumbnail_id.

snippets.title: Responsive Video Embeds for Classic Themes
snippets.description: Makes YouTube, Vimeo and other embedded videos scale to the width of the content on phones and tablets, for older themes that leave them at a fixed size.
snippets.notes: Block themes and themes that already declare responsive embeds are skipped automatically.

snippets.title: Privacy-Enhanced Mode for YouTube Embeds
snippets.description: Switches every embedded YouTube video to youtube-nocookie.com, YouTube's privacy-enhanced mode, which does not set tracking cookies until the visitor plays the video.

snippets.title: Show Only Your Own Related Videos on YouTube Embeds
snippets.description: Adds rel=0 to YouTube embeds so the suggestions shown when a video ends come from the same channel instead of from other creators.
snippets.notes: YouTube no longer allows hiding suggestions completely; rel=0 limits them to the video's own channel.

snippets.title: Change the Default Embed Size
snippets.description: Sets the default maximum width and height WordPress asks for when embedding videos and other media from a link.
snippets.notes: Embeds that are already cached keep their old size until the post is updated.

snippets.title: Show Custom Image Sizes in the Editor Size Menu
snippets.description: Adds every image size registered by your theme and plugins to the size dropdown in the editor and media modal, instead of only Thumbnail, Medium, Large and Full.

snippets.title: Sort Uploads Into Folders by File Type
snippets.description: Stores new uploads in images, videos, audio and documents folders inside your uploads directory, which keeps the file system tidy on large sites.
snippets.notes: Only new uploads are affected; existing files stay where they are. The year and month folders are kept inside each type folder when that setting is on.

snippets.title: Infinite Scrolling in the Media Library
snippets.description: Brings back infinite scrolling in the Media Library grid, so more files load as you scroll instead of clicking "Load more".
snippets.code: add_filter( 'media_library_infinite_scrolling', '__return_true' );

snippets.title: Photo Credit Field for Images
snippets.description: Adds a "Photo credit" field to images in the Media Library and prints the credit under the image whenever it is used in an Image block.
snippets.notes: The credit is added below Image blocks that point to the attachment; classic editor images are not changed.

snippets.title: Disable Right-Click and Dragging on Images
snippets.description: Stops visitors from right-clicking or dragging images to save them, a simple deterrent for photographers and artists.
snippets.notes: This only discourages casual copying; images can still be saved through browser tools or screenshots.

snippets.title: Link Gallery Images to the Full File by Default
snippets.description: Makes [gallery] shortcodes link each thumbnail to the full-size image and use medium-size thumbnails, unless the shortcode sets its own options.
snippets.notes: Applies to classic [gallery] shortcodes; Gallery blocks keep the settings chosen in the editor.

snippets.title: Turn On the Image Lightbox by Default
snippets.description: Switches on the built-in "Enlarge on click" lightbox for every Image block, so readers can view photos full screen without a lightbox plugin.
snippets.notes: Images linked to a page or file keep their link instead of the lightbox. Editors can still turn it off per image.

snippets.title: Allow Only Images and PDFs for Non-Administrators
snippets.description: Limits the file types authors, editors and other non-admin users can upload to common images and PDF documents.
snippets.notes: Administrators keep the full list. Add extensions in the same format WordPress uses, such as 'mp4|m4v'.

snippets.title: Do Not Preload Audio and Video Files
snippets.description: Sets audio and video players to preload nothing until the visitor presses play, saving bandwidth on pages with several media files.

snippets.title: Alt Text Column in the Media Library
snippets.description: Adds an Alt text column to the Media Library list view and flags images that have none, making accessibility clean-ups much quicker.

snippets.title: Disable PDF Preview Images
snippets.description: Stops WordPress from generating preview images for every uploaded PDF, saving disk space and server time when you upload many documents.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'fallback_intermediate_image_sizes', '__return_empty_array' );
snippets.notes: PDFs uploaded while this is active show a generic document icon in the Media Library.

snippets.title: Name Uploaded Files After Their Post
snippets.description: Renames files uploaded from inside the post editor to match the post's slug, so "DSC_0042.jpg" becomes "summer-menu.jpg", which is better for image search.
snippets.notes: Only files uploaded while editing a post or page are renamed. WordPress adds -1, -2 and so on when a name is taken.

snippets.title: Block Duplicate Uploads
snippets.description: Stops the same file from being uploaded twice by comparing a fingerprint of each new upload with files already in the Media Library, and tells the user where the existing copy is.
snippets.notes: Only files uploaded after the snippet is activated have a fingerprint, so older duplicates are not detected.

snippets.title: Fill Missing Alt Text in Bulk (Run Once)
snippets.description: A one-off task that gives every image without alt text a description based on its title. Run it from the snippet editor whenever you want to catch up.
snippets.notes: Processes up to 500 images per run; run it again for more. Review important images afterwards, as titles are not always good descriptions.

snippets.title: Gallery Hover Zoom (SCSS)
snippets.description: Adds rounded corners and a gentle zoom on hover to images in Gallery blocks and classic galleries, with motion turned off for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
snippets.notes: Adjust $radius and $zoom to taste.

snippets.title: Image Captions as Overlays (SCSS)
snippets.description: Places Image block captions on top of the bottom of the photo with a soft dark gradient, a magazine-style look that saves vertical space.
snippets.notes: Applies to Image blocks with captions inside post content.

snippets.title: Add nofollow to External Links in Content
snippets.description: Adds rel="nofollow" to links in posts and pages that point to other websites, while keeping any rel values already set. Links to your own domain are untouched.
snippets.notes: Add domains you trust to $wpide_follow_domains to keep their links followed.

snippets.title: Mark Affiliate Links as Sponsored
snippets.description: Adds rel="sponsored nofollow" to links that go to your affiliate programs or cloaked /go/ links, as search engines ask for paid links.
snippets.notes: List affiliate domains and any local link prefixes, such as /go/ or /recommends/, at the top.

snippets.title: Breadcrumbs Shortcode With Schema Markup
snippets.description: Adds a [breadcrumbs] shortcode that prints a Home > Category > Post trail with BreadcrumbList markup, so search results can show your site structure.
snippets.notes: Place [breadcrumbs] in a Shortcode block in your templates or at the top of content. Change the separator and home label at the top.

snippets.title: Breadcrumb Structured Data for Posts and Pages
snippets.description: Adds BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to posts (Home > Category > Post) and pages (Home > Parent > Page) so Google can show a breadcrumb trail instead of a raw URL.
snippets.notes: Skipped automatically when Yoast SEO, Rank Math, AIOSEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework is active.

snippets.title: FAQ Shortcode With FAQ Schema
snippets.description: Adds a [faq] shortcode for collapsible questions and answers, and outputs matching FAQPage structured data for every question on the page.
snippets.notes: Example: [faq question="Do you ship abroad?"]Yes, to most countries.[/faq]. Google now shows FAQ rich results mainly for authoritative sites, but the markup still describes your content.

snippets.title: Canonical URLs on Archive Pages
snippets.description: Adds canonical link tags to the blog page, category, tag, author and post type archives, which WordPress only does for single posts and pages by default.
snippets.notes: Each paginated page points to itself. Skipped when a major SEO plugin is active.

snippets.title: Exclude Specific Posts and Pages From the Sitemap
snippets.description: Leaves the posts and pages you list out of the built-in XML sitemap, such as thank-you pages, landing pages for ads or legal pages.
snippets.notes: Add the post or page IDs to the list. This does not noindex the pages; combine it with a noindex rule if they should not appear in search at all.

snippets.title: Last Modified Dates in the XML Sitemap
snippets.description: Adds the date each post was last updated to the built-in sitemap, which helps search engines find changed content faster.

snippets.title: Change the Number of URLs per Sitemap Page
snippets.description: Changes how many links each page of the built-in XML sitemap holds (2,000 by default), for example to split a huge sitemap into smaller files.
snippets.notes: Values between 100 and 50,000 are allowed by the sitemap protocol.

snippets.title: Change the Title Separator
snippets.description: Changes the character between the page name and the site name in browser tabs and search results, for example from a dash to a vertical bar.
snippets.notes: Some SEO plugins set their own separator and ignore this one.

snippets.title: Custom Title for the Homepage
snippets.description: Sets the browser and search result title of the homepage to the exact text you choose instead of "Site Name - Tagline".
snippets.notes: Skip this if an SEO plugin already manages your homepage title.

snippets.title: Remove the Site Name From Post Titles
snippets.description: Shows only the post or page name in the browser tab and search results on single posts and pages, leaving more room for a descriptive title.
snippets.notes: Set $wpide_title_post_types to limit it to certain post types.

snippets.title: WebSite Structured Data With Site Search
snippets.description: Adds WebSite JSON-LD to the homepage, including a SearchAction that tells search engines how your site search works.
snippets.notes: Skipped when a major SEO plugin is active, as they output the same data.

snippets.title: Local Business Structured Data
snippets.description: Adds LocalBusiness JSON-LD with your address, phone, opening hours and map location to the homepage, to support local search and map results.
snippets.notes: Fill in your details at the top. Use a more specific type such as Restaurant, Dentist or Store when one fits.

snippets.title: Author Profile Structured Data
snippets.description: Adds ProfilePage JSON-LD to author archives, describing the author as a person with their name, bio, avatar and website.
snippets.notes: Author archives must be enabled for this to have any effect.

snippets.title: Noindex Selected Posts and Pages
snippets.description: Asks search engines not to index the posts and pages you list, such as thank-you, login or internal pages, while still following their links.
snippets.notes: Add the IDs to the list. Pair it with the sitemap exclusion snippet so the pages are not listed there either.

snippets.title: Block AI Training Crawlers in robots.txt
snippets.description: Adds rules to your virtual robots.txt that ask AI training bots such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot and Google-Extended not to crawl your site.
snippets.notes: robots.txt is a request, not an enforcement. A physical robots.txt file in the site root overrides the virtual one. Edit the list to allow bots you want.

snippets.title: SEO Title, Description and Noindex Fields
snippets.description: Adds a small SEO box to the editor of posts and pages with a custom title, a meta description and a "hide from search engines" option, for sites without an SEO plugin.
snippets.notes: Do not combine it with an SEO plugin or with the Automatic Meta Description snippet, or pages will get two descriptions. Noindexed entries are also left out of the XML sitemap.

snippets.title: Notify IndexNow When Content Is Published
snippets.description: Tells search engines that support IndexNow (Bing, Yandex, Seznam and others) about new and updated posts as soon as they are published, so they are crawled sooner.
snippets.notes: Only runs on sites whose environment type is production. A key is generated on first use and served at /your-key.txt as the protocol requires.

snippets.title: X (Twitter) Handle Meta Tags
snippets.description: Adds twitter:site with your brand's X handle to every page, and twitter:creator with the author's handle on posts, so shared links credit the right accounts.
snippets.notes: The author handle is read from a user meta field named twitter; leave it empty and only the site handle is used.

snippets.title: Article Published and Modified Date Meta Tags
snippets.description: Adds article:published_time and article:modified_time meta tags to blog posts, which social networks and search engines use to understand how fresh a post is.

snippets.title: Noindex Posts in Selected Categories
snippets.description: Keeps posts from the categories you choose, such as internal news or short announcements, out of search engine results.
snippets.notes: Use category slugs. The category archive pages themselves are noindexed too.

snippets.title: Noindex Category and Tag Pages With Few Posts
snippets.description: Adds noindex to category, tag and custom taxonomy archives that hold fewer posts than a minimum, so near-empty pages do not dilute your search presence.
snippets.notes: Change the minimum number of posts at the top. The pages start being indexed again once they reach it.

snippets.title: Add Custom URLs to the XML Sitemap
snippets.description: Adds a sitemap of extra URLs, such as static landing pages or sections served outside WordPress, to the built-in sitemap index.
snippets.notes: List full URLs on your own domain. The new sitemap appears at /wp-sitemap-extra-1.xml and in /wp-sitemap.xml.

snippets.title: HTML Sitemap Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds an [html_sitemap] shortcode that lists all your pages and your posts grouped by category, giving visitors and crawlers one page that links to everything.
snippets.notes: Use [html_sitemap posts_per_category="20"] to limit long categories, or [html_sitemap show_posts="no"] to list pages only.

snippets.title: Allow Full Text and Video Previews in Search Results
snippets.description: Adds max-snippet:-1 and max-video-preview:-1 to the robots meta tag, letting search engines show longer text snippets and video previews for your pages.
snippets.notes: WordPress already allows large image previews; this adds the matching text and video settings.

snippets.title: Breadcrumb Trail Styling (SCSS)
snippets.description: Styles breadcrumb trails from the Breadcrumbs shortcode and popular SEO plugins with smaller muted text, chevron separators and a clear current page.
snippets.notes: Adjust $muted and the separator character to taste.

snippets.title: Featured Images as media:content in RSS
snippets.description: Adds each post's featured image to the RSS feed as a media:content element, the format email newsletter tools and feed readers use to show a thumbnail.
snippets.notes: Mailchimp, Feedly and most RSS-to-email services read this element. The image size is set at the top.

snippets.title: Keep Tagged Posts Out of RSS Feeds
snippets.description: Leaves any post with a "no-feed" tag out of all RSS feeds, so you can publish a post on the site without sending it to subscribers and newsletter tools.
snippets.notes: Create a tag with the slug no-feed (or change the slug at the top) and add it to posts you want to hide from feeds.

snippets.title: JSON Feed for Your Posts
snippets.description: Publishes your latest posts as a JSON Feed at /feed/json/, a modern alternative to RSS supported by many feed readers and easy to use from apps and scripts.
snippets.notes: With pretty permalinks, visit Settings > Permalinks once after activating so the /feed/json/ address works; ?feed=json works right away.

snippets.title: Tell Feed Readers How Often to Check
snippets.description: Sets the update period and time-to-live in your RSS feed, so feed readers check a daily blog once a day instead of every hour.
snippets.notes: Readers treat these values as hints. Match them to how often you actually publish.

snippets.title: Display an External RSS Feed With a Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds an [rss_feed] shortcode that shows the latest items from any RSS or Atom feed, such as your podcast, YouTube channel or a partner blog, on a page.
snippets.notes: Example: [rss_feed url="https://example.com/feed/" items="5" show_date="yes" show_summary="no"]. Feeds are cached for 12 hours by WordPress.

snippets.title: "Read the Full Article" Link in Feeds
snippets.description: Adds a link back to the post at the end of every feed item, so readers who see a summary in their reader or inbox can click through to your site.
snippets.notes: Change the link text at the top.

snippets.title: Campaign Tags on Feed Item Links
snippets.description: Adds utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign parameters to the links in your RSS feed, so visits from feed readers and RSS emails show up clearly in your analytics.
snippets.notes: Change the parameter values to match your analytics naming.

snippets.title: Custom Title for Your RSS Feeds
snippets.description: Sets the title feed readers and podcast apps show for your feeds, for example "Acme Blog" instead of the full site name and archive name.

snippets.title: Use Your Logo as the Feed Image
snippets.description: Shows your own logo in feed readers instead of the site icon, which is often too small or too simple for that space.
snippets.notes: Put the full URL of a square image of at least 144 pixels in $wpide_feed_logo, or leave it empty to use the theme's custom logo.

snippets.title: Keep Password-Protected Posts Out of Feeds
snippets.description: Removes password-protected posts from all feeds, where they otherwise appear with a "There is no excerpt because this is a protected post" message.

snippets.title: Remove Images From Feed Content
snippets.description: Strips images and image captions from the content sent in your feeds, keeping feeds light for readers and services that only want the text.
snippets.notes: The featured image added by other feed snippets is not affected.

snippets.title: Keep Feeds Out of Search Results
snippets.description: Sends an X-Robots-Tag header that asks search engines not to index your RSS feeds, so feed URLs do not compete with your real pages.
snippets.notes: Feed readers ignore this header, so subscribers are not affected.

snippets.title: Order Feeds by Last Updated Date
snippets.description: Lists feed items by the date they were last updated instead of the publish date, so readers see refreshed articles again.
snippets.notes: Some readers show an updated post as a new item. Use it if you regularly refresh older content.

snippets.title: Only Include Recent Posts in Feeds
snippets.description: Limits your feeds to posts published in the last few days, which keeps them short for busy news sites and stops readers re-importing old items.
snippets.notes: Change the number of days at the top. A feed can be empty if nothing was published in that time.

snippets.title: Fix Relative Links and Images in Feeds
snippets.description: Turns relative links and image paths such as "/about/" in feed content into full URLs, so they work in feed readers and RSS emails.

snippets.title: Remove Category, Tag and Author Feed Links From the Head
snippets.description: Stops WordPress from advertising separate feeds for every category, tag, author, search and archive page, while keeping your main feed link.
snippets.notes: The feeds still work if someone visits them directly. Use the Remove Comment Feeds snippet for comment feed links.

snippets.title: Feed-Only and Hide-in-Feed Shortcodes
snippets.description: Adds [feed_only] and [hide_in_feed] shortcodes, so you can show a special message to RSS subscribers or keep interactive parts of a post out of feeds.
snippets.notes: Example: [hide_in_feed]Interactive calculator here[/hide_in_feed][feed_only]Visit the post to use the calculator.[/feed_only]

snippets.title: RSS Subscribe Box After Posts
snippets.description: Adds a small box at the end of each blog post inviting readers to follow the site by RSS, with a link to your feed.
snippets.code: Never miss a post: subscribe with your RSS reader.
snippets.notes: Edit the wording in the snippet; the feed URL is filled in automatically.

snippets.title: Refresh External RSS Feeds More Often
snippets.description: Changes how long WordPress caches feeds fetched from other sites for the RSS widget and feed shortcodes, which is 12 hours by default.
snippets.notes: Very short times add load to your server and to the source site; one hour is a sensible minimum.

snippets.title: Choose Which Post Types Appear in Search
snippets.description: Sets exactly which content types the site search returns, for example posts, pages and your portfolio, instead of every public type.
snippets.notes: List the post type names to include. Types that do not exist are ignored.

snippets.title: Search Inside Custom Fields
snippets.description: Lets the site search also match text stored in custom fields, such as a subtitle, location or product code, not just titles and content.
snippets.notes: List the field names to search. Leave the list empty to search every visible custom field, which is slower on big sites.

snippets.title: Match Category and Tag Names in Search
snippets.description: Makes the site search also return posts whose categories or tags match the search words, so searching "recipes" finds everything filed under Recipes.
snippets.notes: Add custom taxonomies to $wpide_search_taxonomies to include them too.

snippets.title: Exclude a Category From Search Results
snippets.description: Keeps posts from the categories you choose, such as internal updates or sponsored posts, out of the site search results.
snippets.notes: Use category IDs. Posts stay visible in their category archives.

snippets.title: Sort Search Results by Newest First
snippets.description: Lists search results by publish date, newest first, instead of WordPress's relevance order, which suits news sites and blogs where freshness matters most.

snippets.title: Minimum Search Term Length
snippets.description: Ignores searches shorter than a few characters, which return huge, useless result lists and put extra load on the database.
snippets.notes: Short searches show the normal "nothing found" page.

snippets.title: Block Spam Searches
snippets.description: Answers search requests that contain links, markup, very long strings or words you block with a 404, stopping bots from filling search pages with spam.
snippets.notes: Add words to $wpide_blocked_search_words. Legitimate visitors rarely search for URLs, so they are blocked too.

snippets.title: Noindex Search Result Pages
snippets.description: Asks search engines not to index your internal search result pages, which are thin, endless and a favorite target for spam links.

snippets.title: Search Form Shortcode With Post Type Filter
snippets.description: Adds a [search_form] shortcode that places a search box anywhere and can limit results to certain post types, such as a docs-only or products-only search.
snippets.notes: Example: [search_form post_type="docs" placeholder="Search the docs" button="Go"]. Pages cannot be targeted this way because WordPress does not allow them in query URLs.

snippets.title: Log Site Searches in a Dashboard Widget
snippets.description: Records what visitors search for, how often, and whether anything was found, and shows the top searches in a dashboard widget so you can spot missing content.
snippets.notes: Searches by logged-in editors are not counted. The log keeps the 300 most recent distinct terms in one option.

snippets.title: Show the Number of Search Results
snippets.description: Prints a line such as 12 results for "pricing" above the search results, so visitors know how much was found.
snippets.notes: The line appears where your theme starts the results loop.

snippets.title: Rate-Limit Site Searches
snippets.description: Limits how many searches one visitor can run per minute and answers the rest with "429 Too Many Requests", protecting your database from search floods.
snippets.notes: Visitors are identified by an anonymous hash of their IP address. Behind a proxy or CDN that hides visitor IPs, everyone may share one limit.

snippets.title: Search for the Whole Phrase
snippets.description: Makes multi-word searches match the exact phrase instead of any page that contains all the words somewhere, giving tighter results on large sites.
snippets.notes: Visitors get fewer results, so test it with common searches first.

snippets.title: Instant Search Suggestions
snippets.description: Shows a dropdown of matching posts and pages under every search box as the visitor types, using the built-in REST API search.
snippets.notes: Suggestions start after three characters. Style the dropdown with the .wpide-live-results class.

snippets.title: Press "/" to Jump to the Search Box
snippets.description: Lets visitors press the slash key on any page to put the cursor in the search box, a shortcut many people know from popular websites.
snippets.notes: The shortcut is ignored while the visitor is typing in a form field.

snippets.title: Show the Matching Text in Search Results
snippets.description: Replaces the usual opening-lines excerpt in search results with the passage of the post that actually contains the search words.
snippets.notes: Combine it with the Highlight Search Terms snippet to mark the words inside the passage.

snippets.title: Search WooCommerce Products by SKU
snippets.description: Lets shoppers find products by typing their SKU into the store search, including SKUs of individual variations.
snippets.notes: Uses WooCommerce's product lookup table, so it stays fast on large catalogs.

snippets.title: Product Search Box Above the Shop
snippets.description: Places the WooCommerce product search box above the product grid on the shop and product category pages.
snippets.notes: Style it with the .wpide-shop-search class.

snippets.title: Search Post Titles Only
snippets.description: Restricts the site search to titles, so results contain only posts whose title matches, which is useful for glossaries, directories and recipe sites.
snippets.notes: Requires WordPress 6.2 or newer.

snippets.title: Search Box in the Main Menu
snippets.description: Adds the search form as the last item of a classic theme's main navigation menu.
snippets.notes: Set the theme menu location; it is often primary or main. Block themes should add a Search block to the Navigation block instead.

snippets.title: Rounded Pill Search Form (SCSS)
snippets.description: Restyles the theme search form and the Search block as a single rounded pill with an inline button and a clear focus ring.
snippets.notes: Change $accent to your brand color.

snippets.title: Search Term Highlight Style (SCSS)
snippets.description: Gives highlighted search words a soft marker-pen look instead of the browser's default yellow box, matching the Highlight Search Terms snippet and any mark elements.
snippets.notes: Change $marker to your brand color; dark mode uses a deeper tone automatically.

snippets.title: Widget Area Above Single Posts
snippets.description: Registers a "Before Post Content" widget area and shows its widgets at the top of every blog post, ideal for notices, ads or a table of contents widget.
snippets.notes: Add widgets under Appearance > Widgets. Nothing is printed while the area is empty.

snippets.title: Widget Area at the Top of Every Page
snippets.description: Adds a "Top Bar" widget area that prints right after the opening body tag, handy for a contact line, social links or a short promo across the whole site.
snippets.notes: Your theme must call wp_body_open(), which all modern themes do.

snippets.title: Show Widgets Only to Logged-In or Logged-Out Visitors
snippets.description: Adds a "Show to" setting to every classic widget so you can display it to everyone, only to logged-in users, or only to visitors who are not logged in.
snippets.notes: Works with classic widgets and the Legacy Widget block. Block widgets do not have the setting.

snippets.title: Hide a Sidebar on Selected Pages or Post Types
snippets.description: Empties a widget area on the pages or post types you choose, for example to keep the sidebar off landing pages and checkout pages.
snippets.notes: Set the sidebar ID (shown in Appearance > Widgets or your theme's code). Some themes still reserve the column; switch those pages to a full-width template if so.

snippets.title: Exclude a Category From the Recent Posts Widget
snippets.description: Keeps posts from the categories you choose out of the classic Recent Posts widget, for example sponsored posts or internal news.
snippets.notes: Use category IDs. The Latest Posts block has its own category setting.

snippets.title: Hide Staff Replies in the Recent Comments Widget
snippets.description: Leaves comments written by authors, editors and administrators out of the Recent Comments widget, so it highlights what readers are saying.

snippets.title: Archives Widget: Yearly Links and a Limit
snippets.description: Changes the classic Archives widget to list years instead of months and caps how many entries it shows, keeping the sidebar short on old blogs.
snippets.notes: Set the type to monthly to keep months and only apply the limit.

snippets.title: Tag Cloud Widget: Most Popular Tags Only
snippets.description: Limits the Tag Cloud widget and block to your most used tags and orders them by popularity, so the cloud stays readable on sites with hundreds of tags.

snippets.title: Pages Widget: Exclude Pages and Sort by Menu Order
snippets.description: Hides pages such as Privacy Policy or Thank You from the Pages widget and sorts the rest by their menu order.
snippets.notes: Use page IDs.

snippets.title: Custom CSS Classes for Widgets
snippets.description: Adds a "CSS classes" field to every classic widget, so you can style individual widgets from your theme or a CSS snippet.
snippets.notes: Separate several classes with spaces. Works with classic widgets and the Legacy Widget block.

snippets.title: Recent Posts Widget With Thumbnails
snippets.description: Adds a "Recent Posts With Thumbnails" widget that lists your latest posts with a small featured image and optional date, for classic sidebars.
snippets.notes: Add it under Appearance > Widgets (as a Legacy Widget in the block widget editor).

snippets.title: Contact Details Widget
snippets.description: Adds a "Contact Details" widget for your address, phone number, email and opening hours, with tap-to-call and spam-protected email links.
snippets.notes: Add it under Appearance > Widgets (as a Legacy Widget in the block widget editor).

snippets.title: Hide Widget Titles That Start With "!"
snippets.description: Lets you keep a descriptive widget title in the admin but hide it on the site, just by starting the title with an exclamation mark.
snippets.notes: Example: a widget titled "!Newsletter form" shows no heading on the site.

snippets.title: Keep the Last Sidebar Widget in View
snippets.description: Makes the last widget in the sidebar stick to the top of the screen while the visitor scrolls long posts, a good spot for a newsletter form or ad.
snippets.notes: Only applies on screens wider than 1024 pixels. Adjust the selectors if your theme uses different sidebar classes.

snippets.title: Widget Area Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [widget_area] shortcode that prints any widget area inside a page, post or block template, so the same widgets can be reused anywhere.
snippets.notes: Example: [widget_area id="sidebar-1"]. Find the IDs of your widget areas in your theme or with the Register Extra Widget Areas snippet.

snippets.title: Register Extra Widget Areas
snippets.description: Creates additional widget areas, such as a shop sidebar or a blog sidebar, that you can fill under Appearance > Widgets and place with a shortcode or theme hook.
snippets.notes: Add or rename areas in the list. Show them with [widget_area id="..."] from the Widget Area Shortcode snippet.

snippets.title: Limit the Blocks Available in the Widget Editor
snippets.description: Restricts the block widget editor and the Customizer to a short list of blocks that make sense in sidebars, keeping widget areas tidy for clients.
snippets.notes: Edit the list to allow more blocks. Blocks already placed in widget areas keep working.

snippets.title: Recent Posts Widget Follows the Current Category
snippets.description: Makes the classic Recent Posts widget list posts from the same category as the post being read, turning it into a simple related posts list.
snippets.notes: On pages other than single posts the widget shows the latest posts as usual.

snippets.title: Filters Widget Area Above the Shop
snippets.description: Registers a "Shop Filters" widget area and shows it above the product grid on shop and category pages, a natural home for price, attribute and rating filters.
snippets.notes: Works with classic WooCommerce shop templates. Block-based shop templates should use the Product Filters blocks instead.

snippets.title: Sidebar Widgets as Cards (SCSS)
snippets.description: Styles each sidebar widget as a card with a border, rounded corners, an underlined title and tidy list dividers.
snippets.notes: Adjust the variables at the top. Selectors cover the usual classic theme sidebar classes.

snippets.title: Tag Cloud as Pills (SCSS)
snippets.description: Restyles the Tag Cloud widget and block as a tidy row of rounded pills with equal font sizes, which reads better than a jumble of sizes.
snippets.notes: Font sizes set by the tag cloud are overridden on purpose.

snippets.title: Allowed Blocks per Post Type
snippets.description: Limits the blocks that can be inserted for specific post types, so structured content such as testimonials or team members only uses the blocks that fit.
snippets.notes: Post types that are not listed keep every block. Blocks already in a post keep working.

snippets.title: Use the Classic Editor for Selected Pages or Templates
snippets.description: Opens specific pages, or pages using certain templates, in the classic editor while everything else keeps the block editor.
snippets.notes: List page IDs and template file names, such as template-legacy.php. Requires the classic editor to be available (it is built in for posts that opt out).

snippets.title: Register Your Own Block Pattern
snippets.description: Adds a reusable "Call to action" pattern in its own "My Patterns" category to the block inserter, as a starting point for your own patterns.
snippets.code:
add_action( 'init', function () { register_block_pattern_category( 'wpide-patterns', array( 'label' => 'My Patterns' ) ); register_block_pattern( 'wpide/call-to-action', array( 'title' => 'Call to action', 'description' => 'A centered heading, short text and a button.', 'categories' => array( 'wpide-patterns', 'call-to-action' ), 'keywords' => array( 'cta', 'button', 'banner' ), 'content' => '

Ready to get started?

Tell visitors what they get and why it matters.

Contact us
', ) ); } );
snippets.notes: Design the layout in the editor, copy it with "Copy" from the block toolbar and paste the markup into the content setting.

snippets.title: Extra Block Styles: Card, Pill Button, Shadow Image and Checklist
snippets.description: Adds four ready-made style options to the block editor: a card style for Group blocks, a pill style for buttons, a soft shadow for images and a checkmark style for lists.
snippets.notes: Pick the styles in the block sidebar under Styles. Edit the CSS in each inline_style to match your design.

snippets.title: Remove Built-In Block Style Options
snippets.description: Removes block style choices you do not want editors to use, such as the outline button, rounded image or dotted separator, keeping the design consistent.
snippets.notes: Edit the list of block names and style names. Content that already uses a removed style keeps its look.

snippets.title: Limit the Embed Providers in the Inserter
snippets.description: Hides the long list of embed blocks (TikTok, Reddit, Kickstarter and dozens more) from the inserter, keeping only the providers you actually use.
snippets.notes: Pasting a URL from a hidden provider still embeds it. Provider names are lowercase, such as youtube, vimeo, twitter, spotify or soundcloud.

snippets.title: Lock Colors and Sizes to the Theme Presets
snippets.description: Removes the custom color picker, custom gradients and free-form font and spacing sizes from the editor, so editors can only choose from your theme's palette and scales.
snippets.notes: Existing content with custom values keeps them. Works with block and classic themes.

snippets.title: Add Brand Colors to the Editor Palette
snippets.description: Adds your brand colors to the color palette in the block editor, next to the theme's colors, so the exact shades are one click away.
snippets.notes: Colors with a slug the theme already uses replace the theme color. Each color also becomes a CSS variable such as --wp--preset--color--brand.

snippets.title: Add Custom Font Sizes to the Editor
snippets.description: Adds your own named font sizes, such as "Lead" or "Display", to the font size picker in the block editor alongside the theme's sizes.
snippets.notes: Sizes accept any CSS length, including clamp() for fluid type. A slug the theme already uses replaces the theme size.

snippets.title: Wider Content Area in the Editor
snippets.description: Makes the writing area of the block editor wider, giving more room on large screens without changing how the site looks to visitors.
snippets.notes: Set any CSS width such as 1000px or 75rem.

snippets.title: Block Template for New Posts
snippets.description: Starts every new post with a set of placeholder blocks, such as a summary paragraph, a heading and an image, so writers follow the same structure.
snippets.notes: Change the post type, the blocks and the lock. Lock 'insert' stops blocks being added or removed; 'all' also stops moving them.

snippets.title: Skip the Pre-Publish Checks Panel by Default
snippets.description: Publishes posts with a single click instead of opening the "Are you ready to publish?" panel first. Each user can still switch the panel back on in the editor preferences.

snippets.title: Hide Template Editing in the Post Editor
snippets.description: Removes the option to switch to and edit the site template from inside the post and page editor, so content editors cannot change the site layout by accident.
snippets.notes: Administrators can still edit templates in the Site Editor.

snippets.title: Disable Duotone Filters
snippets.description: Removes the duotone image filter controls from the editor and stops WordPress outputting the default duotone presets.

snippets.title: Simplify the Editor's Typography Controls
snippets.description: Hides letter spacing, text transform, text decoration, font style, font weight, line height and writing mode controls, leaving a calmer sidebar for content editors.
snippets.notes: Remove lines from the list to keep a control.

snippets.title: Turn On Modern Block Features in Classic Themes
snippets.description: Enables wide and full alignments, responsive embeds, spacing, border, line height and link color controls for classic themes that never declared them.
snippets.notes: Your theme's CSS decides how wide alignments look; test a few pages after enabling it.

snippets.title: Outline Blocks While Editing
snippets.description: Draws a faint dashed outline around blocks as you hover over them in the editor, making nested groups, columns and empty blocks easy to see.

snippets.title: Hide the Custom HTML Block From Non-Administrators
snippets.description: Removes the Custom HTML block from the inserter for users who cannot post unfiltered HTML, so authors use proper blocks instead of pasting raw markup.
snippets.notes: Existing Custom HTML blocks stay editable; only inserting new ones is hidden.

snippets.title: Synced Pattern Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [synced_pattern] shortcode that prints a synced pattern (formerly reusable block) anywhere shortcodes work, such as classic widgets, page builders or theme files.
snippets.notes: Example: [synced_pattern id="123"]. Find the ID in Appearance > Patterns by opening the pattern and checking the address bar.

snippets.title: Insert Images at Large Size by Default
snippets.description: Makes new Image blocks and media inserted in the editor use the Large size by default, instead of the full original file.
snippets.notes: Change large to medium or another registered size.

snippets.title: Disable the Theme's Block Patterns
snippets.description: Removes the patterns bundled with your active theme from the inserter, for sites that only want their own patterns.
snippets.notes: Patterns from WordPress core and plugins are not affected. Use Disable Core Block Patterns for those.

snippets.title: Turn Off the Starter Patterns Window for New Pages
snippets.description: Stops the "Choose a pattern" window from popping up every time someone creates a new page. Users can switch it back on in the editor preferences.

snippets.title: Limit Heading Levels in the Editor
snippets.description: Shows only the heading levels you allow (for example H2 to H4) in the Heading block toolbar, so editors keep a clean document outline and never add a second H1.
snippets.notes: Requires WordPress 6.7 or newer. Existing headings keep their level.

snippets.title: Remove Formatting Buttons From the Block Toolbar
snippets.description: Removes rarely needed formatting options, such as text color highlight, inline image, keyboard input and language, from the rich text toolbar.
snippets.notes: Format names include core/text-color, core/image, core/keyboard, core/language, core/subscript, core/superscript, core/code and core/strikethrough.

snippets.title: Hide Blocks on Mobile or Desktop With a CSS Class
snippets.description: Adds hide-on-mobile, hide-on-tablet and hide-on-desktop classes you can put in any block's "Additional CSS class" field to show it only on certain screen sizes.
snippets.notes: Breakpoints are 600px and 1024px; change them to match your theme.

snippets.title: Default Block Editor Preferences for Everyone
snippets.description: Sets sensible defaults for every user of the block editor, such as the top toolbar, the List View opened and button text labels, while each person can still change them.
snippets.notes: Only defaults change; anything a user has already set in Preferences wins. Set a value to true or false to taste.

snippets.title: Button Block Hover Effects (SCSS)
snippets.description: Adds a smooth lift, shadow and color shift when visitors hover over or focus Button blocks, with motion turned off for people who prefer reduced motion.
snippets.notes: Adjust the lift distance and shadow in the variables.

snippets.title: Bind Blocks to Site Details (Block Bindings)
snippets.description: Registers a Block Bindings source so Paragraph, Heading and Button blocks can display the site name, tagline, URL or current year and stay up to date automatically.
snippets.notes: Requires WordPress 6.5 or newer. In the code editor use for example {"metadata":{"bindings":{"content":{"source":"wpide/site-details","args":{"key":"year"}}}}} on a Paragraph block. Keys are name, tagline, url and year.

snippets.title: Make a Custom Field Usable in Blocks
snippets.description: Registers a custom field (such as a subtitle) with the REST API so it can be connected to Paragraph or Heading blocks through Block Bindings and edited right in the block.
snippets.notes: Requires WordPress 6.5 or newer. Bind it with {"metadata":{"bindings":{"content":{"source":"core/post-meta","args":{"key":"subtitle"}}}}}. Change the post type and field name at the top.

snippets.title: Accordion Style for the Details Block (SCSS)
snippets.description: Styles the core Details block as a polished accordion with borders, a rotating plus icon and comfortable spacing, so FAQs look finished without a plugin.
snippets.notes: Consecutive Details blocks join into one accordion list.

snippets.title: Utility Classes for Blocks (SCSS)
snippets.description: Adds a small set of classes, such as has-shadow, is-rounded, has-hover-lift and text-balance, that editors can type into any block's "Additional CSS class" field.
snippets.notes: Add more utilities in the same style. The class names have no prefix so editors can remember them easily.

snippets.title: Legal Disclaimer After Content (Blocks)
snippets.description: Adds a small, separated disclaimer built from blocks at the end of posts and pages, for example a "not financial or medical advice" notice.
snippets.code: Disclaimer: This content is for general information only and is not professional advice. Please consult a qualified professional before making decisions based on it.
snippets.notes: Edit the wording in the snippet editor and use conditions to limit it to certain categories if needed.

snippets.title: Force HTTPS on the Front End
snippets.description: Sends visitors who open a page over plain HTTP to the secure HTTPS address with a permanent redirect, once your site URL is set to https.
snippets.notes: Only runs when the Site Address already starts with https. Proxies and CDNs that report HTTPS through standard headers are detected, so it does not loop behind Cloudflare or a load balancer.

snippets.title: Redirect to the www or Non-www Version of Your Domain
snippets.description: Sends visitors who arrive on the other version of your domain (with or without www) to the one set as your Site Address, so search engines see a single site.
snippets.notes: Your host must point both versions to this site. A redirect at the server or DNS level is faster when available.

snippets.title: Redirect URLs With Capital Letters to Lowercase
snippets.description: Permanently redirects addresses typed or linked with capital letters, such as /About-Us/, to their lowercase form, avoiding duplicate URLs and broken links.
snippets.notes: Encoded characters such as %C3%A9 are left as they are. Query strings are kept unchanged.

snippets.title: Send Single Entries of a Post Type to Its Archive
snippets.description: Redirects the single pages of post types that only make sense in a list, such as testimonials, FAQs or team members, to their archive or another page.
snippets.notes: Set the post types and, optionally, a fixed target path. Without a target, the post type archive (or the homepage) is used.

snippets.title: Send Empty Parent Pages to Their First Child Page
snippets.description: When a parent page has no content of its own (it only groups subpages in the menu), visitors who open it are sent to its first child page instead of a blank page.
snippets.notes: Only pages whose content is completely empty are redirected; the first child is chosen by menu order, then title. The redirect is temporary, so adding content later works right away.

snippets.title: Wildcard Redirects for Moved Sections
snippets.description: Redirects whole groups of old URLs with simple * patterns, for example everything under /old-blog/ to the same address under /blog/, without a redirect plugin.
snippets.notes: The rule list is empty by default; add your own using the examples. Use * for any text and $1, $2 in the target for what each * matched. On a subdirectory install include the subdirectory in the patterns. Redirects to the same address are skipped, so a rule cannot loop.

snippets.title: Turn 404 Errors Into Search Results
snippets.description: Sends visitors who hit a missing page to a site search for the words in the broken address, so they land on likely matches instead of a dead end.
snippets.notes: Missing files such as images, scripts and PDFs still return a normal 404.

snippets.title: Log 404 Errors Under Tools
snippets.description: Records the addresses visitors request that do not exist, with hit counts, last seen time and referring page, and lists them under Tools > 404 Log so you can fix or redirect them.
snippets.notes: Keeps the 200 most recent distinct addresses in one option. Clear the log from the same screen.

snippets.title: Send Logged-In Members From the Homepage to Their Page
snippets.description: Redirects logged-in users who visit the homepage to a members area, dashboard or account page, while guests still see the normal homepage.
snippets.notes: Nothing happens until the target page exists. Users with the capability in $wpide_member_home_skip (editors and up by default) still see the homepage.

snippets.title: Redirect Field for Posts and Pages
snippets.description: Adds a "Redirect to" box to the post and page editor; when filled in, visitors who open that post are sent to the address you entered, on your site or elsewhere.
snippets.notes: Uses a permanent (301) redirect. Clear the field to switch it off. Only users who can edit the post can set it.

snippets.title: Require Login for Selected Pages
snippets.description: Sends visitors who are not logged in to the login screen when they open the pages you list, and brings them back to the page after they log in.
snippets.notes: List page or post IDs. Child pages are not included automatically.

snippets.title: Redirect an Old Domain to This Site
snippets.description: Permanently redirects every request that arrives on your previous domain to the same address on your current domain, after a rebrand or domain move.
snippets.notes: The old domain must still point to this hosting account. List each old host name, including www versions.

snippets.title: Redirect Old Date-Based Post URLs
snippets.description: After switching from /2019/05/post-name/ style permalinks to plain post names, sends visitors and search engines from the old dated addresses to the right posts.
snippets.notes: Only runs when the old address would otherwise be a 404.

snippets.title: Skip the Cart and Go Straight to Checkout
snippets.description: Sends shoppers who open the cart page directly to checkout whenever their cart has products, shortening the path to purchase.
snippets.notes: An empty cart still shows the cart page with its "return to shop" message.

snippets.title: Send Customers to the Shop After Login
snippets.description: Takes customers to the shop page after they log in or register through WooCommerce, instead of the My Account dashboard.
snippets.notes: Shop managers and administrators keep the default destination.

snippets.title: Send Visitors to Login for Private Posts
snippets.description: When a logged-out visitor opens a private post or page, they are sent to the login screen and back again, instead of seeing a "not found" error.
snippets.notes: After logging in, users who are not allowed to read private content still see the 404 page.

snippets.title: Send Each Role to Its Own Page After Login
snippets.description: Chooses where people land after logging in based on their role, for example editors to the posts list, customers to their account and subscribers to a members page.
snippets.notes: Use {admin} at the start of a value for an admin page, or a path on your site. Explicit redirect_to links, such as from a protected page, are respected.

snippets.title: Require Login to Browse the Shop
snippets.description: Sends visitors who are not logged in from the shop, product, cart and checkout pages to the My Account login form, for wholesale and members-only stores.
snippets.notes: The My Account page stays open so customers can log in or register. After logging in, customers go back to the shop.

snippets.title: Redirect Old .html Page Addresses
snippets.description: Sends visitors from addresses of a previous static site, such as /about.html or /services/web.php, to the WordPress page with the same name.
snippets.notes: Only runs when the old address would otherwise be a 404. /index.html goes to the homepage.

snippets.title: Redirect a Category Archive to a Page
snippets.description: Sends visitors from a category archive to a hand-built landing page, for example /category/news/ to your Newsroom page, while posts keep their category.
snippets.notes: The list is empty by default. Map category slugs to paths of pages that exist on your site.

snippets.title: Temporary Homepage Redirect Between Two Dates
snippets.description: Sends homepage visitors to a promotion or event page during a date range you set, such as a Black Friday sale, then switches back automatically.
snippets.notes: Fill in both dates and the target first; nothing happens while they are empty. Dates use the site time zone, editors are not redirected, and page caching may delay the switch.

snippets.title: Cookie Consent Banner With Google Consent Mode
snippets.description: Shows a simple Accept / Reject cookie banner, sets Google Consent Mode v2 defaults to "denied" until the visitor accepts, and remembers the choice for six months.
snippets.notes: A basic banner, not a full consent platform; WPIDE pixel snippets wait for it when their $require_consent is set to true.

snippets.title: Google Consent Mode v2 Default Settings
snippets.description: Sets Google Consent Mode defaults before any Google tag loads, denying ad and analytics storage for visitors in the EEA, UK and Switzerland until your consent tool grants it.
snippets.notes: Your cookie banner must send the matching gtag('consent', 'update', ...) call. Edit $regions to apply the denied default elsewhere.

snippets.title: Honor Global Privacy Control Signals
snippets.description: Detects visitors whose browser sends a Global Privacy Control (GPC) or Do Not Track signal and updates Google Consent Mode to deny ad storage and personalization for them.
snippets.notes: Analytics storage is left to your consent banner. Set $deny_analytics to true to deny it too for these visitors.

snippets.title: GA4 Purchase Event for WooCommerce Orders
snippets.description: Sends a Google Analytics 4 "purchase" event with the order ID, value, tax, shipping and items when a customer reaches the order received page, once per order.
snippets.notes: Needs the GA4 tag (gtag.js) on the page, for example from the Google Analytics 4 snippet. Reloading the thank-you page does not send the event again.

snippets.title: GA4 view_item and add_to_cart Events for WooCommerce
snippets.description: Sends GA4 ecommerce events when a shopper views a product page and when they add a product to the cart, from the product page or with AJAX buttons on shop pages.
snippets.notes: Needs the GA4 tag (gtag.js) on the page. Prices are sent as displayed (including or excluding tax per your store settings).

snippets.title: GA4 begin_checkout Event for WooCommerce
snippets.description: Sends a GA4 "begin_checkout" event with the cart value and items when the customer opens the checkout page.
snippets.notes: Needs the GA4 tag (gtag.js) on the page.

snippets.title: WooCommerce Purchase Data in the GTM dataLayer
snippets.description: Pushes a GA4-style "purchase" ecommerce object to the Google Tag Manager dataLayer on the order received page, ready for GA4, Google Ads or Meta tags in GTM.
snippets.notes: Needs your GTM container on the page; create a Custom Event trigger for "purchase" in GTM. Sent once per order.

snippets.title: Meta Pixel Purchase Event for WooCommerce
snippets.description: Fires the Meta (Facebook) Pixel "Purchase" event with the order value, currency and product IDs on the order received page, once per order.
snippets.notes: Needs the Meta Pixel base code on the page. The order key is sent as event ID so you can deduplicate with the Conversions API.

snippets.title: Meta Pixel ViewContent and AddToCart for WooCommerce
snippets.description: Sends Meta (Facebook) Pixel "ViewContent" on product pages and "AddToCart" when products are added, so you can build retargeting audiences and optimize ads.
snippets.notes: Needs the Meta Pixel base code on the page.

snippets.title: Google Ads Conversion Tracking for WooCommerce
snippets.description: Loads the Google Ads tag and reports a purchase conversion with the order value and transaction ID on the WooCommerce order received page.
snippets.notes: Set $conversion_id (AW-...) and $conversion_label from Google Ads > Goals > Conversions. Nothing is output while the placeholders are in place.

snippets.title: Pinterest Tag
snippets.description: Adds the Pinterest tag to every public page and records page visits, with an option to wait for cookie consent.
snippets.notes: Replace YOUR_TAG_ID with the tag ID from Pinterest Ads Manager > Conversions; nothing is output while the placeholder is in place.

snippets.title: X (Twitter) Pixel
snippets.description: Adds the X (formerly Twitter) website tag to every public page for conversion tracking and audiences, with an option to wait for cookie consent.
snippets.notes: Replace YOUR_PIXEL_ID with the pixel ID from X Ads > Tools > Events Manager. Nothing is output while the placeholder is in place.

snippets.title: Reddit Pixel
snippets.description: Adds the Reddit Ads pixel to every public page and tracks page visits, with an option to wait for cookie consent.
snippets.notes: Replace YOUR_PIXEL_ID with your Reddit pixel ID (it starts with a2_ or t2_). Nothing is output while the placeholder is in place.

snippets.title: TikTok Pixel
snippets.description: Adds the TikTok pixel to every public page and records page views, with an option to wait for cookie consent.
snippets.notes: Replace YOUR_PIXEL_ID with the pixel ID from TikTok Ads Manager > Assets > Events. Nothing is output while the placeholder is in place.

snippets.title: Hotjar Tracking Code
snippets.description: Adds Hotjar heatmaps and session recordings to your public pages, without recording logged-in staff.
snippets.notes: Replace YOUR_SITE_ID with your Hotjar Site ID; nothing is output while the placeholder is in place. Mention Hotjar in your privacy policy.

snippets.title: Matomo Analytics (Self-Hosted or Cloud)
snippets.description: Adds the Matomo tracking code to every public page, with optional cookieless tracking and without counting logged-in staff.
snippets.notes: Set $matomo_url to your Matomo address (with a trailing slash) and $site_id. Nothing is output while $matomo_url is empty.

snippets.title: Umami Analytics
snippets.description: Adds the privacy-friendly Umami analytics script (cloud or self-hosted) to every public page, skipping logged-in staff.
snippets.notes: Replace YOUR-WEBSITE-ID with your Umami website ID (and $script_url if self-hosted); nothing is output while the placeholder is in place.

snippets.title: Simple Analytics
snippets.description: Adds the cookie-free Simple Analytics script to your public pages. No tracking ID is needed: data is matched to the domain you added in Simple Analytics.
snippets.notes: Add your domain in the Simple Analytics dashboard first. Set $enabled to true to start loading the script.

snippets.title: Cloudflare Web Analytics Beacon
snippets.description: Adds Cloudflare's free, cookieless Web Analytics beacon to your public pages, for sites not proxied through Cloudflare or that want manual setup.
snippets.notes: Replace YOUR_TOKEN with the token from Cloudflare dashboard > Analytics & Logs > Web Analytics. Nothing is output while the placeholder is in place.

snippets.title: Microsoft Advertising UET Tag
snippets.description: Adds the Microsoft Advertising (Bing Ads) Universal Event Tracking tag to every public page for conversion tracking and remarketing.
snippets.notes: Replace 00000000 with your UET tag ID from Microsoft Advertising > Tools > UET tag. Nothing is output while the placeholder is in place.

snippets.title: Track Phone, Email and WhatsApp Link Clicks
snippets.description: Sends an event to Google Analytics 4 (or the GTM dataLayer) whenever a visitor clicks a phone number, email address or WhatsApp link, so you can count leads from these contacts.
snippets.notes: Events are named contact_click with a method parameter (phone, email, whatsapp). Mark contact_click as a key event in GA4 to count it as a conversion.

snippets.title: Scroll Depth Events in the dataLayer
snippets.description: Pushes scroll_depth events to the Google Tag Manager dataLayer when visitors scroll 25, 50, 75 and 90 percent of a page, to measure how far content is read.
snippets.notes: In GTM, create a Custom Event trigger for "scroll_depth" and read the percent value from the dataLayer variable "scroll_percent".

snippets.title: Send Login Status and User Role to GA4
snippets.description: Sets GA4 user properties for whether the visitor is logged in and their role (for example customer or subscriber), so you can compare members and guests in reports.
snippets.notes: Register logged_in and user_role as user-scoped custom dimensions in GA4 > Admin > Custom definitions. No personal data such as names or emails is sent.

snippets.title: Send Post Category and Author to GA4
snippets.description: Tells Google Analytics 4 which category, author and post type each page belongs to, so you can see which topics and writers bring the most engagement.
snippets.notes: content_group appears in GA4 reports automatically. Register post_author and post_type as event-scoped custom dimensions to report on them.

snippets.title: Track 404 Errors in GA4
snippets.description: Sends a page_not_found event to Google Analytics 4 with the broken URL and the page the visitor came from, so you can find and fix dead links.
snippets.notes: Needs the GA4 tag on the page. Find the events under Reports > Engagement > Events.

snippets.title: Track Searches With No Results in GA4
snippets.description: Sends a search_no_results event with the search term to Google Analytics 4 when a site search finds nothing, showing you what visitors want but cannot find.
snippets.notes: Needs the GA4 tag on the page. Register search_term as an event-scoped custom dimension to report on terms.

snippets.title: Page Details in the GTM dataLayer
snippets.description: Pushes page information (page type, post type, categories, author, publish date and login status) to the dataLayer before Google Tag Manager loads, for use in tags and triggers.
snippets.notes: Create Data Layer Variables in GTM for the keys you need, for example pageType or postCategories.

snippets.title: Remember UTM Parameters and Fill Hidden Form Fields
snippets.description: Saves utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content and gclid from the landing page in a first-party cookie, then fills matching hidden fields in your forms so leads keep their campaign source.
snippets.notes: Add hidden fields named utm_source, utm_medium and so on to your forms (most form plugins support this). The cookie lasts 30 days and holds only campaign data.

snippets.title: Post Views Counter With Admin Column
snippets.description: Counts views of posts and pages, shows the totals in a sortable "Views" column in the admin, and adds a [wpide_views] shortcode to display the count.
snippets.notes: Counting happens with a small request after the page loads, so it works with page caching; editors and repeat views in the same session are not counted.

snippets.title: Tag Microsoft Clarity Sessions With Page and User Type
snippets.description: Adds custom tags to Microsoft Clarity recordings for the page type, post type and whether the visitor is logged in, so you can filter recordings by them.
snippets.notes: Needs the Microsoft Clarity tracking code on the page. Filter recordings by these tags under Filters > Custom tags.

snippets.title: GA4 Purchase Event for Easy Digital Downloads
snippets.description: Sends a Google Analytics 4 "purchase" event with the order total and downloads when a customer lands on the Easy Digital Downloads purchase confirmation page.
snippets.notes: Needs the GA4 tag (gtag.js) on the page. Uses EDD 3 order functions and sends the event once per order.

snippets.title: View the Debug Log in the Admin
snippets.description: Adds a Tools > Debug Log screen that shows the last lines of wp-content/debug.log, so administrators can check errors without FTP access.
snippets.notes: Turn on WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_LOG in wp-config.php to write the log. Change $lines to show more or fewer lines.

snippets.title: Delete Expired Transients From the Admin Bar
snippets.description: Adds a toolbar button for administrators that removes expired transients from the database in one click, keeping the options table lean.
snippets.notes: Only expired transients are deleted, so cached data that is still valid is kept.

snippets.title: Flush the Object Cache From the Admin Bar
snippets.description: Adds a toolbar button for administrators that empties the object cache (Redis, Memcached or the built-in cache) after deployments or data fixes.
snippets.notes: Flushing a shared persistent cache affects every site using it; on multisite it clears the whole network's cache.

snippets.title: Example Custom REST API Endpoint
snippets.description: Registers a read-only endpoint at /wp-json/wpide/v1/latest that returns your latest posts in a compact format, as a starting point for your own API routes.
snippets.notes: Change the namespace, route and callback to build your own endpoint. Make permission_callback stricter for anything that is not public.

snippets.title: Expose a Custom Field in the REST API and Block Editor
snippets.description: Registers a post meta field (a subtitle by default) so it is saved safely, available in the REST API and usable by the block editor and block bindings.
snippets.notes: Change $meta_key and $post_type. Only users who can edit the post can update the field.

snippets.title: Add a Custom Block Style
snippets.description: Registers extra style variations for core blocks, such as an "Outline" button and a "Card" group, that editors can pick in the block sidebar.
snippets.notes: Edit the CSS in $styles. Each entry adds one option under Styles in the block settings.

snippets.title: Load a Script or Stylesheet Only on Selected Pages
snippets.description: Enqueues a JavaScript or CSS file only on the pages you list, instead of on every page, to keep the rest of the site fast.
snippets.notes: Set $pages to page slugs or IDs and $script_url / $style_url to your files. Leave a URL empty to skip it.

snippets.title: Remove Specific Scripts and Styles by Handle
snippets.description: Stops chosen plugin or theme scripts and stylesheets from loading on the front end, optionally everywhere except the pages where they are needed.
snippets.notes: Find handles with your browser's view source (the id attribute minus -js or -css) or the "List Enqueued Assets" snippet. Removing a needed file can break features, so test after each change.

snippets.title: Add a Custom WP-CLI Command
snippets.description: Registers a "wp site-stats" WP-CLI command that prints counts of posts, pages, comments and users, as a template for your own command-line tools.
snippets.notes: Run "wp site-stats" or "wp site-stats --format=json". The snippet only loads when WP-CLI is running.

snippets.title: Show PHP Version, Memory and Queries in the Admin Footer
snippets.description: Replaces the WordPress version in the bottom right of admin screens with the PHP version, peak memory use and database query count of the current page.
snippets.notes: Visible to administrators only.

snippets.title: Log Slow Page Loads
snippets.description: Writes a line to the PHP error log for every request that takes longer than a set number of seconds, with the URL, time, memory and query count.
snippets.notes: Change $threshold. Enable WP_DEBUG_LOG or check your server's PHP error log to read the entries.

snippets.title: Scheduled Cron Events Viewer
snippets.description: Adds a Tools > Cron Events screen listing every scheduled WP-Cron event with its next run time, recurrence and hook name, to debug missed or duplicate tasks.
snippets.notes: Read-only: nothing can be deleted or run from this screen.

snippets.title: Allow JSON, CSV and Other Data File Uploads
snippets.description: Lets administrators upload data files such as JSON, CSV, XML and Markdown to the Media Library, which WordPress blocks by default.
snippets.notes: Only users with the manage_options capability get the extra file types. Edit $types to add or remove extensions.

snippets.title: Simple Site Details Settings Page
snippets.description: Adds Settings > Site Details where you can store your phone number, address and opening hours once, then show them anywhere with [wpide_site_detail key="phone"].
snippets.notes: Edit $fields to add more details. Values are stored in the wpide_site_details option.

snippets.title: Subtitle Field for Posts
snippets.description: Adds a "Subtitle" box to the post editor, saves it securely and provides a [wpide_subtitle] shortcode and a helper to display it in your theme.
snippets.notes: In a classic theme you can print it with echo esc_html( get_post_meta( get_the_ID(), '_wpide_subtitle', true ) );

snippets.title: Register an "Archived" Post Status
snippets.description: Adds an "Archived" status for posts that should leave the site without being deleted, with its own filter link in the Posts list and a status choice in the editor.
snippets.notes: Archived posts are not public. Set them via Quick Edit or the status dropdown in the block editor's summary panel.

snippets.title: Limit REST API CORS to Your Own Apps
snippets.description: Replaces WordPress's permissive cross-origin (CORS) headers with an allow-list, so only the browser apps you name, such as a headless front end, can call the REST API with credentials.
snippets.notes: List exact origins including the protocol and no trailing slash. Requests from other origins still work server to server, but browsers will block them.

snippets.title: Raise the REST API per_page Limit
snippets.description: Lets REST API requests for posts and pages ask for more than 100 items at once, useful for exports and static site generators.
snippets.notes: Large values make heavy queries; keep $max reasonable.

snippets.title: Run a Daily Task With WP-Cron
snippets.description: Schedules a custom task once a day and gives you a function to fill in, for example to clean up data or send a report. Includes the scheduling and the hook.
snippets.notes: Put your code inside the wpide_daily_task callback. To stop the task after removing the snippet, run "wp cron event delete wpide_daily_task".

snippets.title: List Enqueued Scripts and Styles in the Page Source
