snippets.description: Stamps each Contact Form 7 form with a signed time when it is shown and treats submissions sent within a few seconds as spam. People take longer than bots to fill in a form.
snippets.notes: Works with page caching because older stamps always pass; raise the seconds for long forms if you see false positives in the spam log.

snippets.title: Block Contact Form 7 Messages Containing Spam Words
snippets.description: Marks Contact Form 7 submissions as spam when any field contains a word or phrase from your block list, such as SEO offers or crypto pitches.
snippets.notes: Matching is case-insensitive on whole words; add phrases you keep receiving to the list.

snippets.title: Block Email Domains in Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Rejects Contact Form 7 submissions whose email address belongs to a domain on your block list, with a clear message under the email field.
snippets.notes: List bare domains; subdomains of a listed domain are blocked too.

snippets.title: Require a Business Email in Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Asks visitors to use their work email instead of a free webmail address such as Gmail or Yahoo, which helps B2B sites get qualified leads.
snippets.notes: Limit it to certain fields by adding their names to the list at the top; leave the list empty to check every email field.

snippets.title: Block Links in Contact Form 7 Messages
snippets.description: Shows an error when a message field contains more web links than you allow. Most contact form spam exists to place links.
snippets.notes: Set the allowed number of links to 1 or 2 if customers often send you a link to their site.

snippets.title: Treat Contact Form 7 Messages in Foreign Scripts as Spam
snippets.description: Marks a Contact Form 7 submission as spam when most of its message is written in Cyrillic, Chinese or another script your business does not use.
snippets.notes: Remove a script from the list if you do get genuine enquiries in that language.

snippets.title: Validate Phone Numbers in Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Checks Contact Form 7 phone fields for a realistic number of digits and only the characters phone numbers use, instead of accepting any text.
snippets.notes: Adjust the minimum and maximum digit counts for your country; spaces, dashes, dots, brackets and a leading + are always allowed.

snippets.title: "Confirm Email" Field for Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Makes visitors type their email twice and shows an error when the two addresses do not match, so you do not lose replies to typos.
snippets.notes: Add a second email field named your-email-confirm to the form, for example [email* your-email-confirm], or change the names at the top.

snippets.title: Minimum Message Length in Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Requires message fields to contain a few real words, which stops one-word and empty-looking submissions and gives you enough detail to reply.
snippets.notes: CF7 also has a minlength: option per tag; this snippet sets a site-wide minimum in words instead of characters.

snippets.title: Custom Pattern Rules for Contact Form 7 Fields
snippets.description: Validates chosen Contact Form 7 fields against your own patterns, such as postcodes, order numbers or membership IDs, each with its own error message.
snippets.notes: Keys are field names from your form; patterns are PHP regular expressions matched against the whole value.

snippets.title: Limit Contact Form 7 Submissions per Visitor
snippets.description: Allows only a few Contact Form 7 submissions per IP address each hour and treats the rest as spam, which stops bots and angry repeat senders flooding your inbox.
snippets.notes: IP addresses are stored only as hashes in short-lived transients; raise the limit for forms used from shared offices.

snippets.title: Prefill Contact Form 7 With the Logged-In User's Details
snippets.description: Fills the name and email fields of Contact Form 7 forms with the details of the logged-in visitor, so members do not have to type them again.
snippets.notes: Uses the default field names your-name and your-email; change the map at the top for your own field names.

snippets.title: Fill a Contact Form 7 Drop-Down With Your Posts
snippets.description: Fills a Contact Form 7 select field with the titles of published posts, pages or a custom post type, so a services or products list stays in sync with your content.
snippets.notes: Add an empty select tag such as [select* menu-service] to your form and set the field name and post type at the top; the list is cached for an hour and refreshed when a post of that type is saved.

snippets.title: Redirect to a Thank-You Page After Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Sends visitors to a thank-you page after a Contact Form 7 form is sent successfully, with a different page per form if you like. Handy for conversion tracking.
snippets.notes: Map form IDs (from the form shortcode) to page URLs; the "default" entry covers every other form, so leave it empty to redirect only the forms you list.

snippets.title: Redirect Contact Form 7 Based on an Answer
snippets.description: Sends visitors to a different page after submitting depending on what they chose in a drop-down or radio field, such as a sales or support thank-you page.
snippets.notes: Set the field name and map each option value to a URL; options you do not list keep the normal on-page message.

snippets.title: Save Contact Form 7 Submissions in the Admin
snippets.description: Keeps a copy of every Contact Form 7 message in a private "Form Messages" list in the admin, so nothing is lost when an email goes missing.
snippets.notes: Messages are stored as private posts that only administrators can see (file uploads are not kept), so delete old ones from the list from time to time.

snippets.title: Send Contact Form 7 Submissions to a Webhook
snippets.description: Posts each Contact Form 7 submission as JSON to a webhook URL, such as Zapier, Make, n8n or your CRM, so leads flow into your other tools automatically.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_CF7_WEBHOOK_URL (and optionally WPIDE_CF7_WEBHOOK_SECRET for an X-Signature HMAC header) in wp-config.php; limit it to certain forms with the list at the top.

snippets.title: Post Contact Form 7 Messages to Slack
snippets.description: Sends a short summary of every Contact Form 7 submission to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook, so your team sees new leads right away.
snippets.notes: Create an incoming webhook in Slack and define WPIDE_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL in wp-config.php; the fields shown are listed at the top.

snippets.title: Route Contact Form 7 Emails by Department
snippets.description: Sends each Contact Form 7 message to the right inbox based on the department or topic the visitor picked, instead of one shared address.
snippets.notes: Add your choices and addresses to the map at the top (unknown choices keep the form's own recipient); CF7 pipes (Label|email) are an alternative that keeps addresses inside the form.

snippets.title: Send Contact Form 7 Messages to the Post Author
snippets.description: When a Contact Form 7 form is placed on a post, listing or profile page, the message goes to that post's author instead of the site admin.
snippets.notes: Limit it to certain post types with the list at the top; on other pages the form's own recipient is used.

snippets.title: Prefix Contact Form 7 Email Subjects
snippets.description: Adds the form name and a short reference number to the subject of every Contact Form 7 email, so messages are easy to filter and refer to in your inbox.
snippets.notes: Change the format string at the top; %1$s is the form title and %2$s the reference.

snippets.title: Add Visitor Details to Contact Form 7 Emails
snippets.description: Appends the page the form was sent from, the date, the visitor's browser and IP address to every Contact Form 7 email, without editing each form's mail template.
snippets.notes: Applies to the main mail only, not the autoresponder; remove the IP line if your privacy policy does not cover it.

snippets.title: Friendlier Contact Form 7 Response Messages
snippets.description: Replaces the standard Contact Form 7 success, error and spam messages on every form with your own wording in one place.
snippets.notes: Keys are CF7 message names (mail_sent_ok, mail_sent_ng, validation_error, spam, accept_terms, invalid_required); remove a line to keep the form's own text.

snippets.title: Stop Contact Form 7 Adding Paragraph Tags
snippets.description: Turns off Contact Form 7's automatic paragraph and line-break tags, so forms built with your own HTML or grid markup render exactly as written.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'wpcf7_autop_or_not', '__return_false' );
snippets.notes: After enabling, add your own wrappers (div or p) around fields in the form editor where you want spacing.

snippets.title: Default Upload Limits for Contact Form 7 File Fields
snippets.description: Gives every Contact Form 7 file field a safe default list of allowed file types and a maximum size, unless the field already sets its own.
snippets.notes: Fields with their own filetypes: or limit: options keep them; the server's upload_max_filesize must also allow the size.

snippets.title: Don't Email Submissions of Certain Contact Form 7 Forms
snippets.description: Stops Contact Form 7 sending emails for the forms you list while still showing the success message, useful when submissions are saved or sent to a CRM instead.
snippets.notes: Add the form IDs at the top and pair it with a snippet that saves submissions or sends them to a webhook, otherwise the messages are lost.

snippets.title: Close a Contact Form 7 Form After a Number of Entries
snippets.description: Accepts only a set number of successful submissions for a Contact Form 7 form, such as event places or giveaway entries, then shows a "closed" message instead of the form.
snippets.notes: Add form IDs and limits to the list at the top; the count is stored per form in the option wpide_cf7_count_<ID>, which you can delete to reopen the form.

snippets.title: Open a Contact Form 7 Form Only Between Two Dates
snippets.description: Shows a Contact Form 7 form only during the dates you set, for example an application period, and blocks late submissions from pages left open.
snippets.notes: Add form IDs with start and end dates (site timezone, Y-m-d H:i) to the list at the top; leave the start empty to open the form straight away.

snippets.title: Block IP Addresses From Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Silently rejects Contact Form 7 submissions from IP addresses or ranges you list, such as a persistent spammer, while the rest of the site stays open to them.
snippets.notes: Supports exact addresses and prefix ranges ending in a dot or colon, such as 203.0.113.; behind a proxy CF7 reads the visitor IP it is given.

snippets.title: Tidy Up Contact Form 7 Submissions
snippets.description: Trims stray spaces, lowercases email addresses and collapses repeated blank lines in Contact Form 7 submissions before they are emailed or stored.
snippets.notes: Field names containing "email" are lowercased; everything else keeps its case.

snippets.title: Load Contact Form 7 reCAPTCHA Only on Form Pages
snippets.description: Stops the Google reCAPTCHA script that Contact Form 7 adds to every page from loading where no form is shown, which speeds up the rest of the site and hides the badge there.
snippets.notes: Add page IDs to the list if a form appears outside the post content, for example in a footer widget.

snippets.title: Autofill Hints for Contact Form 7 Fields
snippets.description: Adds the right autocomplete attributes to Contact Form 7 name, email, phone and company fields, so browsers and password managers can fill them in one tap.
snippets.notes: Map your own field names to autocomplete tokens at the top; fields that already have an autocomplete attribute are left alone.

snippets.title: Scroll to the Contact Form 7 Response Message
snippets.description: Scrolls the page to the Contact Form 7 success or error message after submitting, so visitors on long pages and phones see the result.
snippets.notes: Jumps instantly instead of animating for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

snippets.title: Hide the Contact Form 7 Form After It Is Sent
snippets.description: Hides the fields of a Contact Form 7 form once it has been sent successfully and leaves only the thank-you message, so people do not submit twice.
snippets.notes: Contact Form 7 adds the "sent" class to the form after a successful submission; reloading the page shows the form again.

snippets.title: Modern Styling for Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Gives Contact Form 7 forms clean full-width fields, clear focus outlines, readable error messages and a solid submit button that work in light and dark themes.
snippets.notes: Change the custom properties at the top to match your brand colors.

snippets.title: Contact Form 7 Theme With SCSS Variables
snippets.description: A complete Contact Form 7 look written in SCSS: set a few variables for colors, radius and spacing and every field, checkbox, message and button follows.
snippets.notes: Edit the variables at the top; the dark-mode block follows the visitor's system setting.

snippets.title: Track Contact Form 7 Sends in Google Analytics 4
snippets.description: Sends a generate_lead event to Google Analytics 4 or Google Tag Manager each time a Contact Form 7 form is sent successfully, with the form ID attached.
snippets.notes: Works with gtag.js or a GTM dataLayer already on the site; rename the event at the top to match your conversion setup.

snippets.title: Block Email Domains in Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Shows an error when someone enters an email address from a domain on your block list, such as throwaway inbox services, in any Gravity Forms email field.
snippets.notes: Subdomains of listed domains are blocked as well; add more domains to the list as spam arrives.

snippets.title: Require a Work Email in Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Asks for a company email address instead of Gmail, Yahoo or other free webmail in Gravity Forms email fields, for B2B lead and demo request forms.
snippets.notes: Add the CSS class work-email to an email field in the form editor (Appearance tab) to check only that field; without the class every email field is checked.

snippets.title: Block Links in Gravity Forms Text Fields
snippets.description: Rejects Gravity Forms submissions that put web links in name, text or paragraph fields, which removes most link-spam without a captcha.
snippets.notes: Website fields are never checked; add the CSS class allow-links to a field that should accept links.

snippets.title: Mark Gravity Forms Entries With Spam Words as Spam
snippets.description: Sends Gravity Forms entries to the Spam list when any field contains a word or phrase from your block list, so they skip notifications and stay out of your entries.
snippets.notes: Spam entries can still be reviewed and restored from the form's Spam list; matching is case-insensitive on whole words.

snippets.title: Reject Gravity Forms Submitted Too Quickly
snippets.description: Adds a signed time stamp to each Gravity Forms form and marks entries sent within a few seconds of the page loading as spam, which catches bots that fill forms instantly.
snippets.notes: Safe with page caching because older stamps always pass; multi-page forms keep the first stamp.

snippets.title: Turn On the Gravity Forms Honeypot for Every Form
snippets.description: Switches on Gravity Forms' built-in anti-spam honeypot for all forms, including ones created later, so nobody has to remember the setting.
snippets.notes: Exclude a form by adding its ID to the list at the top.

snippets.title: Treat Gravity Forms Entries in Foreign Scripts as Spam
snippets.description: Marks a Gravity Forms entry as spam when most of its text is written in Cyrillic, Chinese or another script you never receive genuine enquiries in.
snippets.notes: Remove scripts from the list that your customers actually write in.

snippets.title: Limit Gravity Forms Entries per IP Address
snippets.description: Stops a visitor from sending more than a few Gravity Forms entries per hour from the same IP address, with a polite message, to block flooding and repeat spam.
snippets.notes: Counts entries already stored for that IP across all forms; set a form ID in the list to limit only specific forms.

snippets.title: One Gravity Forms Entry per Email Address per Day
snippets.description: Prevents the same email address from submitting a Gravity Forms form more than once in 24 hours, useful for giveaways, sign-ups and quote forms.
snippets.notes: Only checks the forms listed at the top, using each form's first email field; Gravity Forms' own "No Duplicates" setting blocks repeats forever instead.

snippets.title: Stricter Phone Validation in Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Checks Gravity Forms phone fields set to the international format for a realistic number of digits and only valid characters, instead of accepting any text.
snippets.notes: Fields using the US (###) ###-#### format keep Gravity Forms' own check; adjust the digit range for your country.

snippets.title: Minimum Age Check on a Gravity Forms Date of Birth
snippets.description: Rejects a Gravity Forms date of birth that makes the person younger than the age you set, for age-restricted sign-ups and applications.
snippets.notes: Add the CSS class date-of-birth to the date field; works with every Gravity Forms date format.

snippets.title: Fill Gravity Forms Fields With the Logged-In User's Details
snippets.description: Lets Gravity Forms fields fill themselves with the visitor's name, email, username or role when they are logged in, using simple parameter names.
snippets.notes: In a field's Advanced tab tick "Allow field to be populated dynamically" and enter one of the parameter names: user_email, user_first_name, user_last_name, user_display_name, user_login or user_role.

snippets.title: Record the Page and Referrer in Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Fills hidden Gravity Forms fields with the title and address of the page the form is on and the site the visitor came from, so you know the context of each entry.
snippets.notes: Allow dynamic population on hidden fields with the parameter names page_title, page_url or referrer_url.

snippets.title: Fill Gravity Forms Choices From Your Posts
snippets.description: Fills Gravity Forms drop-down, radio and checkbox fields with the titles of your posts, pages or a custom post type, so the choices update when you publish content.
snippets.notes: Give the field the CSS class populate-posts (or populate-<post type>, such as populate-product); the list is cached for an hour and refreshed when posts change.

snippets.title: Fill Gravity Forms Choices With Team Members
snippets.description: Fills a Gravity Forms drop-down or radio field with the names of users in a role, such as staff or agents, so visitors can choose who they want to contact.
snippets.notes: Give the field the CSS class populate-role-<role> (for example populate-role-editor); values are user IDs, so pair it with a routing snippet if you email the chosen person.

snippets.title: Redirect Gravity Forms Based on an Answer
snippets.description: Sends people to a different page after submitting a Gravity Forms form depending on what they chose in one field, such as a sales or support thank-you page.
snippets.notes: Set the form ID, field ID and the value-to-URL map at the top; other answers keep the form's normal confirmation.

snippets.title: Send Gravity Forms Entries to a Webhook
snippets.description: Posts every new Gravity Forms entry as JSON, with field labels as keys, to a webhook URL such as Zapier, Make, n8n or your CRM, without the paid webhooks add-on.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_GF_WEBHOOK_URL (and optionally WPIDE_GF_WEBHOOK_SECRET for an X-Signature HMAC header) in wp-config.php; spam entries are never sent.

snippets.title: Post Gravity Forms Entries to Slack
snippets.description: Sends a short summary of each new Gravity Forms entry to a Slack channel with a link to the entry, so your team can respond to leads quickly.
snippets.notes: Create a Slack incoming webhook and define WPIDE_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL in wp-config.php; only the first five filled fields are included.

snippets.title: Send Gravity Forms Notifications to the Page Author
snippets.description: Sends the admin notification of a Gravity Forms form to the author of the post or page the form was submitted from, ideal for agent, listing or staff profile pages.
snippets.notes: Only notifications named in the list at the top are changed; the original recipient is used when the author has no email.

snippets.title: Copy All Gravity Forms Notifications to an Archive Address
snippets.description: Adds a blind copy of every Gravity Forms notification to an archive or CRM inbox, so you keep a record of all submissions even if entries are deleted.
snippets.notes: Existing BCC addresses on a notification are kept; set the archive address at the top.

snippets.title: Stop Gravity Forms Notifications on Staging Sites
snippets.description: Turns off all Gravity Forms email notifications when the site is not the production environment, so tests on staging never email clients or your team.
snippets.notes: Uses the WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE setting; set it to staging, development or local in wp-config.php on copies of the site.

snippets.title: Add the Entry Number to Gravity Forms Email Subjects
snippets.description: Prefixes every Gravity Forms notification subject with the form name and entry ID, so you can find, filter and refer to submissions easily.
snippets.notes: Change the format at the top; %1$s is the form title and %2$d the entry ID.

snippets.title: Reply Directly to People Who Fill In Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Sets the Reply-To of Gravity Forms admin notifications to the email address the visitor entered, so hitting Reply answers them instead of your own site.
snippets.notes: Notifications that already have a Reply-To keep it; the first email field in the form is used.

snippets.title: Scroll to the Gravity Forms Confirmation Message
snippets.description: Makes every Gravity Forms form jump to its confirmation or error message after submitting, so visitors on long pages and phones see the result.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'gform_confirmation_anchor', '__return_true' );
snippets.notes: Applies to all forms; return false in the filter for a form where you want to stay at the top.

snippets.title: Use a Real Button for the Gravity Forms Submit
snippets.description: Replaces the Gravity Forms submit input with a button element that carries your theme's button classes, so it matches the rest of the site and can hold icons.
snippets.notes: Set the classes at the top to your theme's button classes, such as wp-element-button or btn btn-primary.

snippets.title: Remove Tabindex From Gravity Forms Fields
snippets.description: Stops Gravity Forms adding tabindex numbers to fields, which can make keyboard users jump around the page in the wrong order, especially with several forms on one page.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'gform_tabindex', '__return_false' );
snippets.notes: Fields then follow the natural document order, which is what screen reader and keyboard users expect.

snippets.title: Clearer Gravity Forms Error Summary
snippets.description: Replaces the error message at the top of a Gravity Forms form with your own wording and lists how many fields need attention, announced to screen readers.
snippets.notes: Edit the sentence at the top; %d is replaced with the number of fields that need fixing.

snippets.title: Delete Old Gravity Forms Entries Automatically
snippets.description: Deletes Gravity Forms entries older than the number of days you choose once a day, so you do not keep personal data longer than you need.
snippets.notes: Does nothing until you set the number of days at the top; it then deletes old entries permanently (including uploaded files) in batches of 100 per daily run, so export anything you need first.

snippets.title: Tidy Names and Emails in Gravity Forms Entries
snippets.description: Trims spaces, lowercases email addresses and capitalizes names in Gravity Forms entries before they are saved, so your lists and CRM exports look consistent.
snippets.notes: Names already in mixed case (such as McDonald) are left as typed; only all-lowercase or all-uppercase names are changed.

snippets.title: Default Upload Limits for Gravity Forms File Fields
snippets.description: Gives every Gravity Forms file upload field a safe list of allowed file types and a maximum file size when the field does not set its own.
snippets.notes: Values set in the field's own settings always win; the server's upload limit must also allow the size.

snippets.title: Extra Merge Tags for Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Adds {site_name}, {site_url}, {form_entry_count} and {current_year} merge tags you can use in Gravity Forms notifications and confirmations.
snippets.notes: The tags appear in the merge tag menu of notification and confirmation editors.

snippets.title: Clean Modern Styling for Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Gives Gravity Forms fields rounded borders, comfortable spacing, a visible focus ring, clear error colors and a bold submit button, while following your theme's fonts.
snippets.notes: Built for the Gravity Forms 2.5+ markup; change the custom properties at the top for your colors.

snippets.title: Gravity Forms Theme With SCSS Variables
snippets.description: Styles Gravity Forms from a handful of SCSS variables (accent, radius, spacing, error color), including choices, multi-page progress bars, buttons and dark mode.
snippets.notes: Edit the variables at the top; written for the Gravity Forms 2.5+ markup.

snippets.title: Sensible Year Range for Gravity Forms Date Drop-Downs
snippets.description: Sets the years offered in Gravity Forms date drop-downs to a range that fits your form, such as the last 100 years for birth dates or the next two years for bookings.
snippets.notes: Applies to date fields using the drop-down input type; adjust how many years back and forward to offer.

snippets.title: Put Your Main Countries First in Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Moves the countries you sell to most to the top of Gravity Forms address and country drop-downs, so most visitors find theirs without scrolling.
snippets.notes: Use the English country names exactly as Gravity Forms lists them; set $wpide_gf_only_listed to true to offer only those countries.

snippets.title: Track Gravity Forms Submissions in Google Analytics 4
snippets.description: Sends a generate_lead event to Google Analytics 4 or Google Tag Manager when a Gravity Forms form shows its confirmation, including AJAX forms.
snippets.notes: Needs gtag.js or a GTM container already on the site; non-AJAX forms are tracked when the confirmation page loads.

snippets.title: Block IP Addresses From Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Stops Gravity Forms submissions from IP addresses or ranges you list and marks them as spam, without blocking those visitors from reading the site.
snippets.notes: Use exact addresses or prefixes ending in a dot or colon (198.51.100.) for ranges.

snippets.title: Word Limits for Gravity Forms Paragraph Fields
snippets.description: Lets you require a minimum and maximum number of words in Gravity Forms paragraph fields, for essays, applications and testimonials.
snippets.notes: Add a CSS class such as words-50-300 to a paragraph field to require 50 to 300 words; use words-50-0 for a minimum only.

snippets.title: Allow Only Future Dates in Gravity Forms Date Fields
snippets.description: Rejects dates in the past in Gravity Forms date fields used for bookings, deliveries or appointments, with an optional number of days' notice.
snippets.notes: Add the CSS class future-date to a date field; set the minimum notice in days at the top (0 allows today).

snippets.title: Stop Gravity Forms Storing Visitors' IP Addresses
snippets.description: Saves Gravity Forms entries without the visitor's IP address, which helps with privacy rules when you have no need to keep it.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'gform_ip_address', '__return_empty_string' );
snippets.notes: IP-based features such as rate limiting by stored IP will no longer work after enabling this.

snippets.title: Don't Keep Entries for Certain Gravity Forms Forms
snippets.description: Deletes the entry of the forms you list right after its notifications are sent, so sensitive submissions live only in your inbox and never in the database.
snippets.notes: Runs after notifications and add-on feeds that process on submission; delayed feeds such as payment add-ons would lose their entry, so only list simple contact forms.

snippets.title: Block Email Domains in WPForms
snippets.description: Shows an error when an email address from a domain on your block list, such as throwaway inbox services, is entered in any WPForms email field.
snippets.notes: Subdomains of listed domains are blocked too; add domains as spam arrives.

snippets.title: Require a Work Email in WPForms
snippets.description: Asks for a company email address instead of Gmail, Yahoo or other free webmail in WPForms email fields, so B2B forms collect qualified leads.
snippets.notes: Limit it to specific forms with the list of form IDs at the top; empty checks every form.

snippets.title: Block WPForms Submissions Containing Spam Words
snippets.description: Quietly discards WPForms submissions when any field contains a word or phrase from your block list, the same way WPForms treats a filled honeypot.
snippets.notes: Matching is case-insensitive on whole words; WPForms discards matching submissions silently, like its own honeypot, so bots get no hint.

snippets.title: Block Links in WPForms Paragraph Fields
snippets.description: Shows an error when a WPForms paragraph text field contains web links, which stops most link spam without adding a captcha.
snippets.notes: Set the number of links you allow at the top if customers often share a link.

snippets.title: Reject WPForms Messages in Foreign Scripts
snippets.description: Blocks WPForms submissions written mostly in Cyrillic, Chinese or another script your business never receives genuine messages in.
snippets.notes: Remove scripts from the list that your customers actually write in.

snippets.title: Limit WPForms Submissions per Visitor
snippets.description: Allows only a few WPForms submissions per IP address each hour and blocks the rest with a polite message, to stop flooding and repeat spam.
snippets.notes: IPs are kept only as hashes in short-lived transients; raise the limit for forms used from shared offices or schools.

snippets.title: Minimum Message Length in WPForms
snippets.description: Requires WPForms paragraph fields to contain at least a few words, so you get enough detail to reply and fewer one-word junk messages.
snippets.notes: Empty optional fields are skipped; required fields must reach the minimum.

snippets.title: Prefill WPForms With the Logged-In User's Details
snippets.description: Fills WPForms name and email fields with the logged-in visitor's details, so members and customers do not have to type them again.
snippets.notes: Works with the Simple name format and email fields; fields with their own default value are left alone.

snippets.title: Fill a WPForms Drop-Down With Your Posts
snippets.description: Fills a WPForms drop-down with the titles of published posts, pages or a custom post type, both when the form is shown and when it is processed, so entries keep the chosen title.
snippets.notes: Give the drop-down the CSS class wpide-posts-<post type> (for example wpide-posts-page) in the field's Advanced settings.

snippets.title: Redirect WPForms Based on an Answer
snippets.description: Sends visitors to a different thank-you page after a WPForms form depending on the option they picked, such as separate pages for sales and support.
snippets.notes: Set the form ID, field ID and map at the top, and set the form's confirmation type to "Go to URL (Redirect)" with a fallback URL that this snippet swaps by answer.

snippets.title: Send WPForms Entries to a Webhook
snippets.description: Posts every WPForms submission as JSON with field labels as keys to a webhook URL, such as Zapier, Make, n8n or a CRM, without a paid add-on.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_WPFORMS_WEBHOOK_URL (and optionally WPIDE_WPFORMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET for an X-Signature HMAC header) in wp-config.php.

snippets.title: Post WPForms Submissions to Slack
snippets.description: Sends a summary of each WPForms submission to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook, so the team sees new enquiries straight away.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL in wp-config.php; only the first six filled fields are included.

snippets.title: Save WPForms Lite Entries in the Admin
snippets.description: Keeps a copy of every WPForms Lite submission in a private "Form Entries" list in the admin, since the free version does not store entries.
snippets.notes: Entries are private posts visible to administrators only; WPForms Pro already stores entries, so skip this snippet there.

snippets.title: Route WPForms Notifications by Department
snippets.description: Sends WPForms email notifications to a different address depending on the department or topic the visitor picked, instead of one shared inbox.
snippets.notes: Set the field ID of the drop-down and add each choice label with its address to the map at the top; other choices keep the notification's own recipients.

snippets.title: Send WPForms Notifications to the Page Author
snippets.description: Sends WPForms notifications to the author of the post or page where the form was filled in, for agent, listing or team profile pages.
snippets.notes: Limit it to forms in the list at the top; the original recipients are used when the page cannot be found.

snippets.title: Prefix WPForms Notification Subjects
snippets.description: Adds the form name and the submitter's name to the subject of WPForms notifications, so messages are easy to tell apart and filter in your inbox.
snippets.notes: Uses the first Name field of the form; change the format at the top.

snippets.title: Reply Directly to People Who Fill In WPForms
snippets.description: Sets the Reply-To of WPForms notifications to the email address the visitor entered when no Reply-To is configured, so pressing Reply answers them.
snippets.notes: Uses the first email field of the form; notifications with their own Reply-To setting are not changed.

snippets.title: Extra Smart Tags for WPForms
snippets.description: Adds {current_year}, {user_role} and {site_name_plain} smart tags you can use in WPForms notifications, confirmations and default values.
snippets.notes: The tags appear in the Smart Tags list of the form builder.

snippets.title: Personal WPForms Confirmation Message
snippets.description: Greets visitors by their first name in the WPForms confirmation message after submitting, which feels friendlier than a generic thank-you.
snippets.notes: Uses the first Name field; the greeting is added before your existing confirmation text.

snippets.title: Stop WPForms Emails on Staging Sites
snippets.description: Turns off all WPForms notification emails when the site is not running as production, so test submissions on staging never reach clients.
snippets.notes: Relies on WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE being set to staging, development or local on non-live copies.

snippets.title: Modern Styling for WPForms
snippets.description: Gives WPForms fields consistent borders, rounded corners, a visible focus ring, clear errors and a bold submit button that follow your theme's fonts.
snippets.notes: Change the custom properties at the top; for full control set WPForms > Settings > Include Form Styling to "Base styling only".

snippets.title: WPForms Theme With SCSS Variables
snippets.description: Styles WPForms from a few SCSS variables (accent, radius, spacing, error color), including choices, buttons, errors and a dark-mode variant.
snippets.notes: Edit the variables at the top; works best with WPForms set to "Base styling only".

snippets.title: Theme Button Classes on WPForms Submit Buttons
snippets.description: Adds your theme's button classes to every WPForms submit button, so forms match the other buttons on your site without extra CSS.
snippets.notes: Set the classes your theme uses, such as wp-element-button for block themes or btn btn-primary for Bootstrap themes.

snippets.title: Default Upload Limits for WPForms File Fields
snippets.description: Gives every WPForms file upload field a safe list of allowed file types and a maximum size when the field does not set its own.
snippets.notes: Applies to the File Upload field available in WPForms Pro and newer Lite versions; values set on the field always win.

snippets.title: Track WPForms Submissions in Google Analytics 4
snippets.description: Sends a generate_lead event to Google Analytics 4 or Google Tag Manager when an AJAX WPForms form is submitted successfully.
snippets.notes: Turn on "Enable AJAX form submission" in each form's settings; needs gtag.js or a GTM container on the site.

snippets.title: Tidy Up WPForms Submissions
snippets.description: Trims spaces, lowercases email addresses and capitalizes all-lowercase names in WPForms submissions before they are emailed or stored.
snippets.notes: Names typed in mixed case (such as McDonald) are left as they are.

snippets.title: Block IP Addresses From WPForms
snippets.description: Rejects WPForms submissions from IP addresses or ranges you list, such as a persistent spammer, while they can still read the site.
snippets.notes: Use exact addresses, or prefixes ending in a dot or colon for ranges.

snippets.title: One WPForms Submission per Email per Day
snippets.description: Stops the same email address from submitting a WPForms form more than once in 24 hours, useful for giveaways and quote requests, even in WPForms Lite.
snippets.notes: Only the forms listed at the top are checked; addresses are kept only as hashes in transients that expire after the waiting period.

snippets.title: Hide the WPForms Dashboard Widget
snippets.description: Removes the WPForms entries widget from the WordPress dashboard for everyone, keeping the dashboard focused on what you use.
snippets.notes: Entries remain available under WPForms > Entries.

snippets.title: Block Email Domains in Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Shows an error when someone uses an email address from a domain on your block list, such as throwaway inbox services, in a Fluent Forms form.
snippets.notes: Needs Fluent Forms 5.0 or later and checks the field named "email" unless you list other email field names at the top.

snippets.title: Require a Work Email in Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Asks for a company email address instead of Gmail, Yahoo or other free webmail in Fluent Forms, so B2B forms bring in qualified leads.
snippets.notes: Limit it to forms in the list at the top; the field named "email" is checked unless you change it.

snippets.title: Block Fluent Forms Messages Containing Spam Words
snippets.description: Stops Fluent Forms submissions when any text field contains a word or phrase from your block list, such as SEO offers or crypto pitches.
snippets.notes: The error is shown on the first text field that contains a blocked word; matching is case-insensitive on whole words.

snippets.title: Block Links in Fluent Forms Messages
snippets.description: Shows an error when a Fluent Forms message field contains web links, which removes most link spam without a captcha.
snippets.notes: List the names of the fields to check at the top; the default is the "message" field.

snippets.title: Reject Fluent Forms Messages in Foreign Scripts
snippets.description: Stops Fluent Forms submissions that are written mostly in Cyrillic, Chinese or another script your business does not receive genuine messages in.
snippets.notes: Remove scripts from the list that your customers actually write in.

snippets.title: Limit Fluent Forms Submissions per Visitor
snippets.description: Allows only a few Fluent Forms submissions per IP address each hour and shows a polite message after that, which stops flooding and repeated spam.
snippets.notes: IPs are stored only as hashes in short-lived transients; raise the limit for forms used from shared offices.

snippets.title: Minimum Message Length in Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Requires the message field of Fluent Forms to contain at least a few words, so you get enough detail to answer and fewer junk submissions.
snippets.notes: Change the field name and number of words at the top.

snippets.title: "Confirm Email" Check for Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Makes visitors type their email address twice in a Fluent Forms form and shows an error when the two do not match, so you do not lose replies to typos.
snippets.notes: Add a second email field named email_confirm to the form, or change both names at the top.

snippets.title: Validate Phone Numbers in Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Checks Fluent Forms phone fields for a realistic number of digits and only the characters phone numbers use, instead of accepting any text.
snippets.notes: Set the phone field names at the top; empty optional fields are skipped.

snippets.title: Redirect Fluent Forms Based on an Answer
snippets.description: Sends visitors to a different page after submitting a Fluent Forms form depending on an answer, such as separate thank-you pages for each service.
snippets.notes: Set the form ID, the field name and the answer-to-URL map at the top; other answers keep the form's normal confirmation.

snippets.title: Send Fluent Forms Entries to a Webhook
snippets.description: Posts each new Fluent Forms entry as JSON to a webhook URL such as Zapier, Make, n8n or your CRM, without the Pro webhook module.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_FLUENT_WEBHOOK_URL (and optionally WPIDE_FLUENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET for an X-Signature HMAC header) in wp-config.php.

snippets.title: Route Fluent Forms Notifications by Department
snippets.description: Sends Fluent Forms email notifications to a different inbox depending on the department or topic chosen in the form.
snippets.notes: Set the field name and add each option value with its address to the map at the top; Fluent Forms Pro also has conditional routing in the notification settings.

snippets.title: Turn Off Fluent Forms Default Styles
snippets.description: Stops Fluent Forms loading its default stylesheet, so forms inherit your theme's form styling or your own CSS without overrides.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'fluentform/load_default_public', '__return_false' );
snippets.notes: Fields may look unstyled until your theme or custom CSS covers them; pair it with the Fluent Forms styling snippet if needed.

snippets.title: Modern Styling for Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Gives Fluent Forms fields consistent borders, rounded corners, a visible focus ring, clear errors and a bold submit button that follow your theme's fonts.
snippets.notes: Change the custom properties at the top for your colors.

snippets.title: Fluent Forms Theme With SCSS Variables
snippets.description: Styles Fluent Forms from a few SCSS variables for accent color, radius, spacing and errors, including checkboxes, buttons and a dark-mode variant.
snippets.notes: Edit the variables at the top; works well together with turning off the default Fluent Forms styles.

snippets.title: Tidy Up Fluent Forms Submissions
snippets.description: Trims spaces and lowercases email addresses in Fluent Forms submissions before they are saved, so entries and exports stay consistent.
snippets.notes: Field names containing "email" are lowercased; other text fields are trimmed only.

snippets.title: Block IP Addresses From Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Stops Fluent Forms submissions from IP addresses or ranges you list, such as a persistent spammer, while they can still read the site.
snippets.notes: Use exact addresses, or prefixes ending in a dot or colon for ranges.

snippets.title: One Fluent Forms Submission per Email per Day
snippets.description: Stops the same email address from submitting a Fluent Forms form more than once in 24 hours, useful for giveaways, trials and quote requests.
snippets.notes: Checks the forms and email field listed at the top; addresses are stored only as hashes in transients that expire.

snippets.title: Fill a Fluent Forms Drop-Down With Your Posts
snippets.description: Fills a Fluent Forms drop-down with the titles of your published posts, pages or a custom post type, so the options stay in sync with your content.
snippets.notes: Add the container class wpide-posts-<post type> (for example wpide-posts-page) to the drop-down in its Advanced Options.

snippets.title: GA4 Lead Event for Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Sends a generate_lead event to Google Analytics 4 or Google Tag Manager whenever a Fluent Forms form is submitted successfully.
snippets.notes: Needs gtag.js or a GTM container already on the site.

snippets.title: Contact Form Shortcode Without a Plugin
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_contact_form] shortcode with name, email and message fields that emails you each message, protected by a nonce, a hidden honeypot, a time trap and a per-visitor hourly limit.
snippets.notes: Add [wpide_contact_form] to any page (messages go to the admin email unless you set a recipient), and exclude that page from full-page caching so its security token stays fresh.

snippets.title: Newsletter Sign-Up With Double Opt-In
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_newsletter] sign-up shortcode that stores subscribers in the admin, emails a confirmation link (double opt-in), and lets you export confirmed addresses as CSV.
snippets.notes: Confirmed subscribers are listed under Tools > Subscribers with a CSV export for your mailing tool, and unconfirmed sign-ups older than 7 days are removed daily.

snippets.title: Quote Request Form Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_quote_form] shortcode where visitors pick a service, budget and timeline and describe their project; requests are emailed to you with spam protection and rate limiting built in.
snippets.notes: Edit the services, budgets and recipient at the top; replies go straight to the visitor thanks to the Reply-To header.

snippets.title: "Request a Call Back" Form Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a short [wpide_callback_form] form where visitors leave their name, phone number and the best time to call, and emails the request to you.
snippets.notes: Change the time slots and recipient at the top; works well in a sidebar or at the end of service pages.

snippets.title: Event RSVP Form With a Guest Limit
snippets.description: Adds an [wpide_rsvp] shortcode for events: guests reply with their name, email and party size, replies are saved on the event post with a running total, and the form closes when it is full.
snippets.notes: Use [wpide_rsvp limit="50"] on the event post or page; each email address can reply once and the guest list appears in a box on that post's edit screen.

snippets.title: Testimonial Submission Form for Customers
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_testimonial_form] shortcode where customers submit a testimonial with their name and rating; each one is saved as a pending post for you to review and publish.
snippets.notes: Submissions become pending posts of the testimonial post type if one exists (otherwise regular posts in a "Testimonials" category), and the admin is emailed about each one.

snippets.title: Job Application Form With CV Upload
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_job_application] shortcode where candidates send their details and a CV (PDF or Word, size-limited); the CV is attached to the email you receive and then deleted from the server.
snippets.notes: Use [wpide_job_application position="Senior Designer"] to name the role and change the size limit and recipient at the top; CVs are never kept on the server.

snippets.title: Simple Poll Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_poll] shortcode that shows a question with answer buttons and, after voting, the results as accessible bars. One vote per visitor, stored without personal data.
snippets.notes: Use [wpide_poll id="coffee" question="Tea or coffee?" options="Tea|Coffee|Neither"] with a unique id per poll; votes are counted in an option per poll.

snippets.title: "Report a Problem on This Page" Form
snippets.description: Adds a small expandable form at the end of posts where readers can report a typo, broken link or outdated information; reports are emailed to the post author with the page link.
snippets.notes: Shows on single posts by default (change the post types at the top) and accepts at most five reports per visitor per day.

snippets.title: "Was This Page Helpful?" Buttons
snippets.description: Adds Yes and No buttons at the end of posts and pages so readers can rate them, and shows the helpful score in a column in the admin post list.
snippets.notes: Votes are saved as post meta through a nonce-checked request, limited to one per visitor per page; change the post types at the top.

snippets.title: Email-Gated Download Form
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_gated_download] shortcode that asks for an email address before a guide or PDF can be downloaded, then emails a private download link valid for 48 hours.
snippets.notes: Use [wpide_gated_download file="123" title="Free pricing guide"] with the media attachment ID; the file URL is never shown on the page and collected emails are sent to the admin.

snippets.title: Required Privacy Consent Checkbox on Comments
snippets.description: Adds a required "I agree to the privacy policy" checkbox to the comment form and rejects comments that are submitted without it, with a link to your privacy page.
snippets.notes: Links to the privacy policy page set under Settings > Privacy; logged-in users are not asked.

snippets.title: Placeholders in Comment Form Fields
snippets.description: Adds helpful placeholder text to the comment, name, email and website fields of the comment form while keeping the visible labels for accessibility.
snippets.notes: Edit the texts at the top; placeholders never replace labels, so screen readers still announce each field.

snippets.title: Theme-Styled Button for the Comment Form
snippets.description: Replaces the comment form's submit input with a real button element that carries your theme's button classes, so it matches the other buttons on your site.
snippets.notes: Set the classes your theme uses, such as wp-element-button for block themes or btn btn-primary for Bootstrap-based themes.

snippets.title: Star Rating Field in Comments
snippets.description: Adds an optional 1 to 5 star rating to the comment form, saves it with the comment and shows the stars above the comment text, for review-style posts.
snippets.notes: Limit it to certain post types with the list at the top; ratings are stored as comment meta named wpide_rating.

snippets.title: Hide the "Logged in as" Line Above Comments
snippets.description: Removes the "Logged in as … Edit your profile. Log out?" line from the top of the comment form for a cleaner look on member sites.
snippets.notes: Members can still log out from the admin bar or your account menu.

snippets.title: Pre-Tick "Save My Name" on the Comment Form
snippets.description: Ticks the "Save my name, email, and website in this browser" box on the comment form by default, so returning commenters do not retype their details.
snippets.notes: Check your privacy rules first; some jurisdictions require consent boxes to start unticked.

snippets.title: Post Comments Without Reloading the Page
snippets.description: Submits the comment form in the background and shows the new comment (or the "awaiting moderation" note) right away, instead of reloading the page.
snippets.notes: Uses WordPress's own comment handling, so spam checks and moderation rules still apply; falls back to the normal form if JavaScript fails.

snippets.title: "Confirm Email" Field on the Registration Form
snippets.description: Adds a second email field to the WordPress registration form and refuses the sign-up when the two addresses differ, so new users do not lock themselves out with a typo.
snippets.notes: Applies to the standard wp-login.php?action=register form.

snippets.title: Phone Number Field on Registration and Profiles
snippets.description: Adds a phone number field to the WordPress registration form, saves it with the new account and lets users and admins edit it on the profile screen.
snippets.notes: Set $wpide_phone_required to false to make it optional; the number is stored in user meta named phone.

snippets.title: Log New Users In Right After Registering
snippets.description: Signs people in straight after they register through the WordPress registration form and sends them to a welcome page, instead of making them wait for an email.
snippets.notes: Change the welcome URL at the top, and only use this when users choose their own password at registration, because the emailed set-password link still arrives.

snippets.title: Helpful Message on the Lost Password Form
snippets.description: Shows a short explanation above the lost password form telling people what will happen next and where to get help if the email does not arrive.
snippets.notes: Edit the text and support address at the top.

snippets.title: Save Long Form Answers in the Browser
snippets.description: Keeps what visitors type into a long form saved in their browser, so a reload, a crash or an accidental back click does not wipe out their answers. Cleared after submitting.
snippets.notes: Add the class wpide-save-progress to a form (most form builders have a CSS class setting); password, file and hidden fields are never stored.

snippets.title: Character Counter for Any Text Box With a Limit
snippets.description: Shows a live "120 / 500 characters" counter under every text box that has a maximum length, announced politely to screen readers as the limit gets close.
snippets.notes: Works with any form that sets a maxlength of up to 10,000 characters on its textareas, including form plugins; very high technical limits (like the comment box's default) are ignored.

snippets.title: Stop Phones Zooming Into Form Fields
snippets.description: Sets form fields to at least 16px text so iPhones stop zooming in when a field is tapped, and makes inputs full width on small screens.
snippets.notes: Applies to all forms on the front of the site; the full-width rule only kicks in below 600px.

snippets.title: Clear Valid and Invalid States for Form Fields
snippets.description: Colors form fields red with a short hint once a visitor has interacted with them and entered something invalid, without flagging untouched empty fields.
snippets.notes: Uses the :user-invalid selector supported by current browsers; older browsers simply show no color change.

snippets.title: Mark Required Form Fields With an Asterisk
snippets.description: Adds a red asterisk after the label of every required field in standard HTML forms, so visitors can see at a glance what they must fill in.
snippets.notes: Applies when the label sits directly before a field with the required attribute; labels that already contain a .required marker (like the comment form) are skipped.

snippets.title: Sequential Reference Number Mail Tag for Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Adds a [_wpide_ref] mail tag that gives every Contact Form 7 submission a running reference number like WEB-1042, which you can quote in the subject or autoresponder.
snippets.notes: Change the prefix and starting number at the top; the counter is shared by all forms and stored in an option.

snippets.title: Use the Comment Blocklist for Contact Form 7
snippets.description: Marks Contact Form 7 submissions as spam when they contain any word, IP address or email from WordPress's own Disallowed Comment Keys list, so one blocklist protects comments and forms.
snippets.notes: Manage the list under Settings > Discussion > Disallowed Comment Keys, one entry per line.

snippets.title: Use the Comment Blocklist for Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Sends Gravity Forms entries to spam when they contain any word, IP address or email from WordPress's Disallowed Comment Keys list, so one blocklist covers comments and forms.
snippets.notes: Manage the list under Settings > Discussion > Disallowed Comment Keys, one entry per line.

snippets.title: Show How Many People Filled In a Gravity Form
snippets.description: Adds a [wpide_gf_count form="1"] shortcode that prints the number of entries a Gravity Forms form has received, for petitions, sign-ups and social proof.
snippets.notes: Counts active entries only, cached for ten minutes; add offset="100" to start from a higher number.

snippets.title: Start the Gravity Forms Progress Bar at 0%
snippets.description: Makes multi-page Gravity Forms progress bars start at 0% on the first page and reach 100% only on submit, which better matches how far people really are.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'gform_progressbar_start_at_zero', '__return_true' );
snippets.notes: Affects every multi-page form that uses the progress bar indicator.

snippets.title: Lighter Loading Spinner for Gravity Forms
snippets.description: Replaces the Gravity Forms AJAX loading spinner with a small inline SVG spinner in your brand color, with no extra file to download.
snippets.notes: Change the color at the top; the spinner is embedded as a data URI.

snippets.title: One Gravity Forms Entry per Logged-In User
snippets.description: Lets each logged-in member submit a Gravity Forms form only once, for surveys, applications or votes, and shows a friendly message instead of the form afterwards.
snippets.notes: List the form IDs at the top and turn on "Require user to be logged in" in those forms' settings.

snippets.title: Use the Comment Blocklist for WPForms
snippets.description: Blocks WPForms submissions that contain any word, IP address or email from WordPress's Disallowed Comment Keys list, so one blocklist protects comments and forms.
snippets.notes: Manage the list under Settings > Discussion > Disallowed Comment Keys, one entry per line.

snippets.title: Custom Pattern Rules for WPForms Text Fields
snippets.description: Validates WPForms single-line text fields against your own patterns, such as postcodes, order numbers or VAT IDs, chosen per field with a CSS class.
snippets.notes: Give a text field one of the CSS classes from the list at the top (Advanced tab); patterns are PHP regular expressions matched against the whole value.

snippets.title: One WPForms Submission per Logged-In User
snippets.description: Lets each logged-in member submit the WPForms forms you choose only once, for surveys, votes or applications, and replaces the form with a message afterwards.
snippets.notes: List the form IDs at the top; submissions are remembered in user meta, so it works in WPForms Lite too, and logged-out visitors are not limited.

snippets.title: Use the Comment Blocklist for Fluent Forms
snippets.description: Blocks Fluent Forms submissions that contain any word, IP address or email from WordPress's Disallowed Comment Keys list, so one blocklist protects comments and forms.
snippets.notes: Manage the list under Settings > Discussion > Disallowed Comment Keys, one entry per line.

snippets.title: Custom Pattern Rules for Fluent Forms Fields
snippets.description: Validates chosen Fluent Forms fields against your own patterns, such as postcodes, order numbers or membership IDs, each with its own error message.
snippets.notes: Keys are field names (the Name Attribute in the field's Advanced Options); patterns are PHP regular expressions matched against the whole value.

snippets.title: JavaScript Check Against Comment Spam Bots
snippets.description: Adds a hidden field to the comment form that only a real browser running JavaScript fills in; comments without it go to the spam queue instead of moderation.
snippets.notes: Comments are sent to spam, never deleted, so you can rescue a real one; works with page caching because the token changes only once a day.

snippets.title: Send Comments From Blocked Email Domains to Spam
snippets.description: Sends comments to the spam queue when the commenter's email address belongs to a throwaway inbox service or any other domain on your list.
snippets.notes: Subdomains of listed domains match too; extend the list as spam arrives.

snippets.title: Send Comments in Foreign Scripts to Spam
snippets.description: Sends comments written mostly in Cyrillic, Chinese, Arabic or another script your readers do not use to the spam queue, where most of them belong.
snippets.notes: Remove scripts from the list if your community writes in them.

snippets.title: Daily Comment Limit per Visitor
snippets.description: Holds comments for moderation once a single IP address has posted more than a set number of comments in 24 hours, which stops comment floods and spam runs.
snippets.notes: Logged-in users are not limited; extra comments are held, not rejected, so you can still approve genuine ones.

snippets.title: Reject Registrations Submitted Too Fast
snippets.description: Stamps the WordPress registration form with a signed time and refuses sign-ups sent within a few seconds of loading it, which stops most registration bots.
snippets.notes: Real people need a few seconds to type a username and email; raise the minimum if bots adapt.

snippets.title: Block Comments Posted Without Visiting Your Site
snippets.description: Rejects comment submissions that do not come from a page on your own site, which stops bots that post directly to wp-comments-post.php.
snippets.notes: Browsers send the page address when a form is submitted; very strict privacy setups that strip it entirely would be blocked, so watch for complaints.

snippets.title: Spam Comments Linking to Suspicious Domains
snippets.description: Sends comments to spam when the commenter's website field points to a domain ending you have chosen to distrust, such as .xyz, .top or .click.
snippets.notes: Edit the endings at the top to match the spam you actually receive.

snippets.title: Spam Comments Copied Across Several Posts
snippets.description: Sends a comment to spam when exactly the same text was already posted on another post in the last day, a typical sign of a spam bot working through your site.
snippets.notes: Short comments under 30 characters (like "Thanks!") are ignored so genuine readers are not caught.

snippets.title: Log Every Email to Daily Files With Rotation
snippets.description: Writes one line per outgoing email (time, recipient, subject, result) to a daily log file in a protected uploads folder, and deletes files older than the number of days you choose.
snippets.notes: Files live in uploads/wpide-mail-logs with an unguessable name, an index.php and an Apache deny rule (on Nginx keep that folder private), and message bodies are not logged.

snippets.title: Full Email Log With Search, Viewer and Resend
snippets.description: Records every outgoing email in its own database table and adds Tools > Mail Log, where you can search, read the full message, resend it, and clear old entries automatically.
snippets.notes: Creates the {prefix}wpide_mail_log table the first time an administrator opens the admin and purges old entries daily; message bodies can hold personal data, so keep the retention short.

snippets.title: Catch All Email Locally With Mailpit or MailHog
snippets.description: On local and development sites, sends every WordPress email to a local mail catcher such as Mailpit, MailHog or the one built into Herd, Local or DDEV, so nothing reaches real inboxes.
snippets.notes: Only active when WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE is local or development; change the host and port to match your tool (Mailpit and MailHog use port 1025).

snippets.title: Write SMTP Conversation to the Debug Log
snippets.description: Records the conversation between WordPress and your SMTP server in the PHP error log while you troubleshoot, with passwords and login tokens blanked out.
snippets.notes: Only runs while WPIDE_SMTP_DEBUG is defined as true in wp-config.php; turn it off when you are done because the log grows quickly.

snippets.title: Check the SMTP Connection Without Sending
snippets.description: Adds Tools > SMTP Check, which connects and logs in to your configured SMTP server and reports success or the exact error, without sending an email to anyone.
snippets.notes: Uses whatever SMTP settings your other snippets or mail plugin apply through phpmailer_init; if nothing switches WordPress to SMTP, it tells you so.

snippets.title: WP-CLI Command to Send a Test Email
snippets.description: Adds "wp wpide-mail test you@example.com" to WP-CLI, which sends a test email and prints the exact error if it fails, handy on servers without admin access.
snippets.notes: Add --subject="..." to change the subject; the command only exists when WP-CLI is running.

snippets.title: Reply to Commenters From Moderation Emails
snippets.description: Adds the commenter's email as the Reply-To of comment moderation emails, so you can answer or ask a question just by pressing Reply in your inbox.
snippets.notes: WordPress already does this for post author notifications; this adds it to the "please moderate" emails.

snippets.title: Reply-To Address Rules by Email Subject
snippets.description: Sets a different Reply-To address depending on the email's subject, so replies to order, support or form emails reach the right team automatically.
snippets.notes: Add your subject-to-address rules at the top (the first match wins); emails that already have a Reply-To are left alone.

snippets.title: Wrap Emails in a Template File From Your Theme
snippets.description: Wraps every plain-text WordPress email in an HTML template file stored in your theme, so designers can edit the email layout like any other template.
snippets.notes: Create emails/wrapper.php in your (child) theme using $content (safe HTML) and $subject; without the file emails are unchanged, and do not combine it with another HTML wrapper snippet.

snippets.title: Add a Signature to Every WordPress Email
snippets.description: Appends a short signature, such as your company name, address and support link, to the bottom of every email the site sends, in both plain-text and HTML emails.
snippets.notes: Edit the lines at the top; HTML emails get the signature before the closing body tag.

snippets.title: Never Email Certain Addresses or Domains
snippets.description: Removes addresses and whole domains on your suppression list from every outgoing email, such as bouncing inboxes or people who asked not to be contacted, and skips emails left with no recipient.
snippets.notes: List full addresses or "@domain.com" entries; CC and BCC headers are not filtered.

snippets.title: Hourly Limit on Outgoing Emails
snippets.description: Caps how many emails the site can send per hour and stops the rest, which protects your mail account and domain reputation if a form or plugin is abused to send spam.
snippets.notes: Set the limit above your busiest real hour; blocked emails are reported as failures and noted in the PHP error log once per hour.

snippets.title: Clean Up Email Recipient Lists Before Sending
snippets.description: Removes duplicate, malformed and placeholder addresses (such as example.com or .test domains) from email recipient lists, so one bad address does not make the whole email fail.
snippets.notes: Only the To list is cleaned; edit the reserved domains at the top if you really send to any of them.

snippets.title: Send WordPress Email Through the Postmark API
snippets.description: Delivers all WordPress emails through Postmark's HTTP API instead of PHP mail or SMTP, for fast, reliable delivery on hosts that block outgoing mail ports.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_POSTMARK_TOKEN (your server API token) in wp-config.php and send from a verified Postmark sender; emails with attachments fall back to the normal mailer.

snippets.title: Send WordPress Email Through the Mailgun API
snippets.description: Delivers all WordPress emails through Mailgun's HTTP API, which avoids blocked SMTP ports and gives you Mailgun's delivery logs and tracking.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_MAILGUN_KEY and WPIDE_MAILGUN_DOMAIN (plus WPIDE_MAILGUN_EU as true for EU accounts) in wp-config.php; emails with attachments fall back to the normal mailer.

snippets.title: Send WordPress Email Through the SendGrid API
snippets.description: Delivers all WordPress emails through SendGrid's v3 Mail Send API instead of PHP mail or SMTP, for reliable delivery and SendGrid's activity feed.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_SENDGRID_KEY in wp-config.php and verify your sender domain in SendGrid; emails with attachments fall back to the normal mailer.

snippets.title: Send WordPress Email Through the Brevo API
snippets.description: Delivers all WordPress emails through the Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) transactional email API, so mail goes out even where SMTP ports are blocked.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_BREVO_KEY (a v3 API key) in wp-config.php and use a sender verified in Brevo; emails with attachments fall back to the normal mailer.

snippets.title: Use Resend to Deliver WordPress Email
snippets.description: Delivers all WordPress emails through the Resend email API with a single API key, a simple way to get reliable delivery without SMTP.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_RESEND_KEY in wp-config.php and send from a domain verified in Resend; emails with attachments fall back to the normal mailer.

snippets.title: Send Fatal Error Emails to Your Developers
snippets.description: Sends WordPress's "your site is experiencing a technical issue" recovery emails to your developers instead of (or as well as) the site owner, so the right people can fix it.
snippets.notes: Add your developers' addresses at the top and set $wpide_recovery_keep_admin to false to stop the site owner receiving them; WordPress sends at most one such email per day.

snippets.title: Stop "Data Request Confirmed" Emails to the Admin
snippets.description: Stops WordPress emailing the site admin each time a user confirms a personal data export or erasure request; you can still see requests under Tools.
snippets.notes: Users still receive their own confirmation and data emails; check Tools > Export/Erase Personal Data regularly instead.

snippets.title: Stop Automatic Update Debug Emails
snippets.description: Stops the long technical "background update" debug emails WordPress sends after automatic updates on development, beta and nightly versions.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'automatic_updates_send_debug_email', '__return_false' );
snippets.notes: Success and failure emails for normal releases are not affected.

snippets.title: Send Automatic Update Emails to Your Developer
snippets.description: Sends WordPress core, plugin and theme auto-update emails to your developer or agency instead of the site owner, who usually does not need them.
snippets.notes: Add one or more addresses at the top; once set, the site owner stops receiving these emails.

snippets.title: Daily Digest of Comments Awaiting Moderation
snippets.description: Replaces the one-email-per-comment moderation notices with a single daily email listing every comment waiting for approval, with a link to the moderation screen.
snippets.notes: Sent at the hour set at the top (site time) only when comments are waiting; goes to the admin email address.

snippets.title: Weekly Site Activity Summary by Email
snippets.description: Emails the site admin every Monday with last week's numbers: new posts, comments, pending items and new users, so you keep an eye on the site without logging in.
snippets.notes: Sent on Monday at the hour set at the top (site time); add more recipients to the list.

snippets.title: Daily Digest of New User Registrations
snippets.description: Replaces the "New user registration" email WordPress sends for every sign-up with one daily email listing all new users, their role and email address.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.1 or later, users still get their own welcome email, and nothing is sent on days without new registrations.

snippets.title: Weekly Email of Upcoming Scheduled Posts
snippets.description: Emails editors and the admin every Monday with the posts scheduled to publish in the coming week, so everyone knows what is going live and when.
snippets.notes: Goes to every user with the Editor role plus the admin email; nothing is sent when no posts are scheduled.

snippets.title: Remind Authors About Old Drafts
snippets.description: Once a week, emails each author a list of their drafts that have not been touched for a month, with edit links, so good ideas do not get forgotten.
snippets.notes: Change the number of days at the top; each author gets at most one email per week listing up to 20 drafts.

snippets.title: Email When Plugin or Theme Updates Are Available
snippets.description: Checks once a day for plugin, theme and WordPress updates and emails the admin a list when there is something new to install, so outdated software does not linger.
snippets.notes: Only emails when the list of available updates changes, so you are not reminded daily about the same ones.

snippets.title: Stop Gmail Grouping Your Site's Emails Into Threads
snippets.description: Adds a unique reference header to every email so Gmail shows each notification separately instead of bundling emails with the same subject into one long conversation.
snippets.notes: Invisible to recipients; Gmail uses the X-Entity-Ref-ID header to decide whether to thread messages.

snippets.title: Dark Mode Support for HTML Emails
snippets.description: Adds the color-scheme meta tags to HTML emails, so mail apps like Apple Mail and Outlook render them properly in dark mode instead of inverting your colors badly.
snippets.notes: Only changes emails that already contain an HTML head; your template should also look fine on dark backgrounds.

snippets.title: Remove the [Site Name] Prefix From Email Subjects
snippets.description: Strips the "[Your Site Name]" WordPress puts at the start of its email subjects, which looks dated and wastes space on phones.
snippets.notes: Only removes the prefix when it matches your site title exactly.

snippets.title: Keep the From Address on Your Own Domain
snippets.description: When a plugin sends email "from" a visitor's or a free webmail address, switches the From to your own domain and keeps the original address as Reply-To, so emails pass SPF and DMARC checks.
snippets.notes: Set the address to use at the top, or leave it empty to use wordpress@ your domain.

snippets.title: Remove the X-Mailer Header From Emails
snippets.description: Stops outgoing emails announcing "PHPMailer" and its version in the X-Mailer header, which reveals details about your server and can count against you in spam filters.
snippets.notes: PHPMailer omits the header entirely when it is set to a single space.

snippets.title: Email Delivery Check in Site Health
snippets.description: Adds a test to Tools > Site Health that warns when WordPress sends mail with plain PHP mail() instead of SMTP or an API, and when an email has failed recently.
snippets.notes: Failures are recorded from the moment the snippet is active; the warning clears seven days after the last failure.

snippets.title: Email Alert When Posts or Pages Are Trashed
snippets.description: Emails the site admin whenever a post or page is moved to the trash, with who did it and a link to restore it, so accidental or malicious deletions are spotted quickly.
snippets.notes: Limit the post types with the list at the top; trashing by administrators can be skipped with $wpide_trash_skip_admins.

snippets.title: Follow-Up Email a Few Days After Sign-Up
snippets.description: Sends new users a second, friendly email a few days after they register, with tips or links to get started, scheduled automatically with WP-Cron.
snippets.notes: Edit the delay, subject and message at the top ({name} and {site} are replaced); the email is skipped if the account has been deleted meanwhile.

snippets.title: Daily Email Summary of New PHP Errors
snippets.description: Reads new lines in debug.log once a day and emails a short summary of fatal errors, warnings and notices with how often each occurred, so problems do not go unnoticed.
snippets.notes: Needs WP_DEBUG_LOG enabled, reads at most 1 MB of new log per day and lists the 30 most frequent messages; set the recipient at the top.

snippets.title: Copy Admin Notification Emails to Slack
snippets.description: Posts the subject and the start of every email sent to the site admin address into a Slack channel, so the team sees new users, comments and alerts where they already work.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL in wp-config.php; only emails addressed to the admin email are copied, and they are still sent as usual.

snippets.title: Email the Admin When Someone Else Publishes
snippets.description: Emails the site admin whenever a post or page is published by a user who is not an administrator, so you can review new content as soon as it goes live.
snippets.notes: Covers posts and pages by default; scheduled posts trigger the email when they actually go live.

snippets.title: Email Alert When a User Account Is Deleted
snippets.description: Emails the site admin when any user account is deleted, including who deleted it and whether their content was reassigned, so removals never go unnoticed.
snippets.notes: Works for single sites; on multisite network user deletions use a different hook.

snippets.title: More Details in the New User Admin Email
snippets.description: Adds the new user's role, the page they signed up from, their IP address and a link to their profile to the "New user registration" email the admin receives.
snippets.notes: Remove the IP line if your privacy policy does not cover it.

snippets.title: Retry Emails That Failed to Send
snippets.description: Keeps emails that fail because of a temporary mail server problem and tries to send them again up to three times over the following half hour.
snippets.notes: Emails with attachments are not retried because the attached files may be gone; the queue holds at most 50 emails.

snippets.title: Deliver Site Emails With SparkPost
snippets.description: Delivers all WordPress emails through SparkPost's Transmissions API instead of PHP mail or SMTP, for dependable delivery and SparkPost's event reporting.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_SPARKPOST_KEY (plus WPIDE_SPARKPOST_EU as true for EU accounts) in wp-config.php and verify the sending domain; emails with attachments fall back to the normal mailer.

snippets.title: Mailjet Delivery for All WordPress Email
snippets.description: Delivers all WordPress emails through Mailjet's Send API v3.1, a reliable alternative to SMTP that also gives you Mailjet's delivery statistics.
snippets.notes: Define WPIDE_MAILJET_KEY and WPIDE_MAILJET_SECRET in wp-config.php and send from a sender validated in Mailjet; emails with attachments fall back to the normal mailer.

snippets.title: Alert When an Administrator Password Reset Is Requested
snippets.description: Emails the site admin whenever someone requests a password reset for an administrator account, an early warning sign of an attempt to take over the site.
snippets.notes: Sends at most one alert per account per hour; the requester's IP address is included.

snippets.title: Skip Oversized Email Attachments
