snippets.description: Removes attachments that would make an email larger than your mail server accepts and notes it in the message, so the email still arrives instead of bouncing.
snippets.notes: Set the limit a little below your provider's maximum (often 10 to 25 MB); base64 encoding makes attachments about a third larger, which the snippet accounts for.

snippets.title: Fix Plain Emails Sent as HTML
snippets.description: When a plugin switches all emails to HTML, WordPress's own plain emails arrive as one squashed paragraph with broken links; this adds line breaks and clickable links back.
snippets.notes: Only touches emails sent as HTML whose body contains no HTML tags, such as the password reset and new user emails.

snippets.title: Limit the Number of Recipients per Email
snippets.description: Refuses to send any single email to more than a set number of recipients across To, CC and BCC, which stops a compromised form or plugin from blasting your contacts.
snippets.notes: Raise the cap if you legitimately email larger groups; blocked emails are reported as failures.

snippets.title: Email Alert When the Theme Is Changed
snippets.description: Emails the site admin whenever someone switches the active theme, with who did it and the old and new theme, so unexpected design changes are caught immediately.
snippets.notes: Theme updates do not trigger it, only switching to a different theme.

snippets.title: Email Alert When Key Site Settings Change
snippets.description: Emails the site admin when important settings change, such as the site address, admin email, open registration or the default role for new users, a common sign of a hacked site.
snippets.notes: Edit the watched options at the top; each change is reported with the old and new value and the user who made it.

snippets.title: Email Subscribers When a New Post Is Published
snippets.description: Emails all users with the Subscriber role a short announcement with the title, excerpt and link whenever a new blog post is published, sent in small batches to protect your mail server.
snippets.notes: Sends 50 BCC recipients per batch every two minutes (change the role, batch size or post type at the top); use a proper newsletter service for large lists.

snippets.title: Email All Users of a Role From the Admin
snippets.description: Adds Users > Email Users, where administrators can write a plain-text message and send it to every user with a chosen role, delivered in batches in the background.
snippets.notes: Messages go out as BCC batches of 40 every minute through WP-Cron; recipients' addresses are never shown to each other.

snippets.title: Friendlier Subjects for Account Emails
snippets.description: Gives WordPress's new account, password changed and email address changed emails friendlier subjects of your own, without touching the rest of the message.
snippets.notes: Use %s for the site name; remove a line to keep WordPress's default subject for that email.

snippets.title: Email Alert When Disk Space Runs Low
snippets.description: Checks free disk space on the server twice a day and emails the admin when it drops below your threshold, before uploads, backups and the database start failing.
snippets.notes: Does nothing on hosts that disable disk_free_space(), and repeats the alert at most once a day while space stays low.

snippets.title: Email Alert When WP-Cron Stops Running
snippets.description: Warns the admin by email when scheduled tasks are more than an hour overdue, so you notice before scheduled posts, digests and backups silently stop.
snippets.notes: The check runs when an administrator loads the admin, so it works even when cron itself is broken; at most one alert per day.

snippets.title: Styles for the WPIDE Form Shortcodes
snippets.description: Gives the contact, quote, newsletter and other WPIDE form shortcodes a clean, consistent look with full-width fields, clear notices and a solid button that follows your theme colors.
snippets.notes: Targets the .wpide-form wrapper used by the library's form shortcodes; change the custom properties at the top.

snippets.title: Friendlier Messages on the Registration Screens
snippets.description: Explains what happens next above the WordPress registration form and replaces the terse "Registration complete" notice with clearer instructions about the confirmation email.
snippets.notes: Edit both texts at the top; they appear on wp-login.php?action=register and right after registering.

snippets.title: Optional Title Field for Comments
snippets.description: Adds an optional "Title" field to the comment form and shows it as a heading above the comment, handy for reviews and longer discussions.
snippets.notes: Titles are limited to 100 characters and stored as comment meta named wpide_comment_title.

snippets.title: Send Contact Form 7 Emails From Your Own Domain
snippets.description: When a Contact Form 7 form is set to send "from" the visitor's address, switches the sender to your own domain and moves the visitor's address to Reply-To, so emails stop landing in spam.
snippets.notes: Set the sender address at the top or leave it empty to use wordpress@ your domain; replying still goes to the visitor.

snippets.title: Send Gravity Forms Notifications From Your Own Domain
snippets.description: When a Gravity Forms notification uses the visitor's email or another outside domain as the From address, switches it to your domain and keeps that address as Reply-To.
snippets.notes: Merge tags in the From field are resolved first; set your own sender at the top or leave it empty for wordpress@ your domain.

snippets.title: One Contact Form 7 Submission per Logged-In User
snippets.description: Lets each logged-in member send the Contact Form 7 forms you choose only once, for surveys, applications or votes, and shows a message instead of the form afterwards.
snippets.notes: List the form IDs at the top and combine with CF7's "subscribers_only: true" additional setting so only logged-in users can use the form.

snippets.title: One Fluent Forms Submission per Logged-In User
snippets.description: Lets each logged-in member submit the Fluent Forms forms you choose only once, which suits surveys, votes and applications, with a clear message on a second attempt.
snippets.notes: List the form IDs at the top; submissions are remembered in user meta and logged-out visitors are not limited.

snippets.title: Honeypot Trap on the Lost Password Form
snippets.description: Adds a hidden field to the lost password form that only bots fill in and silently ignores those requests, so bots cannot flood your users with reset emails.
snippets.notes: Real users never see the field; bot requests get the normal "check your email" screen but no email is sent.

snippets.title: Inbox Preview Text for HTML Emails
snippets.description: Adds hidden preview text to HTML emails, the short line mail apps show next to the subject, taken from the first sentence of the message so inboxes no longer show stray template text.
snippets.notes: Only HTML emails with a body tag are changed, and only when they do not already contain preview text.

snippets.title: Newsletter Opt-In Checkbox on the Comment Form
snippets.description: Adds an unticked "Send me the newsletter" checkbox to the comment form and lets you download the email addresses of commenters who opted in as a CSV from Tools.
snippets.notes: Only commenters who tick the box are exported (from Tools > Comment Opt-Ins); import the CSV into your mailing tool, which should handle confirmation.

snippets.title: Skip Links to Navigation, Search and Footer
snippets.description: Adds a small set of keyboard skip links (main content, main menu, search and footer) that appear on the first Tab press. Links whose target is missing on a page are removed automatically.
snippets.code: Skip to main content Skip to main menu Skip to search Skip to footer
snippets.notes: Adjust the CSS selectors in the data-target attributes to match your theme's header, menu, search and footer.

snippets.title: Respect "Reduce Motion" Across the Whole Site
snippets.description: Turns off CSS animations, transitions, parallax backgrounds and smooth scrolling for visitors whose device is set to reduce motion. Visitors without that setting see no change.
snippets.notes: Add selectors for slider or animation libraries your theme uses if they animate with JavaScript instead of CSS.

snippets.title: Stop Autoplaying Videos for Reduced-Motion Users
snippets.description: Pauses autoplaying and looping background videos and adds visible controls when the visitor's device asks for reduced motion, so moving content never starts on its own.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    var query = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') : null;
    if (!query || !query.matches) { return; }
    document.querySelectorAll('video[autoplay], video[loop]').forEach(function (video) {
        video.removeAttribute('autoplay');
        video.pause();
        video.setAttribute('controls', '');
    });
    document.querySelectorAll('img[src$=".gif"]').forEach(function (img) {
        img.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy');
    });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Remove the line that adds controls if your design uses a separate custom play button.

snippets.title: "Pause Animations" Button for Visitors
snippets.description: Adds a floating button that lets any visitor stop animations, transitions and autoplaying videos on the site. The choice is remembered on their device.
snippets.code:
<button type="button" class="wpide-motion-toggle" aria-pressed="false">Pause animations</button>
<style>
.wpide-motion-toggle{position:fixed;left:12px;bottom:12px;z-index:99990;padding:8px 14px;border:2px solid #fff;border-radius:6px;background:#1d2327;color:#fff;font-size:14px;cursor:pointer;}
.wpide-motion-toggle:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #72aee6;outline-offset:2px;}
html.wpide-no-motion *,html.wpide-no-motion *::before,html.wpide-no-motion *::after{animation:none!important;transition:none!important;scroll-behavior:auto!important;}
</style>
<script>
(function () {
    var key = 'wpideNoMotion';
    var btn = document.querySelector('.wpide-motion-toggle');
    if (!btn) { return; }
    function apply(on) {
        document.documentElement.classList.toggle('wpide-no-motion', on);
        btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', on ? 'true' : 'false');
        btn.textContent = on ? 'Play animations' : 'Pause animations';
        document.querySelectorAll('video').forEach(function (v) { if (on) { v.pause(); } });
    }
    var stored = false;
    try { stored = localStorage.getItem(key) === '1'; } catch (e) {}
    apply(stored);
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
        var on = btn.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true';
        apply(on);
        try { localStorage.setItem(key, on ? '1' : '0'); } catch (e) {}
    });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Change the bottom/left values in the CSS to move the button away from other floating elements such as chat widgets.

snippets.title: Accessible Toggle Buttons for Sub-Menus
snippets.description: Adds a real button with aria-expanded next to every menu item that has a sub-menu in classic menus, so keyboard and screen reader users can open and close sub-menus.
snippets.notes: Style .wpide-submenu-toggle to match your theme; the script opens sub-menus by adding the is-open class.

snippets.title: Close Open Menus With the Escape Key
snippets.description: Lets keyboard users press Escape to close an open dropdown or mobile menu and returns focus to the button or link that opened it.
snippets.code:
<script>
document.addEventListener('keydown', function (event) {
    if (event.key !== 'Escape') { return; }
    var open = document.querySelectorAll('[aria-expanded="true"]');
    if (!open.length) { return; }
    var last = open[open.length - 1];
    last.click();
    if (last.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') {
        last.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
        var item = last.closest('.is-open, .focus, .toggled-on');
        if (item) { item.classList.remove('is-open', 'focus', 'toggled-on'); }
    }
    last.focus();
});
</script>
snippets.notes: Works with menus that mark the open state with aria-expanded="true" on the toggle, which most modern themes and the Navigation block do.

snippets.title: Name Each Menu Landmark for Screen Readers
snippets.description: Gives every classic menu location its own accessible name (for example "Primary menu" or "Footer menu"), so screen reader users can tell navigation regions apart.
snippets.notes: Menu locations without a label in the list keep the theme's default; find your location names under Appearance > Menus > Manage Locations.

snippets.title: Announce Links That Open in a New Tab
snippets.description: Adds hidden "(opens in a new tab)" text and a small icon to links in post content that open a new window, so screen reader and keyboard users are not surprised.
snippets.notes: The hidden text uses the screen-reader-text class most themes provide; the icon can be removed by deleting the ::after rule.

snippets.title: Remove Redundant Title Attributes From Menu Links
snippets.description: Strips title attributes from menu links when they only repeat the visible link text, which makes screen readers announce the same words twice.
snippets.notes: Titles that add new information are kept; only exact repeats of the link text are removed.

snippets.title: Descriptive "Read More" Links With the Post Title
snippets.description: Adds the post title as hidden text to "Read more" and "Continue reading" links, so screen reader users hear where each link goes instead of a list of identical links.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_more_text to the visible wording you want; the post title is added for screen readers only.

snippets.title: Pre-Publish Warning for Images Without Alt Text
snippets.description: Shows a panel in the block editor's pre-publish check listing every image block that has no alternative text, with a button to jump to each one.
snippets.notes: Images that are purely decorative can stay without alt text; the panel is a reminder and does not block publishing.

snippets.title: Block Publishing Until Every Image Has Alt Text
snippets.description: Disables the Publish and Update buttons in the block editor while any image block is missing alternative text, and shows a notice explaining why.
snippets.notes: Strict by design; for decorative images type a short description anyway or use the pre-publish warning snippet instead.

snippets.title: Heading Outline Panel With Skipped-Level Warnings
snippets.description: Adds a "Heading outline" panel to the block editor sidebar that lists the post's headings as an indented outline and flags skipped levels (such as an H2 followed by an H4) and empty headings.
snippets.notes: The post title is the page's H1, so the outline expects content headings to start at H2.

snippets.title: Pre-Publish Check for Vague Link Text
snippets.description: Lists links whose text is "click here", "read more", "here" or a bare URL in the block editor's pre-publish panel, so authors can rewrite them to describe where they lead.
snippets.notes: Add phrases in your language to the vague list in the script.

snippets.title: Accessibility Check When a Post Is Saved
snippets.description: After you save a post or page, shows a notice if the content has images without alt text, empty links, empty headings or skipped heading levels. Works with the block editor and the classic editor.
snippets.notes: Checks published content as stored in the database; results are kept for one minute per user, so the notice shows once after each save.

snippets.title: Use the Post Title as Alt Text for Featured Images Without One
snippets.description: When a featured image has no alternative text, outputs the post title as its alt attribute in themes and blocks, instead of leaving it empty.
snippets.notes: Only affects images shown as a post's featured image; images that already have alt text keep it.

snippets.title: "Missing Alt Text" Filter in the Media Library
snippets.description: Adds a dropdown to the Media Library list view that shows only images without alternative text, so you can fix them one by one.
snippets.notes: Works in the list view of the Media Library (upload.php?mode=list).

snippets.title: Images Missing Alt Text Dashboard Widget
snippets.description: Adds a dashboard widget showing how many images in the Media Library have no alternative text, with a link to the most recent ones to fix.
snippets.notes: The count is cached for 12 hours and refreshed whenever an image's alt text changes.

snippets.title: Add Missing Labels to Form Fields From Their Placeholder
snippets.description: Finds form fields on the page that have a placeholder but no label or accessible name and gives them one from the placeholder text, a common problem with theme and plugin forms.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    function fix(root) {
        root.querySelectorAll('input[placeholder], textarea[placeholder], select[data-placeholder]').forEach(function (field) {
            if (field.type === 'hidden' || field.getAttribute('aria-label') || field.getAttribute('aria-labelledby')) { return; }
            if (field.id && document.querySelector('label[for="' + CSS.escape(field.id) + '"]')) { return; }
            if (field.closest('label')) { return; }
            field.setAttribute('aria-label', field.getAttribute('placeholder') || field.getAttribute('data-placeholder'));
        });
    }
    fix(document);
    if ('MutationObserver' in window) {
        new MutationObserver(function (records) {
            records.forEach(function (r) { r.addedNodes.forEach(function (n) { if (n.nodeType === 1) { fix(n); } }); });
        }).observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    }
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: A visible label is always better; use this as a safety net while you fix the forms themselves.

snippets.title: Color Contrast Checker Under Tools
snippets.description: Adds a Tools > Contrast Checker page where you pick a text and background color and instantly see the WCAG contrast ratio and whether it passes AA and AAA for normal and large text.
snippets.notes: Runs entirely in the browser; nothing is saved.

snippets.title: Text Size Buttons Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [text_size_controls] shortcode with "A-", "A" and "A+" buttons that make the whole site's text smaller or larger for that visitor, remembered on their device.
snippets.notes: Works best with themes that size text in rem or em; pixel-based themes only scale partly.

snippets.title: Text Spacing Toggle for Easier Reading
snippets.description: Adds a [text_spacing_toggle] shortcode button that increases line height, letter and word spacing to the levels recommended by WCAG, which helps readers with dyslexia or low vision.
snippets.notes: Place the shortcode in a header or footer widget, or in a Shortcode block on a page.

snippets.title: Always Underline Links in Post Content
snippets.description: Makes links inside posts and pages underlined, so they can be recognised without relying on color alone, as WCAG requires for links in text.
snippets.notes: Buttons styled as links (wp-block-button) are left alone.

snippets.title: Bigger Tap Targets for Small Links and Buttons
snippets.description: Gives menu links, pagination links, icon buttons and form controls a minimum 24 by 24 pixel tap area, the WCAG 2.2 target size minimum, without changing how they look.
snippets.notes: Raise the values to 44px for the stricter AAA level if your layout allows it.

snippets.title: Screen Reader Text Class for Any Theme
snippets.description: Adds the standard .screen-reader-text styles that hide text visually but keep it readable by screen readers, for themes that do not include them.
snippets.notes: Many snippets and plugins rely on this class; add it once if hidden helper text shows up visibly on your site.

snippets.title: Accessible Pagination Labels
snippets.description: Gives numbered pagination links clear labels such as "Page 3" and names the pagination landmark "Posts pages", so screen reader users know what each link does.
snippets.notes: Applies to pagination built with the core paginate_links() and the_posts_pagination() functions.

snippets.title: Descriptive Labels for Previous and Next Post Links
snippets.description: Adds aria-labels like "Previous post: Title" to the previous and next post links in classic themes, so screen readers announce where each link leads.
snippets.notes: Block themes using the Post Navigation Link block already include the title in the link text.

snippets.title: Add Missing Titles to Embedded Iframes
snippets.description: Gives iframes in post content a title attribute when they lack one (for example "YouTube video" or "Embedded map"), so screen reader users know what each frame contains.
snippets.notes: Add more hosts to the $wpide_iframe_titles list for other services you embed.

snippets.title: Remind Editors to Add Captions to Videos
snippets.description: Shows a warning after saving when a post contains a Video block without a captions or subtitles track, so videos are not published without captions by accident.
snippets.notes: Add captions in the Video block settings under "Text tracks"; embedded YouTube and Vimeo videos manage captions on their own platform.

snippets.title: Add Scope to Table Header Cells
snippets.description: Adds scope="col" or scope="row" to table header cells in post content that lack it, so screen readers can tie each data cell to its header.
snippets.notes: Header cells in the first row get scope="col"; header cells elsewhere get scope="row".

snippets.title: Remove Positive Tabindex Values From Content
snippets.description: Removes tabindex values greater than zero from links and fields in post content, which otherwise force a confusing keyboard order, while keeping tabindex 0 and -1.
snippets.notes: Theme and plugin markup outside the post content is not changed.

snippets.title: Announce "Added to Cart" to Screen Readers
snippets.description: Makes screen readers announce when a product is added to the cart with AJAX on shop and category pages, which otherwise happens silently.
snippets.notes: Uses the wp-a11y live region that WordPress provides; change the message text in the script if needed.

snippets.title: Stronger Keyboard Focus Outlines in wp-admin
snippets.description: Makes the keyboard focus indicator in the WordPress dashboard thicker and higher-contrast on links, buttons, menus and form fields, so it is easy to see where you are.
snippets.notes: Uses :focus-visible, so mouse clicks keep the normal look.

snippets.title: Accessibility Statement Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds an [accessibility_statement] shortcode that prints a ready-made accessibility statement with your site name, target standard, contact email and review date.
snippets.notes: Edit the values at the top, then review the text with whoever is responsible for accessibility on your site; this is a starting point, not legal advice.

snippets.title: "Report an Accessibility Problem" Footer Link
snippets.description: Adds a small link at the bottom of every page inviting visitors to report accessibility barriers by email, with the page address filled in for you.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_a11y_contact to a dedicated inbox, or to the URL of a contact page.

snippets.title: Accessibility Toolbar With Text Size, Contrast and Link Highlighting
snippets.description: Adds a small floating accessibility button that opens a panel with larger text, high contrast, highlighted links, a readable font and a reset option. Choices are remembered on the visitor's device.
snippets.notes: A toolbar helps some visitors but does not replace fixing accessibility problems in the theme itself.

snippets.title: Accessibility Quick Check in the Admin Bar
snippets.description: Adds an "A11y check" item to the admin bar on the front of the site. Clicking it outlines images without alt text, empty links and buttons, unlabeled fields and skipped headings on the current page and shows a count.
snippets.notes: Only users who can edit posts see the button; it is a quick check, not a replacement for a full audit tool.

snippets.title: Name Icon-Only Links and Buttons From Their Title
snippets.description: Gives links and buttons that contain only an icon an accessible name taken from their title attribute or the icon's label, so screen readers do not announce them as just "link" or "button".
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    function fix(root) {
        root.querySelectorAll('a, button, [role="button"]').forEach(function (el) {
            if ((el.textContent || '').trim() || el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.getAttribute('aria-labelledby')) { return; }
            var img = el.querySelector('img[alt]:not([alt=""])');
            if (img) { return; }
            var svgTitle = el.querySelector('svg title');
            var name = el.getAttribute('title') || (svgTitle && svgTitle.textContent) || el.getAttribute('data-tooltip') || '';
            if (!name && el.tagName === 'A' && el.hostname) {
                var map = { 'facebook.com': 'Facebook', 'x.com': 'X', 'twitter.com': 'X', 'instagram.com': 'Instagram', 'linkedin.com': 'LinkedIn', 'youtube.com': 'YouTube', 'tiktok.com': 'TikTok', 'pinterest.com': 'Pinterest', 'github.com': 'GitHub' };
                var host = el.hostname.replace(/^www\./, '');
                name = map[host] || '';
            }
            if (name) {
                el.setAttribute('aria-label', name.trim());
                el.querySelectorAll('svg, i, .icon').forEach(function (icon) { icon.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true'); });
            }
        });
    }
    fix(document);
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Elements with no title or labelled icon are left alone; add a title or aria-label to those in your theme or page builder.

snippets.title: Remove Autoplay From Embedded Videos
snippets.description: Strips autoplay settings from YouTube and Vimeo embeds in posts, so videos only start when the visitor presses play.
snippets.notes: Background videos added as Cover blocks are not embeds and are not changed by this snippet.

snippets.title: Allow Pinch-to-Zoom on Mobile
snippets.description: Removes maximum-scale and user-scalable=no from the page's viewport tag when a theme or plugin adds them, so visitors can zoom in on phones as WCAG requires.
snippets.notes: Runs early in the page head and only touches the viewport meta tag.

snippets.title: Announce the Number of Search Results
snippets.description: On search result pages, tells screen reader users how many results were found for their search as soon as the page loads.
snippets.notes: The message is read from a visually hidden live region; sighted visitors see no change.

snippets.title: Show File Type and Size on Document Links
snippets.description: Adds the file type and size, such as "(PDF, 2.4 MB)", after links to PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files in your content, so visitors know what they are about to download.
snippets.notes: The size is only shown for files stored in your uploads folder; links to other sites get the file type only.

snippets.title: Move Focus to the First Invalid Form Field
snippets.description: When a visitor submits a form with missing or invalid fields, moves keyboard focus to the first problem field and announces the browser's error message to screen readers.
snippets.notes: Uses the browser's built-in form validation, so it works with any form that uses required, type="email" and similar attributes.

snippets.title: Highlight Empty Alt Text Fields in the Media Modal
snippets.description: Outlines the Alternative Text field in red when it is empty in the media library and media modal, so authors notice it before inserting an image.
snippets.notes: Pure CSS; it reminds but does not block inserting images.

snippets.title: Turn On Captions by Default in YouTube Embeds
snippets.description: Adds YouTube's captions setting to embedded videos, so subtitles are shown automatically whenever the video has them.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_caption_lang to a language code such as en or fr to prefer that caption language.

snippets.title: Use Real Headings for Widget Titles
snippets.description: Makes classic sidebar widget titles proper H2 headings, so screen reader users can jump between widgets with heading navigation.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_widget_heading to h3 if your theme already uses H2 for the main sections around the sidebar.

snippets.title: Add a Main Landmark When the Theme Has None
snippets.description: Marks the theme's main content area with role="main" when the page has no main element, so screen reader users can jump straight to the content.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    if (document.querySelector('main, [role="main"]')) { return; }
    var area = document.querySelector('#primary, #content, .site-content, .content-area, #main, .entry-content');
    if (area) {
        area.setAttribute('role', 'main');
        if (!area.id) { area.id = 'wpide-main'; }
    }
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Add your theme's content wrapper to the selector list if it uses a different class or id.

snippets.title: Readable Tag Cloud Sizes
snippets.description: Keeps the smallest tags in tag cloud widgets and blocks large enough to read and tap, and sizes them in relative units so they grow with the visitor's text size.
snippets.notes: Change the smallest and largest values (in em) to fit your design.

snippets.title: Hide Decorative SVG Icons From Screen Readers
snippets.description: Adds aria-hidden to inline SVG icons that sit next to visible text inside links and buttons, so screen readers stop announcing meaningless graphic names.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    document.querySelectorAll('a svg, button svg').forEach(function (svg) {
        if (svg.hasAttribute('aria-hidden') || svg.getAttribute('role') === 'img' || svg.hasAttribute('aria-label')) { return; }
        var parent = svg.closest('a, button');
        var text = parent ? parent.textContent.replace(svg.textContent || '', '').trim() : '';
        if (text || (parent && parent.getAttribute('aria-label'))) {
            svg.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
            svg.setAttribute('focusable', 'false');
        }
    });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Icons that are the only content of a link are left alone so the link keeps a name.

snippets.title: Mark the Current Page in Menus Built With Blocks and Widgets
snippets.description: Adds aria-current="page" to any link on the page that points to the page being viewed, for menus, widget link lists and footer links that do not mark it themselves.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    var here = location.origin + location.pathname.replace(/\/$/, '');
    document.querySelectorAll('nav a[href], .widget a[href], footer a[href]').forEach(function (a) {
        if (a.hasAttribute('aria-current') || !a.href) { return; }
        var url;
        try { url = new URL(a.href); } catch (e) { return; }
        if (url.hash && url.pathname === location.pathname) { return; }
        if (url.origin + url.pathname.replace(/\/$/, '') === here) { a.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page'); }
    });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Links that already carry aria-current are not changed.

snippets.title: Return Focus After Closing Popups
snippets.description: Remembers which element opened a popup or modal dialog and moves keyboard focus back to it when the dialog closes, a common gap in theme and plugin popups.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    var opener = null;
    document.addEventListener('click', function (event) {
        var el = event.target.closest('a, button, [tabindex]');
        if (el && !el.closest('dialog, [role="dialog"], [aria-modal="true"]')) { opener = el; }
    }, true);
    function visible(d) {
        return d.isConnected && d.getAttribute('aria-hidden') !== 'true' && !d.hidden && (d.tagName !== 'DIALOG' || d.open) && d.getClientRects().length > 0;
    }
    var open = [];
    var pending = false;
    function check() {
        pending = false;
        var now = Array.prototype.filter.call(document.querySelectorAll('dialog, [role="dialog"], [aria-modal="true"]'), visible);
        var closed = open.filter(function (d) { return now.indexOf(d) === -1; });
        if (closed.length && opener && document.contains(opener)) {
            var active = document.activeElement;
            if (!active || active === document.body || !document.contains(active) || closed.some(function (d) { return d.contains(active); })) { opener.focus(); }
        }
        open = now;
    }
    new MutationObserver(function () {
        if (!pending) { pending = true; requestAnimationFrame(check); }
    }).observe(document.body, { subtree: true, childList: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['open', 'hidden', 'aria-hidden', 'class', 'style'] });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Works with dialogs that use the dialog element or role="dialog" and are hidden by removing them, hiding them or toggling aria-hidden.

snippets.title: Use Image Captions as Alt Text When Alt Is Empty
snippets.description: For image blocks that have a caption but no alternative text, uses the caption text as the alt attribute, so the image is not announced as unlabeled.
snippets.notes: A caption and alt text ideally say different things; treat this as a fallback and write real alt text where you can.

snippets.title: Remove Image Tooltips That Repeat the Alt Text
snippets.description: Removes the title attribute from images in your content when it is the same as the alt text, so screen readers do not read the same description twice.
snippets.notes: Titles that add different information are kept.

snippets.title: Give Theme Search Forms an Accessible Label
snippets.description: Adds an accessible name to the search field of theme search forms that have no label, so screen reader users hear "Search" instead of an unlabeled text field.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_search_label to translate the label.

snippets.title: Product Name as Alt Text for WooCommerce Images Without One
snippets.description: When a product image in the shop, on category pages or on the product page has no alternative text, uses the product name instead of leaving it empty.
snippets.notes: Images with their own alt text in the media library are not changed.

snippets.title: "Larger Text in the Editor" Profile Option
snippets.description: Adds a checkbox to each user's profile that makes the text in the block editor larger and more spaced out, for authors who find the default editor text hard to read.
snippets.notes: Only changes how content looks while editing; the published page is not affected.

snippets.title: High-Contrast Mode for wp-admin
snippets.description: Adds a "High contrast" checkbox to each user's profile that switches the dashboard to dark backgrounds, white text, yellow links and strong borders for that user only.
snippets.notes: Plugin screens with their own styling may not follow every rule; the block editor canvas keeps the theme's colors.

snippets.title: Collapsible Transcript Shortcode for Audio and Video
snippets.description: Adds a [transcript] shortcode that wraps the text version of a podcast or video in an accessible show/hide section, so every recording can have a transcript without cluttering the page.
snippets.notes: Use [transcript title="Read the interview transcript"]...[/transcript]; the section uses the native details element, so it works with keyboards and screen readers.

snippets.title: Hide Empty Headings From Screen Readers
snippets.description: Finds heading tags on the page that contain no text (often left behind by page builders and themes) and hides them from screen readers, so they do not show up as blank entries in the heading list.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6').forEach(function (h) {
        var text = (h.textContent || '').replace(/ /g, ' ').trim();
        var img = h.querySelector('img[alt]:not([alt=""]), svg[aria-label], [aria-label]');
        if (!text && !img) { h.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true'); }
    });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Fix empty headings at the source when you can; this keeps them from confusing screen reader users meanwhile.

snippets.title: Unstick Fixed Headers When Pages Are Zoomed In
snippets.description: Turns sticky and fixed headers into normal headers when the visible screen area is very small, such as at 400% browser zoom or on landscape phones, so they no longer cover most of the content.
snippets.notes: Add your theme's header selector if it is not in the list.

snippets.title: Comfortable Line Length for Reading
snippets.description: Limits paragraphs, lists and quotes in posts to about 75 characters per line, the width recommended for readability, while wide blocks such as images and tables keep the full width.
snippets.notes: Change 75ch to taste; 60 to 80 characters is a good range.

snippets.title: Pause Animated GIFs Until Clicked
snippets.description: Shows the first frame of every animated GIF in your content with a play button, and only plays the animation when the visitor clicks, so moving images never start on their own.
snippets.code:
<style>
.wpide-gif{position:relative;display:inline-block;max-width:100%;}
.wpide-gif canvas,.wpide-gif img{max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;}
.wpide-gif button{position:absolute;left:50%;top:50%;transform:translate(-50%,-50%);padding:10px 16px;border:2px solid #fff;border-radius:6px;background:rgba(0,0,0,.75);color:#fff;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;}
.wpide-gif button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #ffeb3b;outline-offset:2px;}
</style>
<script>
(function () {
    function freeze(img) {
        if (img.dataset.wpideGif) { return; }
        img.dataset.wpideGif = '1';
        var canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
        canvas.width = img.naturalWidth;
        canvas.height = img.naturalHeight;
        canvas.setAttribute('role', 'img');
        canvas.setAttribute('aria-label', img.alt || 'Animated image');
        try { canvas.getContext('2d').drawImage(img, 0, 0); } catch (e) { return; }
        var box = document.createElement('span');
        box.className = 'wpide-gif';
        var btn = document.createElement('button');
        btn.type = 'button';
        btn.textContent = 'Play animation';
        btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'false');
        img.parentNode.insertBefore(box, img);
        box.appendChild(canvas);
        box.appendChild(btn);
        img.style.display = 'none';
        box.appendChild(img);
        btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            var playing = btn.getAttribute('aria-pressed') === 'true';
            btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', playing ? 'false' : 'true');
            btn.textContent = playing ? 'Play animation' : 'Pause animation';
            canvas.style.display = playing ? 'block' : 'none';
            img.style.display = playing ? 'none' : 'block';
            if (!playing) { var src = img.src; img.src = ''; img.src = src; }
        });
    }
    document.querySelectorAll('.entry-content img[src*=".gif"], .wp-block-post-content img[src*=".gif"]').forEach(function (img) {
        if (img.complete && img.naturalWidth) { freeze(img); } else { img.addEventListener('load', function () { freeze(img); }, { once: true }); }
    });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: GIFs loaded from other domains still work; clicking again pauses the animation.

snippets.title: WP-CLI Command to Scan Content for Accessibility Problems
snippets.description: Adds a "wp a11y-scan" command that checks published posts and pages for images without alt text, empty links, iframes without titles, positive tabindex and skipped heading levels, and prints a table you can export.
snippets.notes: Run "wp a11y-scan --post_type=page --format=csv > report.csv"; it reads posts in batches so it works on large sites.

snippets.title: Accessibility Report for All Posts and Pages
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Accessibility Report, which checks your published posts and pages for images without alt text, empty links, iframes without titles and skipped heading levels, and lists each problem with an edit link.
snippets.notes: Checks 100 items per screen with "Next" links for large sites; results reflect the saved content, not theme or plugin output.

snippets.title: Stack Tables Into Labeled Cards on Phones
snippets.description: On small screens, turns each row of the tables in your content into a card where every value is shown with its column heading, so wide tables can be read without sideways scrolling.
snippets.code:
<style>
@media (max-width: 600px) {
    table.wpide-stack thead { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); }
    table.wpide-stack, table.wpide-stack tbody, table.wpide-stack tr, table.wpide-stack td, table.wpide-stack th[scope="row"] { display: block; width: 100%; }
    table.wpide-stack tr { margin: 0 0 1em; border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 6px; padding: .5em; }
    table.wpide-stack td { border: 0; padding: .25em 0; }
    table.wpide-stack td[data-label]::before { content: attr(data-label) ": "; font-weight: 700; }
}
</style>
<script>
(function () {
    document.querySelectorAll('.entry-content table, .wp-block-post-content table').forEach(function (table) {
        var headRow = table.tHead ? table.tHead.rows[0] : null;
        var bodyRows = table.tBodies.length ? Array.prototype.slice.call(table.tBodies[0].rows) : [];
        if (!headRow && bodyRows.length && bodyRows[0].querySelectorAll('th').length === bodyRows[0].cells.length) {
            headRow = bodyRows.shift();
            headRow.classList.add('wpide-stack-head');
        }
        if (!headRow) { return; }
        var labels = Array.prototype.map.call(headRow.cells, function (c) { return c.textContent.trim(); });
        bodyRows.forEach(function (row) {
            Array.prototype.forEach.call(row.cells, function (cell, i) {
                if (labels[i] && !cell.hasAttribute('data-label')) { cell.setAttribute('data-label', labels[i]); }
            });
        });
        table.classList.add('wpide-stack');
    });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Only tables with a header row are changed; the table keeps its real structure for screen readers.

snippets.title: Fixes for Windows High Contrast (Forced Colors) Mode
snippets.description: Makes buttons, focus outlines, icons and custom checkboxes stay visible when visitors use Windows High Contrast or another forced-colors mode, where many themes lose borders and icons.
snippets.notes: Only applies when the visitor's system forces its own colors; nobody else sees a difference.

snippets.title: Respect "Reduce Motion" in Elementor Animations
snippets.description: Shows Elementor content right away without entrance animations, motion effects or background slideshows for visitors whose device asks for reduced motion.
snippets.notes: Visitors without the reduced-motion setting still see your animations.

snippets.title: Respect "Reduce Motion" in Divi Animations
snippets.description: Turns off Divi's entrance animations, parallax and scroll effects for visitors whose device asks for reduced motion, while everyone else keeps the effects.
snippets.notes: Content hidden until its animation starts is made visible immediately.

snippets.title: Readability Score Panel in the Block Editor
snippets.description: Adds a "Readability" panel to the block editor sidebar with the word count, average sentence length, number of very long sentences and a Flesch reading ease score that updates as you write.
snippets.notes: The Flesch score is designed for English text; for other languages focus on sentence length.

snippets.title: Stop Audio and Unmuted Videos From Autoplaying
snippets.description: Removes the autoplay setting from audio players and from videos that are not muted in your content, so sound never starts without the visitor choosing to play it.
snippets.notes: Muted background videos keep autoplaying; use the reduced-motion video snippet if those should stop too.

snippets.title: "How We Use Your Data" Box at WooCommerce Checkout
snippets.description: Shows a short, plain-language summary above the checkout form explaining what order data you collect, why, and how long you keep it, with a link to your full privacy policy.
snippets.code:
How we use your data

  • We use your name, address and email only to process and deliver your order.
  • Payment details go straight to our payment provider; we never see or store your card number.
  • We keep order records for as long as tax law requires, then delete them.

Read our full privacy policy
snippets.notes: Edit the three points to match your store; keep them short so they do not distract from checking out.

snippets.title: Privacy Note Above the Easy Digital Downloads Checkout
snippets.description: Adds a short note above the Easy Digital Downloads purchase form explaining which details are collected for the order and linking to your privacy policy.
snippets.code: We only ask for the details needed to deliver your purchase, send your receipt and manage your licence. Privacy policy
snippets.notes: Change the wording to match how your store handles licences, receipts and newsletters.

snippets.title: Data Retention Note on the Order Thank-You Page
snippets.description: Adds a short note above the WooCommerce order confirmation telling customers how long their order data is kept and how to ask for a copy or deletion.
snippets.code: We keep your order details for 7 years because tax law requires it. You can ask for a copy of your data or for anything else we hold about you to be deleted at any time - see our privacy policy.
snippets.notes: Match the retention period to your WooCommerce privacy settings (WooCommerce > Settings > Accounts & Privacy).

snippets.title: Remove IP Addresses From Comment Notification Emails
snippets.description: Strips commenters' IP addresses and host names from the new comment and moderation emails WordPress sends to authors and administrators, so personal data does not pile up in inboxes.
snippets.notes: The IP address is still visible in the dashboard for administrators if you store it.

snippets.title: Buttons With Automatically Readable Text (SCSS)
snippets.description: Styles buttons from one brand color and picks black or white text automatically based on how light the color is, with matching hover and focus states, so button text always stays readable.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide-primary and $wpide-secondary; the brightness formula is an approximation, so still check final colors with a contrast checker.

snippets.title: "In Short" Plain-Language Summary Above Posts
snippets.description: Shows the post's excerpt in a highlighted "In short" box at the top of single posts, giving every reader, including people with reading or cognitive disabilities, a simple summary before the full text.
snippets.notes: Only hand-written excerpts are shown (posts without one show nothing), so write them in short, simple sentences.

snippets.title: Add the Page Language When the Theme Leaves It Out
snippets.description: Sets the lang attribute on the page's html element from your site language when a theme forgets to print it, so screen readers pronounce your content in the right language.
snippets.notes: Themes that call language_attributes() already do this; the script only acts when the attribute is missing.

snippets.title: Make Scrollable Areas Reachable by Keyboard
snippets.description: Finds code blocks, tables and other boxes that scroll sideways or vertically but contain nothing focusable, and makes them keyboard-focusable with a label, so keyboard users can scroll them with the arrow keys.
snippets.code:
<script>
(function () {
    function fix() {
        document.querySelectorAll('pre, .wp-block-table, .wp-block-code, figure, .table-responsive, [style*="overflow"]').forEach(function (el) {
            var scrolls = el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 2 || el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 2;
            var style = getComputedStyle(el);
            var canScroll = /(auto|scroll)/.test(style.overflowX + style.overflowY);
            if (!scrolls || !canScroll || el.hasAttribute('tabindex') || el.querySelector('a[href], button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]')) { return; }
            el.setAttribute('tabindex', '0');
            if (!el.getAttribute('role')) { el.setAttribute('role', 'region'); }
            if (!el.getAttribute('aria-label')) {
                var caption = el.querySelector('caption, figcaption');
                el.setAttribute('aria-label', caption ? caption.textContent.trim() : (el.tagName === 'PRE' || el.querySelector('code') ? 'Code example' : 'Scrollable content'));
            }
        });
    }
    window.addEventListener('load', fix);
    var timer;
    window.addEventListener('resize', function () { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(fix, 300); });
})();
</script>
snippets.notes: Runs once after the page loads and again when the window is resized.

snippets.title: Move Focus to WooCommerce Checkout Errors
snippets.description: When the classic WooCommerce checkout shows errors (such as a missing field or a declined card), moves keyboard focus to the error list and has screen readers read it out.
snippets.code:
<script>
jQuery(function ($) {
    $(document.body).on('checkout_error', function () {
        var box = document.querySelector('.woocommerce-NoticeGroup-checkout, .woocommerce-error');
        if (!box) { return; }
        box.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
        box.setAttribute('role', 'alert');
        setTimeout(function () { box.focus(); }, 100);
    });
});
</script>
snippets.notes: The block-based checkout handles this itself; this snippet is for the classic [woocommerce_checkout] shortcode checkout.

snippets.title: Announce Cart Updates on the WooCommerce Cart Page
snippets.description: Tells screen reader users when the cart has been updated after they change a quantity, remove a product or apply a coupon on the classic cart page, which otherwise happens silently.
snippets.notes: Uses its own polite live region, so no extra WordPress scripts are needed.

snippets.title: Hide Plugin and Theme Versions in Asset URLs
snippets.description: Replaces the ?ver= value on plugin and theme CSS and JavaScript files with a short hash, so scanners cannot read your exact plugin versions from the page source, while caches still refresh whenever a version changes.
snippets.notes: Plugin readme files can still reveal versions; block access to readme.txt files on your server for full coverage.

snippets.title: Pause Buttons for Auto-Rotating Sliders
snippets.description: Adds a visible pause/play button to every auto-rotating Swiper slider on the page (used by many themes, Elementor and slider plugins) and stops them automatically for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
snippets.code:
<style>
.wpide-slider-pause{position:absolute;right:8px;bottom:8px;z-index:20;padding:6px 12px;border:2px solid #fff;border-radius:4px;background:rgba(0,0,0,.7);color:#fff;font-size:14px;cursor:pointer;}
.wpide-slider-pause:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #ffeb3b;outline-offset:2px;}
</style>
<script>
window.addEventListener('load', function () {
    var reduce = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
    document.querySelectorAll('.swiper, .swiper-container').forEach(function (el) {
        var swiper = el.swiper;
        if (!swiper || !swiper.autoplay || !swiper.params.autoplay || el.querySelector('.wpide-slider-pause')) { return; }
        var btn = document.createElement('button');
        btn.type = 'button';
        btn.className = 'wpide-slider-pause';
        function set(paused) {
            if (paused) { swiper.autoplay.stop(); } else { swiper.autoplay.start(); }
            btn.textContent = paused ? 'Play slideshow' : 'Pause slideshow';
            btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', paused ? 'true' : 'false');
        }
        btn.addEventListener('click', function () { set(btn.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true'); });
        if (getComputedStyle(el).position === 'static') { el.style.position = 'relative'; }
        el.appendChild(btn);
        set(reduce);
    });
});
</script>
snippets.notes: Works with sliders built on Swiper; style .wpide-slider-pause to match your design.

snippets.title: Alt Text Editor for Images Missing a Description
snippets.description: Adds Media > Alt Text Editor, a page that lists images without alternative text with a thumbnail and a text field next to each, so you can describe dozens of images quickly and save them all at once.
snippets.notes: Shows 40 images per page, newest first; leave a field empty to skip that image.

snippets.title: Name Links That Contain Only an Image Without Alt Text
snippets.description: Gives links in your content whose only content is an image with empty alt text an accessible name, using the title of the page they point to, so screen readers no longer announce just the URL.
snippets.notes: Only links to pages and posts on your own site can be named automatically; looked-up titles are cached.

snippets.title: "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" Link
snippets.description: Adds a [do_not_sell_link] shortcode for the opt-out link US state privacy laws such as the CCPA require; clicking it records the visitor's opt-out in a cookie and tells marketing scripts held back by consent snippets not to run.
snippets.notes: Visitors who send the Global Privacy Control signal are treated as opted out automatically; your marketing tools still need to respect the wpide_optout cookie or the consent helpers.

snippets.title: Remember Commenters' Details for 30 Days Instead of a Year
snippets.description: Shortens how long the cookies that remember a commenter's name, email and website last, from WordPress's default of one year to 30 days.
snippets.notes: Change the number of days to suit your audience; the cookies are only set when the commenter ticks the consent box.

snippets.title: Limit How Many Files Non-Administrators Can Upload per Hour
snippets.description: Caps uploads at 30 files per hour for each user who is not an administrator, which limits the damage a compromised author account or a buggy front-end upload form can do.
snippets.notes: Raise $wpide_upload_hourly for teams that upload large batches of photos.

snippets.title: Sandbox Iframes From Untrusted Sites in Your Content
snippets.description: Adds a restrictive sandbox to iframes in posts that come from sites not on your trusted list, so an embedded page cannot redirect your visitors, open pop-ups or run scripts against your site.
snippets.notes: Add every service you embed on purpose to $wpide_trusted_frames; sandboxed embeds from other sites may lose some features.

snippets.title: Convert MyISAM Database Tables to InnoDB
snippets.description: Run on demand to convert your site's remaining MyISAM tables to InnoDB, the modern MySQL engine that handles many visitors at once far better and survives crashes more safely.
snippets.notes: Back up the database first and run it during a quiet period, since large tables take a while; tables already using InnoDB are skipped.

snippets.title: Remove Leftover Data From Uninstalled Plugins
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Leftover Plugin Data, where you enter a prefix (such as old_slider_) to see how many options, post meta, user meta and scheduled tasks use it, and delete them after reviewing the counts.
snippets.notes: Prefixes shorter than 4 characters and WordPress's own prefixes are refused; always preview first and keep a backup.

snippets.title: Block Login Attempts From Scripts and Command-Line Tools
snippets.description: Refuses login, password reset and registration requests sent by tools such as curl, wget, python-requests or empty user agents, which real browsers never use and brute-force scripts often do.
snippets.notes: Legitimate apps that log in through wp-login.php with such tools will be blocked too; the REST API and application passwords are not affected.

snippets.title: Ask for the Current Password Before Changing Email or Password
snippets.description: Adds a "Current password" field to the profile screen and refuses changes to your own email address or password unless it is correct, so someone using an unattended logged-in browser cannot take over the account.
snippets.notes: Applies only when users edit their own profile; administrators editing other users are not asked.

snippets.title: Turn Off Avatars in the Dashboard Only
snippets.description: Stops wp-admin from loading an avatar for every row of the comments and users screens and the dashboard, which saves dozens of requests to Gravatar, while avatars keep showing on the front of the site.
snippets.notes: The block editor and front-end comment lists are not affected.

snippets.title: Turn Off Justified Text for Easier Reading
snippets.description: Aligns justified paragraphs in posts to the start of the line instead, because the uneven gaps that justified text creates make reading harder for people with dyslexia and low vision.
snippets.notes: Paragraphs you centered or right-aligned in the editor keep their alignment; only justified text and the theme's default paragraph alignment are changed.

snippets.title: Old Revisions Cleanup Tool
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Clean Up Revisions, which shows how many post revisions your database holds and deletes revisions older than a chosen number of days after you confirm, always keeping the newest few per post.
snippets.notes: Back up your database first; it works in batches of 500 so it never times out, so click again until the count reaches zero.

snippets.title: Orphaned Metadata Cleanup Tool
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Orphaned Metadata, which counts post, comment, term and user meta rows whose post, comment, term or user no longer exists, and removes them after you confirm.
snippets.notes: Leftover rows usually come from deleted plugins or direct database edits; take a backup before deleting.

snippets.title: Auto-Drafts and Trash Cleanup Tool
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Clean Up Drafts and Trash with counts of leftover auto-drafts, trashed posts and trashed or spam comments, and a button to remove them all permanently after confirmation.
snippets.notes: Auto-drafts are empty placeholders WordPress creates when you open the editor; they are safe to delete once they are a day old.

snippets.title: Clear the Embed (oEmbed) Cache
snippets.description: Run on demand to delete every cached embed (videos, tweets and other oEmbed results) from the database, so they are fetched fresh and stale or broken embeds disappear.
snippets.notes: Run it from the snippet editor; embeds are fetched again the next time each page is viewed.

snippets.title: Remove Orphaned Term Relationships and Fix Term Counts
snippets.description: Run on demand to delete category and tag links that point to posts that no longer exist, and then recount how many posts each term has.
snippets.notes: Run it from the snippet editor; on very large sites run it outside busy hours.

snippets.title: Remove Duplicate Post Meta Rows
snippets.description: Run on demand to find custom field rows that are exact duplicates (same post, key and value) and keep only one of each, a common side effect of buggy imports and plugins.
snippets.notes: Only exact duplicates are removed, keeping the oldest row; back up your database first.

snippets.title: Database Table Sizes and Optimize Buttons
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Database Tables listing every table of your site with its row count, data and index size and reclaimable space, sorted by size, with an Optimize button for tables that need it.
snippets.notes: Optimizing locks the table briefly on MyISAM; on InnoDB it rebuilds the table, so run it outside peak hours.

snippets.title: Autoloaded Options Inspector
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Autoloaded Options showing the total size of options WordPress loads on every page and the 40 largest ones, with a button to stop autoloading any option that does not need it.
snippets.notes: Turning autoload off is safe for options a plugin only reads now and then; core options such as siteurl, active_plugins and cron are protected.

snippets.title: Find and Remove Orphaned Cron Events
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Orphaned Cron Events, listing scheduled tasks that no active plugin or theme handles any more (often left by uninstalled plugins) and removing them after you confirm.
snippets.notes: A task is shown when nothing is hooked to it on admin pages; a few plugins only hook their tasks during cron, so check the hook names before deleting.

snippets.title: Keep WooCommerce Logs for 7 Days
snippets.description: Makes WooCommerce delete its log entries (payment gateways, shipping, webhooks and more) after 7 days instead of 30, keeping the log table and folder small.
snippets.notes: Raise the number while you are debugging a payment or shipping problem.

snippets.title: Delete Image Size Files No Longer Registered
snippets.description: Adds Tools > Unused Image Sizes, which finds resized copies of your images made for sizes your current theme and plugins no longer register, shows how much space they take, and deletes them in batches after confirmation.
snippets.notes: Pages that still hard-code a removed size will fall back to a larger size; back up your uploads folder first.

snippets.title: Delete All Pingbacks and Trackbacks
snippets.description: Run on demand to permanently delete every pingback and trackback stored as a comment, which on older blogs are often thousands of spammy rows nobody reads.
snippets.notes: Run it from the snippet editor; pair it with a snippet that disables pingbacks so new ones do not arrive.

snippets.title: Remove Expired Login Sessions From the Database
snippets.description: Once a day, removes expired login sessions that WordPress keeps in user meta until the user logs in again, which on membership sites and shops adds up to a lot of dead data.
snippets.notes: Processes up to 500 users per run; active sessions are never touched.

snippets.title: Duplicate Database Queries Report for Administrators
snippets.description: Add ?wpide_queries=1 to any page while logged in as an administrator to see, at the bottom of the page, the queries that ran more than once and the ten slowest queries, with the code that called them.
snippets.notes: Query logging only switches on for that one request, so normal visitors and pages are not slowed down.

snippets.title: Log Pages That Run Too Many Database Queries
snippets.description: Records front-end URLs that run more database queries than a limit you set, with the query count and load time, and lists the worst offenders under Tools > Heavy Pages.
snippets.notes: Keeps the 100 most recent heavy pages in one option; nothing is logged for admin, AJAX, REST or cron requests.

snippets.title: Log Slow Outgoing HTTP Requests
snippets.description: Times every request your site makes to other servers (update checks, APIs, license servers) and records the ones slower than a second under Tools > Slow HTTP Calls, so you can find what is holding up page loads.
snippets.notes: Keeps the latest 100 slow calls; URLs are stored without their query strings so API keys are not logged.

snippets.title: Log Scheduled Tasks That Take Too Long
snippets.description: Measures how long each scheduled task (cron event) takes to run and records the slow ones under Tools > Slow Cron Tasks, so you can spot the plugin that makes WP-Cron sluggish.
snippets.notes: Only runs during cron requests; tasks faster than $wpide_cron_slow seconds are not recorded.

snippets.title: Server-Timing Header for Administrators
snippets.description: Adds a Server-Timing header with PHP time, database query count and peak memory to pages viewed by administrators, so you can read the numbers in your browser's developer tools Network tab.
snippets.notes: Visitors never receive the header; the time covers everything WordPress does before the page template starts rendering.

snippets.title: Collect Real Core Web Vitals From Your Visitors
snippets.description: Measures Largest Contentful Paint, Cumulative Layout Shift and Interaction to Next Paint in visitors' browsers and shows the 75th percentile of the last 7 days per page type in a dashboard widget.
snippets.notes: Samples 20% of page views by default and stores only numbers per page type, no visitor data; values are rounded and capped to keep storage tiny.

snippets.title: Find What Is Calling admin-ajax.php
snippets.description: Counts admin-ajax.php requests per action (and whether they come from the front end or the dashboard) for the current day and the previous six, and shows the busiest ones under Tools > AJAX Usage.
snippets.notes: Counts are batched in memory and written once per request; deactivate the snippet when you have found the culprit.

snippets.title: Page Weight Summary in the Admin Bar
snippets.description: Shows an admin bar item on the front of the site with the total size of the page's scripts, stylesheets, images and fonts, and a breakdown with the heaviest files when you click it.
snippets.notes: Sizes are the transferred (compressed) bytes reported by your browser; files served from another domain without timing headers count as 0.

snippets.title: Site Health Check for Compression and Browser Caching
snippets.description: Adds a Site Health test that requests your homepage and one of your theme's stylesheets and reports whether text files are compressed (gzip or Brotli) and whether static files get long browser cache lifetimes.
snippets.notes: Both are configured in your web server or CDN, not in WordPress; the result is cached for 12 hours.

snippets.title: Preload a Chosen Hero Image per Page
snippets.description: Adds a "Preload hero image" field to the post and page editor; when filled in with an image URL, that image is preloaded with high priority on that page, improving Largest Contentful Paint for pages whose main image is not the featured image.
snippets.notes: Use it for hero images set in page builders or cover blocks; preloading the wrong image wastes bandwidth, so pick the one visible at the top.

snippets.title: Delay Third-Party Scripts Until the Visitor Interacts
snippets.description: Holds back the scripts you list (chat widgets, heatmaps, social widgets) until the visitor first scrolls, taps, clicks or presses a key, or after a timeout, so they no longer slow down the initial page load.
snippets.notes: List handles or parts of script URLs; never delay scripts that render content above the fold or that other scripts depend on.

snippets.title: Remove Block Theme Styles From Classic Themes
snippets.description: Stops classic (non-block) themes from loading the global styles, classic theme styles and duotone SVG filters that WordPress adds for block themes, saving inline CSS on every page.
snippets.notes: Only runs on classic themes; check that buttons and colors set in the editor still look right after enabling it.

snippets.title: Inline Small Block Stylesheets Instead of Loading Files
snippets.description: Lets WordPress print more of the small per-block stylesheets directly in the page instead of as separate files, which saves several network requests on pages with many different blocks.
snippets.notes: Works together with loading block styles separately; raise or lower the byte budget to balance page size against request count.

snippets.title: Preload Key Scripts and Stylesheets by Handle
snippets.description: Adds preload hints for the enqueued scripts and stylesheets you name, so the browser fetches files that are discovered late (such as a slider script or icon font CSS) right at the start of the page load.
snippets.notes: Only handles that are actually enqueued on the current page are preloaded; preloading too much slows down more important files.

snippets.title: Show Text Immediately While Google Fonts Load
snippets.description: Adds display=swap to every Google Fonts stylesheet your theme and plugins load, so text appears right away in a fallback font instead of staying invisible while the web font downloads.
snippets.notes: URLs that already set a display value are left alone.

snippets.title: Prefetch the Next Page of Archives and Paginated Posts
snippets.description: Adds a prefetch hint for the next page of blog archives, category pages and multi-page posts, so it opens almost instantly when visitors click "Next".
snippets.notes: Prefetching uses a little extra bandwidth for visitors who never click; it is skipped for visitors with data saver turned on.

snippets.title: Inline Critical CSS From Your Theme
snippets.description: Prints the contents of a critical.css file from your active theme folder directly in the page head, so above-the-fold content is styled before the main stylesheet finishes loading.
snippets.notes: Generate a critical.css file (under 14 KB) with a critical CSS tool and put it in your (child) theme folder; nothing happens until the file exists.

snippets.title: Add Missing Width and Height to Images in Content
snippets.description: Adds width and height attributes to images in your posts that lack them (for example images pasted from other sites or old posts), using the real image file size, which prevents layout jumps while pages load.
snippets.notes: Only images stored in your uploads folder can be measured; sizes are cached per image so files are not read on every page view.

snippets.title: Serve Media and Static Files From a CDN Domain
snippets.description: Rewrites the URLs of your uploads, theme and plugin files to a CDN or pull-zone domain you set, so images, CSS and JavaScript are delivered from the CDN while pages are still served by your site.
snippets.notes: Create a pull zone that points to your site first and set $wpide_cdn_url to its address; admin pages and the block editor keep using your own domain.

snippets.title: Cache-Busting Versions Based on File Changes
snippets.description: Replaces the version number on your theme's and plugins' CSS and JavaScript URLs with the file's last-modified time, so browsers and CDNs cache files for a long time but always fetch a fresh copy right after you change one.
snippets.notes: File times are cached in memory for the request; WordPress core files keep their normal version.

snippets.title: Skip Rendering Off-Screen Comments and Footers Until Needed
snippets.description: Uses the CSS content-visibility property so browsers skip laying out the comments section, footer and related posts until the visitor scrolls near them, which speeds up rendering of long pages.
snippets.notes: Adjust the selectors to your theme; the size hint keeps the scrollbar from jumping.

snippets.title: Load the WooCommerce Password Strength Meter Only When Needed
snippets.description: Removes the password strength meter script (about 400 KB with its dictionary) from every page except the account, checkout and password reset pages where customers actually choose a password.
snippets.notes: The meter still appears on the pages where it is useful.

snippets.title: Browser and CDN Caching for Feeds and Sitemaps
snippets.description: Sends cache headers on RSS feeds and XML sitemaps so feed readers, crawlers and CDNs can reuse them for an hour instead of making WordPress rebuild them on every request.
snippets.notes: Lower $wpide_feed_cache_seconds if you publish many times an hour and want new posts to appear in feeds faster.

snippets.title: Cache Slow Shortcodes With a Wrapper Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [cached] shortcode you wrap around any slow shortcode or content, such as [cached ttl="3600"][some_feed][/cached]; its output is stored for the time you choose and served from cache after that.
snippets.notes: Do not wrap content that differs per visitor (cart, account, forms with nonces); the cache is cleared whenever the post is updated.

snippets.title: Cache Public REST API Responses for Visitors
snippets.description: Stores the responses of public GET requests to the REST API (such as post lists used by headless front ends and block widgets) for a few minutes for logged-out visitors, and clears the cache when content changes.
snippets.notes: Only routes in $wpide_rest_cache_routes are cached and requests using _embed are skipped; with a persistent object cache the entries live in memory instead of the database.

snippets.title: Send Emails in the Background
snippets.description: Queues emails sent by WordPress and plugins and sends them a few seconds later through WP-Cron, so form submissions, orders and registrations no longer wait for the mail server.
snippets.notes: Emails with attachments are sent immediately, because temporary attachment files may be gone later; make sure WP-Cron runs reliably.

snippets.title: Turn Off Autosave for Chosen Post Types
snippets.description: Stops the editor from autosaving the post types you list (for example products or custom data types edited by many people), which removes frequent background requests and extra autosave revisions.
snippets.notes: Unsaved changes are lost if the browser crashes, so only use it for post types where that is acceptable.

snippets.title: Stop Crawlers Paging Endlessly Through Old Archives
snippets.description: Returns a "not found" page for archive pages beyond page 50 (such as /page/873/) for logged-out visitors, which keeps bots from hammering your database with very slow deep pagination queries.
snippets.notes: Visitors can still reach old posts through search, categories and the sitemap; raise $wpide_max_page if your archives are browsed that deep on purpose.

snippets.title: Cache Site-Wide Comment Counts
snippets.description: Stores the comment totals that WordPress shows in the admin menu, toolbar and dashboard for 10 minutes, avoiding a slow counting query on every admin page view on sites with many comments.
snippets.notes: The cache is cleared whenever a comment is added, approved, spammed or deleted, so counts stay accurate.

snippets.title: Preload Header for Your Theme Stylesheet
snippets.description: Sends an HTTP Link preload header for your theme's main stylesheet, so browsers, and CDNs that support Early Hints, start downloading the CSS before the HTML has even arrived.
snippets.notes: Add more files (for example a key web font) to $wpide_link_preloads; keep the list short, since preloading too much slows everything else down.

snippets.title: Stop Yoast SEO Building Indexables on Small or Busy Sites
snippets.description: Turns off Yoast SEO's indexables, the background tables Yoast fills for every post and term, which removes heavy database writes on large sites or cheap hosting.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'Yoast\WP\SEO\should_index_indexables', '__return_false' );
snippets.notes: Yoast features that depend on indexables (internal linking suggestions, some insights) stop working; SEO titles, meta and sitemaps keep working.

snippets.title: Keep Speculative Loading Away From Cart, Checkout and Account Pages
snippets.description: Tells WordPress's built-in speculative loading (prefetching pages on hover) to skip cart, checkout and account pages, which are personal, never cached and expensive to build, so hovering over their links no longer costs server time.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.8 or later; WooCommerce page addresses are detected automatically, and you can add other paths such as a members area.

snippets.title: Hold Tracking Scripts Until the Visitor Consents
snippets.description: Turns the scripts you list by handle into inactive placeholders and only runs them after the visitor gives consent, through the WP Consent API when a consent plugin provides it or the simple wpide_consent cookie otherwise.
snippets.notes: Find script handles with a "list enqueued assets" snippet; scripts that other scripts depend on should not be held back.

snippets.title: Show Embeds Only After Consent With a Shortcode
snippets.description: Wraps any embed or HTML in [consent_content category="marketing"]...[/consent_content] so it stays hidden behind a short notice until the visitor consents, using the WP Consent API when available.
snippets.notes: The notice offers a "Load content" button that unlocks this item only; full consent still comes from your cookie banner.

snippets.title: Store Only Shortened IP Addresses for Comments
snippets.description: Saves commenters' IP addresses with the last part removed (for example 203.0.113.0), which is still enough for spam checks but no longer identifies a person.
snippets.notes: Set $wpide_comment_ip_mode to 'none' to store no IP address at all; some anti-spam services work less well without it.

snippets.title: Don't Store Commenters' Browser Details
snippets.description: Stops WordPress from saving each commenter's browser user agent string with their comment, which is rarely needed and counts as personal data.
snippets.code: add_filter( 'pre_comment_user_agent', '__return_empty_string', 20 );
snippets.notes: Akismet still receives the user agent at submission time for its spam check; it is just not stored.

snippets.title: Anonymize Comment IP Addresses After 60 Days
snippets.description: Once a day, shortens the stored IP address of approved comments older than 60 days, so you keep recent IPs for spam handling without holding personal data forever.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_ip_retention_days to your retention period; already-shortened addresses are skipped.

snippets.title: Delete Spam Comments Older Than 30 Days
snippets.description: Permanently removes comments marked as spam once they are older than 30 days, so spammers' names, emails and IP addresses do not pile up in your database.
snippets.notes: Runs daily in batches of 200; check the Spam folder now and then if you rely on rescuing false positives.

snippets.title: Don't Keep Full IP Addresses in Login Sessions
snippets.description: Shortens the IP address and drops the browser details WordPress stores with every login session, so session records no longer hold full personal data.
snippets.notes: Security snippets that compare session IPs will compare the shortened address instead.

snippets.title: Remove Completed Privacy Requests After 90 Days
snippets.description: Deletes finished export and erasure requests (and failed ones) from Tools > Export/Erase Personal Data once they are 90 days old, since the request records themselves contain email addresses.
snippets.notes: Keep records longer if you need them as proof that requests were handled.

snippets.title: Inactive Subscribers Cleanup Page
snippets.description: Adds Users > Inactive Subscribers, listing subscriber accounts older than two years that have never commented, with checkboxes to delete the ones you select after a confirmation.
snippets.notes: Only the subscriber role is listed and nothing is deleted without your confirmation; customers of shops and members of membership plugins usually have their own roles.

snippets.title: Include Custom Profile Fields in Personal Data Exports
snippets.description: Adds the custom user fields you list (such as phone or company) to the personal data export file WordPress creates under Tools > Export Personal Data.
snippets.notes: List the meta keys your theme or plugins store for users, with the label you want in the export.

snippets.title: Erase Custom Profile Fields on Erasure Requests
