snippets.description: Adds a [show_date] shortcode that prints today's date, or a date relative to it such as "+3 days" or "next friday", in any format, for delivery promises, deadlines and offer end dates.
snippets.notes: Example [show_date offset="+2 weekdays" format="l, F j"]; uses the site time zone. Pages cached by a caching plugin show the date they were cached.

snippets.title: "Years Since" Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [years_since] shortcode that prints how many full years have passed since a date, such as years in business, years of experience or a person's age, so the number never goes out of date.
snippets.notes: Example "Serving customers for [years_since date='2009-05-01'] years".

snippets.title: Download Button Shortcode With File Size
snippets.description: Adds a [download_button] shortcode that turns a Media Library file into a download button showing the file type and size, such as "Brochure (PDF, 2.4 MB)".
snippets.notes: Example [download_button id="123" text="Get the brochure"]; find the ID in the Media Library address bar when you open the file.

snippets.title: Link Card for Another Post Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [post_card] shortcode that shows another post or page as a card with its image, title and excerpt, perfect for "see also" links inside articles.
snippets.notes: Example [post_card id="42"] or [post_card slug="pricing" type="page"]; only published items are shown.

snippets.title: Opening Hours Shortcode With "Open Now" Status
snippets.description: Adds an [opening_hours] shortcode that prints your weekly opening hours as a table, highlights today and shows whether you are open right now, based on the site time zone.
snippets.notes: Edit $wpide_opening_hours (use an empty string for closed days); add status="only" to print just the open or closed badge. Full-page caching can delay the status.

snippets.title: "Get Directions" Map Link Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [map_link] shortcode that links an address to Google Maps or Apple Maps directions, opening the visitor's maps app on phones, without embedding a map or loading any script.
snippets.notes: Example [map_link address="10 Downing St, London" text="Get directions"]; add app="apple" for Apple Maps links.

snippets.title: PDF Viewer Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [pdf_viewer] shortcode that shows a PDF from the Media Library or a URL inside the page with the browser's built-in viewer, plus a download link for phones that cannot display it inline.
snippets.notes: Example [pdf_viewer id="123" height="800"]; PDFs from other domains may be blocked from embedding by that site.

snippets.title: "Coming Soon" Block Listing Scheduled Posts
snippets.description: Registers a "Coming Soon" block, rendered on the server without a build step, that lists the titles and dates of your next scheduled posts to build anticipation for upcoming content.
snippets.notes: Only titles and dates are shown, never content; choose how many posts to list in the block settings.

snippets.title: "Pages in This Section" Block
snippets.description: Registers a server-rendered block that lists the other pages sharing the current page's parent, with the current page marked, giving every section of a large site its own side navigation.
snippets.notes: On a top-level page it lists that page's children instead; add the block to a page template so every page in the section gets it.

snippets.title: Contact Card Block
snippets.description: Registers a "Contact Card" block, rendered on the server, where you type a name, role, phone, email and address in the sidebar and get a tidy card with tap-to-call and email links.
snippets.notes: Uses semantic h-card markup; style it with the .wpide-contact-card class.

snippets.title: Site Announcement Block Managed in Settings
snippets.description: Adds an "Announcement" text field to Settings > General and a block that displays it, so you can place the block on many pages and change the message everywhere from one setting.
snippets.notes: The block outputs nothing while the setting is empty, so you can leave it in place between announcements.

snippets.title: Block Bindings Source: Author Details
snippets.description: Registers a block bindings source so paragraphs, headings, buttons and images can show the post author's name, bio, archive link or avatar, which is handy for author boxes in block themes.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.5+; bind with "source":"wpide/author" and args {"key":"name"} (also bio, url, avatar) in the block's metadata.bindings.

snippets.title: Block Bindings Source: Formatted Post Dates
snippets.description: Registers a block bindings source that fills blocks with the post's published or last updated date in any format, so you can write "Updated on ..." in a paragraph inside block templates.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.5+; bind with "source":"wpide/dates" and args {"key":"modified","format":"F j, Y"} (keys published, modified, year).

snippets.title: Block Bindings Source: Main Category
snippets.description: Registers a block bindings source that shows a post's main category name, link or description in any paragraph, heading or button, for example as a label above titles in a Query Loop.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.5+; bind with "source":"wpide/category" and args {"key":"name"} (also link, description). The first category alphabetically is used.

snippets.title: Your Own Block Category at the Top of the Inserter
snippets.description: Adds a block category named after your site to the top of the block inserter and moves custom blocks with a chosen namespace into it, so editors find your bespoke blocks first.
snippets.notes: Set $wpide_block_namespaces to the prefix of your blocks, such as acme/ or wpide/.

snippets.title: Show Additional CSS Inside the Block Editor
snippets.description: Loads the CSS from Appearance > Customize > Additional CSS into the block editor canvas, so posts look the same while you write as they do on the site.
snippets.notes: Rules are scoped to the editor canvas automatically; very broad selectors such as body may still need small tweaks.

snippets.title: Block Usage Report Under Tools
snippets.description: Adds a Tools > Block Usage screen counting how many posts and pages use each block, with a link to the content using it, so you know which blocks and plugins are safe to remove.
snippets.notes: Scans up to 2,000 published and draft items and caches the result for an hour; click "Rescan" to refresh.

snippets.title: "Used In" Column for Synced Patterns
snippets.description: Adds a "Used in" column to the Patterns list (Appearance > Editor > Patterns > Manage) showing how many posts and pages include each synced pattern, so you know what changes will affect.
snippets.notes: Counts are cached for an hour; patterns nested inside other patterns are counted once for the outer pattern only.

snippets.title: Default Block Template for a Custom Post Type
snippets.description: Registers a block template from code, such as "Single Event", that block themes use automatically for a custom post type, so new post types look right without building the template by hand.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.7+ and a block theme; set the post type slug and edit the block markup. A template saved in the Site Editor overrides this one.

snippets.title: Abbreviation Button in the Block Toolbar
snippets.description: Adds an "Abbreviation" option to the text formatting menu that wraps selected text such as "SEO" in an abbr tag with its full meaning, shown as a tooltip and read by screen readers.
snippets.notes: Select the abbreviation, open the dropdown arrow in the toolbar and choose Abbreviation; click it again on marked text to remove it.

snippets.title: Convert Classic Blocks to Regular Blocks on Open
snippets.description: Converts old "Classic" content into proper paragraph, heading, list and image blocks as soon as a post is opened in the block editor, then tells you so you can review before saving.
snippets.notes: Nothing changes until you save; use Undo or leave without saving to keep the classic block.

snippets.title: Warn About Oversized Images Before Publishing
snippets.description: Lists image blocks whose original file is larger than a size you set, such as 1 MB, in the block editor's publish panel, so heavy photos get replaced before they slow down the page.
snippets.notes: Set $wpide_max_image_kb; the check reads file sizes WordPress stored at upload, so very old uploads without that data are skipped.

snippets.title: Show the Post ID and Short Link in the Block Editor
snippets.description: Adds the post ID and a copyable short link (?p=123) to the Summary panel of the block editor sidebar, which is handy for shortcodes, support tickets and quick sharing.
snippets.notes: The short link always redirects to the current address, even after the slug changes.

snippets.title: Hide Selected Page Templates From Non-Administrators
snippets.description: Removes chosen templates, such as a landing page or a blank canvas, from the template picker for editors and authors, so only administrators can apply layouts that need care.
snippets.notes: List template file names (classic themes, such as template-landing.php) or slugs (block themes, such as blank) in $wpide_admin_only_templates; pages already using them keep working.

snippets.title: Replace a Media File and Keep Its URL
snippets.description: Adds a "Replace file" box to the media edit screen that uploads a new version of an image, PDF or other file over the old one, keeping the same address so every link and embed updates at once.
snippets.notes: The new file must be the same type (for example JPEG for JPEG); image sizes are regenerated automatically. Browsers and CDNs may show the old file until their cache expires.

snippets.title: "Where Is This File Used?" Box in the Media Library
snippets.description: Adds a box to the media edit screen listing every post and page that shows the file in its content or as its featured image, so you can check before replacing or deleting it.
snippets.notes: Searches content for the file name and the image block ID; files used by page builders that store data elsewhere may not be found.

snippets.title: Unused Media Files Report
snippets.description: Adds a Media > Unused Files screen listing uploads that are not attached to any content, not used as a featured image and not found in any post, so you can review and tidy the Media Library.
snippets.notes: Nothing is deleted automatically; check each file before removing it, as themes, widgets and page builders can use files in ways this report cannot see.

snippets.title: Show SVG Previews and Dimensions in the Media Library
snippets.description: Makes uploaded SVG files show a real preview in the Media Library grid and attachment details, and stores their width and height from the viewBox so they display at the right size in posts.
snippets.notes: Only affects SVG files you are already allowed to upload; it does not enable SVG uploads by itself.

snippets.title: Set WebP and AVIF Image Quality
snippets.description: Sets the compression quality WordPress uses when it creates WebP and AVIF images, separately from JPEG, so you can trade a little sharpness for much smaller files.
snippets.notes: Applies to newly generated images only; regenerate thumbnails to update existing ones. WordPress's default is 86 for WebP.

snippets.title: Lower Quality for Small Thumbnails, Higher for Large Images
snippets.description: Saves small thumbnails with stronger compression and large images with higher quality, so grids load fast while hero images stay crisp, instead of one quality for everything.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.8+, which tells the quality filter which size is being made; applies to JPEG and WebP images created from now on.

snippets.title: Add the Date to Uploaded File Names
snippets.description: Prefixes uploaded file names with the upload date, such as 2025-03-14-team-photo.jpg, so files sort chronologically on the server and in downloads.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_upload_date_format, for example to Ymd; files that already start with a date are left alone.

snippets.title: Store Uploads in Folders Named After the Post Type
snippets.description: Saves files uploaded from inside a post, page or custom post into a folder named after its type, such as uploads/products/ or uploads/pages/, keeping the year and month folders inside.
snippets.notes: Only affects new uploads made from the editor; files uploaded directly to the Media Library keep the default folders.

snippets.title: Crop Thumbnails From the Top Instead of the Center
snippets.description: Makes WordPress crop square thumbnails from the top of each image rather than the middle, so heads in portraits and headlines in screenshots are not cut off.
snippets.notes: Applies to new uploads; regenerate thumbnails to update existing images. Also works for other cropped sizes listed in $wpide_top_crop_sizes.

snippets.title: Center Inserted Images by Default
snippets.description: Makes images inserted in the classic editor and the media window centered by default instead of having no alignment, which suits most single-column blogs.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_image_align to left, right or none.

snippets.title: Open the Media Library in List View
snippets.description: Shows Media > Library as a table by default instead of the thumbnail grid, which makes file names, dates, authors and attachment details easier to scan on large libraries.
snippets.notes: Users can still switch to the grid with the icons above the list; the default only applies when no mode is chosen in the address.

snippets.title: Camera Details Box for Photos
snippets.description: Adds a "Camera details" box to the media edit screen showing the camera, lens settings, ISO, shutter speed, focal length and date taken that WordPress read from the photo.
snippets.notes: Only shows values that were in the file at upload time; photos stripped of metadata show nothing.

snippets.title: Use Media Library Alt Text for Images Missing It in Posts
snippets.description: When an image in a post has an empty alt attribute but its Media Library entry has alt text, the library text is used on the page, fixing older posts without editing them.
snippets.notes: Images deliberately left with empty alt text are filled too if the library has a description; clear the library alt text for decorative images.

snippets.title: "Regenerate Sizes" Link for a Single Image
snippets.description: Adds a "Regenerate sizes" link under each image in the Media Library list that rebuilds all its thumbnails, useful after changing image sizes or fixing a bad crop, without a plugin.
snippets.notes: Old size files that are no longer registered stay on disk; for whole-library runs use "wp media regenerate" in WP-CLI.

snippets.title: List the Generated Sizes of Each Image
snippets.description: Adds a box to the image edit screen listing every size WordPress generated for it, with dimensions, file size and a link to open each one, to check crops and spot missing sizes.
snippets.notes: Sizes registered after the image was uploaded will be missing until you regenerate it.

snippets.title: Search Media by Alt Text Too
snippets.description: Makes the Media Library search, in both the grid and list views and the media picker, also match images by their alt text, which often describes the image better than the file name.
snippets.notes: Only adds matches; normal title, caption and file name searches keep working.

snippets.title: Shorten Very Long Upload File Names
snippets.description: Trims uploaded file names longer than 60 characters, such as camera exports or copied web titles, to a tidy length before saving, while keeping the extension.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_max_file_name_length; WordPress still adds -1, -2 when a name is already taken.

snippets.title: Delete a Custom Field From Every Post (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp delete-meta-key" command that removes one custom field key from all posts of a type, for example leftovers from an old SEO or page builder plugin, with a count before anything is deleted.
snippets.notes: Example "wp delete-meta-key _old_plugin_data --post_type=page --yes"; back up the database first.

snippets.title: Media Library Disk Usage by Type and Year (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp media-usage" command that totals how much disk space uploads use, grouped by file type or by upload year, including every generated image size, to see what fills your hosting space.
snippets.notes: Run "wp media-usage --by=year" or "--by=type" (default); it reads file sizes from disk, so large libraries take a moment.

snippets.title: Find the Largest Custom Field Values (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp largest-meta" command listing the biggest post, user and term meta rows with their key and owner, the quickest way to find plugins bloating the database with huge serialized data.
snippets.notes: Example "wp largest-meta --table=user --limit=20"; read-only.

snippets.title: Rename a Shortcode Across All Content (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp rename-shortcode" command that changes every use of one shortcode tag to another in posts and pages, attributes and closing tags included, useful when switching plugins.
snippets.notes: Example "wp rename-shortcode old_button button --yes"; without --yes it only counts. Revisions are created so changes can be rolled back per post.

snippets.title: List Every Shortcode Used in Content (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp shortcodes-in-use" command that scans all content and lists each shortcode tag found, how many posts use it and whether anything is still registered to handle it.
snippets.notes: Tags marked "missing" print as raw text on the site, usually because the plugin that provided them was removed.

snippets.title: Find the Heaviest Posts by Content Size (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp heaviest-posts" command listing the posts and pages with the largest stored content, revisions excluded, to track down pasted base64 images or page builder bloat slowing the editor.
snippets.notes: Example "wp heaviest-posts --limit=20 --format=csv".

snippets.title: List Every Database Query on a Page for Administrators
snippets.description: When SAVEQUERIES is enabled, lets administrators add ?wpide_queries=1 to a front-end URL to see every SQL query of the page with its time and calling function, slowest first.
snippets.notes: Add define( 'SAVEQUERIES', true ); to wp-config.php while debugging only, as it uses extra memory on every request.

snippets.title: Searchable Options Viewer Under Tools
snippets.description: Adds a Tools > Options Viewer screen where administrators can search the options table by name and see each value decoded and pretty-printed, including serialized arrays that Settings > All hides.
snippets.notes: Read-only; values that look like keys, tokens or passwords are masked.

snippets.title: Add Your Own Setting to the Customizer
snippets.description: Adds a "Site extras" section to Appearance > Customize with a footer note and a contact phone field that preview live, and makes them available with a [site_extra] shortcode, as a pattern for your own settings.
snippets.notes: Use [site_extra key="phone"] or get_theme_mod( 'wpide_phone' ) in templates; block themes need the Customize menu brought back to edit them.

snippets.title: Site Settings Object for Your Front-End Scripts
snippets.description: Prints a small window.siteSettings object with the home URL, REST API root, AJAX URL, language and, for logged-in users, a REST nonce, so your custom JavaScript never hard-codes addresses.
snippets.notes: Read it in your scripts as window.siteSettings.restUrl; add your own values to the $data array.

snippets.title: Load a JavaScript Module Only Where It Is Needed
snippets.description: Registers a native JavaScript module with WordPress's Script Modules API and loads it only on pages that contain a chosen block, so modern ES module code needs no bundler and costs nothing elsewhere.
snippets.notes: Needs WordPress 6.5+; put your module file at wp-content/js/site.js (or change $wpide_module_url) and set the block that triggers it.

snippets.title: Cache Any Expensive Result With One Function
snippets.description: Adds a wpide_remember() helper that returns a cached value if there is one, or runs your function, stores the result for a set time and returns it, which makes caching slow queries and API calls a one-liner.
snippets.notes: Example $top = wpide_remember( 'top_posts', HOUR_IN_SECONDS, function () { return get_posts( ... ); } ); call wpide_forget( 'top_posts' ) to clear it.

snippets.title: Admin Color Scheme per User Role
snippets.description: Gives each role its own admin color scheme, for example blue for editors and coffee for shop managers, so people instantly see which kind of account they are using.
snippets.notes: Roles not listed keep each user's own choice; scheme names: fresh, light, modern, blue, coffee, ectoplasm, midnight, ocean, sunrise.

snippets.title: Scheduled Posts Count in the Admin Menu
snippets.description: Shows a small counter next to Posts in the admin menu with the number of scheduled posts waiting to go live, so the publishing queue is visible from every screen.
snippets.notes: Uses WordPress's cached post counts, so it adds no extra queries on most screens.

snippets.title: Remember Your Filters in Admin Lists
snippets.description: Brings back the status, category, author, search and sorting you last used when you return to the Posts, Pages or Media list, instead of starting from "All" every time.
snippets.notes: Click the post type menu link twice, or "All", to clear the remembered filters; stored per user and per screen.

snippets.title: Ask Before Moving Posts to the Trash
snippets.description: Shows a confirmation dialog when someone clicks "Trash" under a post, page or media item, or applies the Move to Trash bulk action, to prevent accidental removals.
snippets.notes: Items in the trash can still be restored for 30 days; this only adds a safety prompt.

snippets.title: Sort the Pages List Alphabetically by Default
snippets.description: Opens Pages sorted by title from A to Z instead of the default order, which makes finding a page on large sites much faster. Clicking a column header still sorts as usual.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_alpha_post_types to sort other post types alphabetically as well.

snippets.title: Search Box for the Admin Menu
snippets.description: Adds a small filter box at the top of the admin menu that hides every menu and submenu item not matching what you type, handy on sites with dozens of plugin menus.
snippets.notes: Press Escape to clear the filter; the box is hidden while the menu is collapsed.

snippets.title: Bookmark Admin Screens in the Admin Bar
snippets.description: Adds a star menu to the admin bar where each user can bookmark the admin screen they are on, such as a plugin's settings or a filtered list, and jump back to it from anywhere.
snippets.notes: Bookmarks are saved per user (up to 15); use "Remove this page" in the menu to delete one.

snippets.title: Floating "Edit This Page" Button on the Front End
snippets.description: Shows a small floating Edit button in the corner of posts and pages for users who can edit them, which is handy when the admin bar is hidden or on phones.
snippets.notes: Change the corner with $wpide_edit_button_side (left or right); it respects the visitor's reduced motion setting.

snippets.title: Comments On/Off Switch in the Posts List
snippets.description: Adds a column to the Posts list with a switch that opens or closes comments on each post in one click, without opening the editor or Quick Edit.
snippets.notes: Only users who can edit the post can flip the switch.

snippets.title: Bulk Remove Featured Images
snippets.description: Adds a "Remove featured image" bulk action to post and page lists that clears the featured image from all selected items at once, without deleting the images from the Media Library.
snippets.notes: The images stay in the Media Library and can be set again at any time.

snippets.title: Stop Authors Editing Posts After They Are Published
snippets.description: Lets authors and contributors write and submit posts as usual, but once a post is published only editors and administrators can change it, which keeps approved content approved.
snippets.notes: Set $wpide_lock_after_days to give authors a grace period, for example 1 day to fix typos.

snippets.title: Default Category per Author
snippets.description: Pre-selects a category for new posts based on who writes them, for example "Recipes" for your food writer, so posts land in the right section without anyone remembering to tick it.
snippets.notes: Map user logins to category slugs in $wpide_author_categories; writers can still change it before publishing.

snippets.title: Limit the Number of Tags per Post
snippets.description: Keeps only the first few tags on each post when it is saved, so tag lists stay focused and tag archives do not fill with one-off tags. Writers see a note when extra tags are dropped.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_max_tags; the order is the order in which the tags were added.

snippets.title: "Minor Edit" Option That Keeps the Last Updated Date
snippets.description: Adds a "Minor edit" checkbox to the block editor; when ticked, fixing a typo does not change the post's last modified date, so "Updated on" labels and sitemaps only change for real updates.
snippets.notes: The checkbox resets after each save; works with the block editor and the REST API.

snippets.title: Remove Inline Styles From Pasted Content on Save
snippets.description: Cleans up formatting pasted from Word, Google Docs and web pages when a post is saved, removing inline fonts, colors and sizes, font tags, bare spans and Office classes so text follows your theme.
snippets.notes: Text alignment and blocks styled through their own settings are kept; administrators can opt out with $wpide_clean_skip_admins.

snippets.title: Warn When a Post Title Is Already Used
snippets.description: Shows a warning in the block editor when another post or page already has the same title, so you avoid confusing duplicates in search results, menus and your own lists.
snippets.notes: The check runs a moment after you stop typing and looks at published, scheduled and draft items of the same type.

snippets.title: Attached Files List Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds an [attached_files] shortcode that lists every PDF, document or other file uploaded to the current post as download links with file type and size, ideal for resources and meeting minutes.
snippets.notes: Example [attached_files type="application/pdf" title="Downloads"]; images are skipped unless you add images="yes".

snippets.title: Recently Updated Posts Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds a [recently_updated] shortcode that lists the posts most recently revised, with the date they were updated, to show readers that older guides are being kept fresh.
snippets.notes: Example [recently_updated count="5" post_type="post,page"]; posts edited within a day of publishing are skipped so new posts do not crowd the list.

snippets.title: Authors List Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds an [authors_list] shortcode that shows everyone who has published posts, with avatar, short bio and number of posts, linking to each author's archive, for "Our writers" pages.
snippets.notes: Example [authors_list orderby="post_count" bio="yes"]; users with no published posts are left out.

snippets.title: "On This Day" Posts Shortcode
snippets.description: Adds an [on_this_day] shortcode that lists posts published on today's date in previous years, a simple way to resurface archive content on the homepage or in a sidebar.
snippets.notes: Shows nothing on days with no matches; add text="..." to change the intro line. The list is cached until midnight.

snippets.title: Search Result Preview in the Block Editor
snippets.description: Adds a panel to the editor sidebar that previews how the post may look as a search engine result, with its title, address and description, updating live as you edit the title and excerpt.
snippets.notes: Uses the excerpt (or the opening text) as the description; SEO plugins with their own preview may make this redundant.

snippets.title: "More From This Author" Block
snippets.description: Registers a server-rendered block that lists the latest posts by the current post's author, excluding the post being read, to keep readers with writers they like.
snippets.notes: Set how many posts to show in the block settings; place it in the single post template of a block theme or inside a post.

snippets.title: Load Block Patterns From a Folder of HTML Files
snippets.description: Registers every .html file in wp-content/patterns/ as a block pattern, using the file name as its title, so designers can add patterns by dropping in markup copied from the editor.
snippets.notes: Copy blocks in the editor (Options > Copy), paste them into a file such as hero-banner.html, and it appears under "Site patterns" in the inserter.

snippets.title: Content-Only Editing of Pages for Non-Administrators
snippets.description: Locks the layout of pages in the block editor for everyone except administrators, so editors can change text and images but cannot move, delete or restyle blocks and break the design.
snippets.notes: Applies to the post types in $wpide_content_only_types; administrators edit normally.

snippets.title: Excerpt Length Counter in the Block Editor
snippets.description: Shows a live character and word count under a short preview of the excerpt in the editor sidebar, colored when it is too short or too long for search results and post cards.
snippets.notes: Adjust $wpide_excerpt_min and $wpide_excerpt_max (characters) to match your theme's cards.

snippets.title: Image Guidelines Note in the Upload Screens
snippets.description: Shows a short note with your image rules, such as recommended sizes, file types and the need for alt text, right inside the media uploader and Media > Add New screen.
snippets.notes: Edit $wpide_upload_guidance; basic HTML such as strong and a links is allowed.

snippets.title: Export the Media Library List to CSV
snippets.description: Adds an "Export to CSV" bulk action to the Media Library list view that downloads the selected files with their URL, title, alt text, caption, type, size, dimensions and upload date.
snippets.notes: Handy for accessibility audits and migrations; switch the library to list view to see bulk actions.

snippets.title: Download Selected Media Files as a ZIP
snippets.description: Adds a "Download as ZIP" bulk action to the Media Library list view that packs the selected original files into one archive, handy for sending a batch of photos or documents to someone.
snippets.notes: Needs the PHP Zip extension; limited to 200 MB of files per download to protect the server.

snippets.title: Store Each User's Uploads in Their Own Folder
snippets.description: Saves uploads into a folder named after the uploader, such as uploads/users/jane/2025/03/, which keeps multi-author and client sites tidy and makes per-person cleanups easy.
snippets.notes: Only affects new uploads; existing files stay where they are. Uses the user's nicename, never their email.

snippets.title: Add an Embed Provider WordPress Does Not Support
snippets.description: Teaches WordPress to embed links from an extra service that offers oEmbed, such as a podcast host, video platform or design tool, so pasting its URL on its own line shows the player.
snippets.notes: Replace the example with the service's URL pattern and oEmbed endpoint from its documentation; only add services you trust, as they inject HTML into your pages.

snippets.title: Protect Featured Images From Deletion
snippets.description: Stops anyone from permanently deleting an image while it is still the featured image of a post or page, and shows which post uses it, so articles never end up with a missing picture.
snippets.notes: Remove the image as featured image first (or use another), then it can be deleted.

snippets.title: Your Writing Stats Widget
snippets.description: Adds a personal dashboard widget showing how many posts and words you published this month and this year, plus your current number of drafts, a small motivation boost for writers.
snippets.notes: Words are counted from published post content; figures are cached per user for an hour.

snippets.title: Comments per Day Chart Widget
snippets.description: Adds a dashboard widget with a simple bar chart of approved comments for each of the last 30 days, so you can see at a glance whether reader engagement is growing.
snippets.notes: Pure HTML and CSS; data is cached for an hour.

snippets.title: Embed an External Analytics Dashboard
snippets.description: Adds a dashboard widget that shows a shared dashboard from another service, such as a public Plausible, Looker Studio or uptime status page, so clients see their numbers without another login.
snippets.notes: Paste the service's public share or embed link into $wpide_embed_url; the service must allow being shown in a frame.

snippets.title: Countdown to a Launch or Deadline Widget
snippets.description: Adds a dashboard widget counting down the days and hours to a date you set, such as a site launch, campaign start or content deadline, to keep the whole team focused.
snippets.notes: Set the date and time in your site's time zone; after the date passes the widget shows a "done" message.

snippets.title: "Since Your Last Visit" Dashboard Widget
snippets.description: Adds a dashboard widget listing what happened since you last logged in to the admin: new posts by others, new comments and new users, so you catch up in seconds.
snippets.notes: Your last visit is recorded at most once an hour, so short breaks do not reset the list.

snippets.title: Allow Application Passwords on Local Sites Without HTTPS
snippets.description: Turns on Application Passwords for local and development copies of the site that run on plain http, so you can test REST API integrations and apps locally the same way as in production.
snippets.notes: Only applies when WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE is local or development; production keeps WordPress's HTTPS requirement.

snippets.title: Keep Plugin Deprecation Notices Out of debug.log
snippets.description: Stops PHP deprecation notices coming from plugins and themes from filling debug.log, so the real warnings and errors you are looking for stand out while debugging.
snippets.notes: Only E_DEPRECATED and E_USER_DEPRECATED from wp-content are silenced; WordPress core notices and all other errors are logged as before.

snippets.title: Export Posts to a JSON File (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp export-json" command that writes published posts with their title, slug, dates, content, excerpt, categories, tags, featured image and author to a JSON file, for static sites, apps or archiving.
snippets.notes: Example "wp export-json --post_type=page --file=pages.json"; without --file the JSON is printed.

snippets.title: Site Identity REST Endpoint for Apps and Headless Sites
snippets.description: Adds a public /wp-json/site/v1/identity endpoint with the site name, tagline, logo, site icon, language and home URL, so headless front ends and apps can brand themselves from WordPress.
snippets.notes: Only public information is returned; the response can be cached by browsers for an hour.

snippets.title: Show the Current Git Branch in the Admin Bar
snippets.description: Shows which Git branch and commit the site or theme is running in the admin bar for administrators, so developers always know what code is deployed on each copy.
snippets.notes: Looks for a .git folder in the site root, then in the active theme; nothing is shown when neither exists. No shell commands are run.

snippets.title: Load Missing Media From the Live Site on Local Copies
snippets.description: On local, development and staging copies, images and files that are not in the local uploads folder are loaded from the live site instead, so you do not need to download gigabytes of uploads.
snippets.notes: Set $wpide_live_url to your production address; it never runs on production and only rewrites URLs whose file is missing locally.

snippets.title: Copy a Post as a Page (or Any Other Post Type)
snippets.description: Adds a "Copy as page" link under posts, and "Copy as post" under pages, that creates a draft of the other type with the same content and featured image, while the original stays untouched.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_copy_targets to offer other post types, for example 'post' => 'product'; categories and tags are only copied when the target type uses them.

snippets.title: Reminder to Remove Inactive Plugins
snippets.description: Shows administrators a gentle notice on the Dashboard and Plugins screens when plugins have been left inactive, since unused plugins still need updates and can be a security risk.
snippets.notes: Add plugins you keep inactive on purpose to $wpide_inactive_allowed; the notice can be dismissed for 30 days.

snippets.title: Share a Draft With a Secret Link
snippets.description: Adds a "Share draft" link under unpublished posts that creates a secret preview address, so a client or reviewer can read the draft without a WordPress account. Links expire after a set number of days.
snippets.notes: Change $wpide_share_days; publishing the post or clicking "Stop sharing" disables the link. Shared drafts are marked noindex.

snippets.title: "Preview" Banner on Unpublished Content
snippets.description: Shows a clear banner at the top of the page whenever someone previews a draft, pending or scheduled post, so reviewers never mistake a preview for the live page or share it by accident.
snippets.notes: Only shown to logged-in users viewing a preview; scheduled posts also show their publish date.

snippets.title: Require a Title Before Publishing
snippets.description: Prevents posts and pages from being published or scheduled without a title, avoiding "(no title)" entries in menus, feeds, search results and social shares.
snippets.notes: Drafts without a title can still be saved; add other post types to $wpide_title_required_types.

snippets.title: Hide the Featured Image on Selected Posts
snippets.description: Adds a "Hide featured image on this post" checkbox to the editor, so a post can keep its image for archives, social shares and related posts but not repeat it at the top of the article.
snippets.notes: Works with themes that print the featured image with the standard functions and with the Post Featured Image block in block themes.

snippets.title: Upgrade http:// Links to Your Own Site to https://
snippets.description: Rewrites old http:// links and images pointing to your own domain to https:// when content is displayed, fixing "not secure" mixed content warnings after moving to SSL without editing every post.
snippets.notes: Only your own domain is changed; a database search and replace is still the permanent fix.

snippets.title: Image Sizes REST Endpoint for Headless Front Ends
snippets.description: Adds a public /wp-json/site/v1/image-sizes endpoint listing every registered image size with its width, height and crop setting, so headless front ends can pick the right size for each layout.
snippets.notes: Read-only and cached by browsers for a day; sizes added by themes and plugins are included.

snippets.title: Mark Each Block in the Page Source for Administrators
snippets.description: Wraps every rendered block in HTML comments with its name, such as core/group or a plugin's block, when an administrator views a page with ?wpide_blocks=1, to see which block produced which markup.
snippets.notes: View the page source after adding ?wpide_blocks=1 to the address; visitors never see the comments.

snippets.title: Show PHP Errors to Administrators With ?debug=1
snippets.description: Lets administrators see PHP warnings and notices on screen by adding ?wpide_debug=1 to any address, while visitors and other users never see them, even with WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY off.
snippets.notes: Errors raised before WordPress knows who is logged in (very early in loading) are not shown; check debug.log for those.

snippets.title: "In Menus" Column for Pages
snippets.description: Adds a column to the Pages list showing which navigation menus link to each page, so editors know before renaming, moving or deleting a page that it appears in the site's menus.
snippets.notes: Covers classic menus (Appearance > Menus); links inside Navigation blocks of block themes are not listed.

snippets.title: Tag Posts Automatically From a Keyword List
snippets.description: Adds tags to posts when they are saved if the title or content mentions keywords you define, for example tagging every post that mentions "WooCommerce" or "Gutenberg", so tagging stays consistent.
snippets.notes: Map keywords to tag names in $wpide_keyword_tags; matching is whole-word and case-insensitive, and existing tags are never removed.

snippets.title: Use a Photo's Embedded Description as Its Alt Text
snippets.description: Fills the alt text of newly uploaded photos from the description or headline embedded by cameras, photo agencies and Lightroom (IPTC data), when it exists and no alt text is set.
snippets.notes: Agency captions can be long; the alt text is trimmed to 25 words. Photos without embedded text are left for you to describe.

snippets.title: Find Insecure http:// Links in Content (WP-CLI)
snippets.description: Adds a "wp find-http-links" command that lists posts containing http:// images, scripts or links, marking which point to your own domain, to clean up mixed content after moving to HTTPS.
snippets.notes: Add --own to list only links to your own domain, which can usually be switched to https:// safely.

snippets.title: Generate a Custom Image Size Only for One Post Type
snippets.description: Registers an image size, such as a wide portfolio banner, but only creates it for images uploaded to that post type, so every other upload is not stored in yet another size.
snippets.notes: The size is created when you upload from inside a post of that type (the image is "attached" to it); set the name, dimensions and post type below.

snippets.title: Let Other Sites Read Your Feeds With JavaScript
snippets.description: Sends a CORS header with your RSS and Atom feeds, so web apps, widgets and dashboards on other domains can load them with fetch() instead of hitting a browser error.
snippets.notes: Set the origins list to specific sites, such as your app's address, to allow only them; feeds are public, so '*' is safe for most sites.

snippets.title: Send Feed Readers to Your Feed Service
snippets.description: Redirects visitors and feed readers from your main feed to its address at a feed service such as FeedPress or Follow.it, while the service itself still reads your real feed.
snippets.notes: Off until you fill in the service address. Point the service at /feed/?origin-feed=1 if its user agent is not in the list.

snippets.title: Custom Field Values in Feed Items
snippets.description: Adds the custom fields you choose, such as an event date or location, to each RSS item as its own element, for newsletter tools, aggregators and partner sites that read your feed.
snippets.notes: The field list is empty by default; add field keys and the element names to use. Password-protected posts are skipped.

snippets.title: Copyright and Contact Details in Your Feeds
snippets.description: Adds a copyright notice to your RSS and Atom feeds, plus optional editor and webmaster contact addresses, which feed directories and readers show alongside your feed.
snippets.notes: {year} and {site} in the copyright text are replaced automatically; leave the email lines empty to skip them.

snippets.title: Reading Time in Feed Items
snippets.description: Shows an estimated reading time such as "4 min read" at the start of each item in your feeds, so subscribers know how long an article takes before they open it.
snippets.notes: Change the words-per-minute value to match your audience; shortcodes and HTML are left out of the word count.

snippets.title: Most Discussed Posts Feed
snippets.description: Publishes a second feed at /feed/popular/ listing your posts with the most comments from recent months, handy for "popular this month" newsletters and sidebar widgets on other sites.
snippets.notes: After activating, visit Settings > Permalinks and click Save so /feed/popular/ works; the list is cached for an hour.

snippets.title: Keep Old Feed Addresses Working After Moving to WordPress
snippets.description: Redirects feed addresses used by Blogger, Ghost, Jekyll, Hugo and other platforms, such as /rss.xml or /feeds/posts/default, to your WordPress feed, so existing subscribers keep receiving posts.
snippets.notes: Only addresses that would otherwise be a 404 are redirected; add any other old feed paths to the list.

snippets.title: Category Name Before Feed Item Titles
snippets.description: Puts the post's category in front of each title in your feeds, for example "[Recipes] Easy Pancakes", so subscribers can scan topics at a glance.
snippets.notes: The default "Uncategorized" category is skipped; change the format string to use another style, such as "Recipes: ".

snippets.title: Keep Certain Authors' Posts Out of Feeds
snippets.description: Leaves posts by the authors you list, such as guest writers or an automated account, out of your main feeds, while their author feed and the posts on the site stay available.
snippets.notes: The author list is empty by default; add user IDs or usernames.

snippets.title: Sponsor Message Inside Feed Items
snippets.description: Places a short sponsor or promotion message after the first paragraph of every item in your feeds, where RSS readers and RSS-to-email newsletters will show it.
snippets.notes: Nothing is added until you write the message; you can limit it to posts in certain categories.

snippets.title: Hashtags From Tags in Feed Items
snippets.description: Turns each post's tags into hashtags such as #HomeOffice at the end of the feed summary, so RSS-to-social tools like Buffer, Zapier or IFTTT post them automatically.
snippets.notes: Set the place to 'both' to add the hashtags to the full content as well; the number of hashtags is capped at four by default.

snippets.title: Show Widgets Only on Certain Page Types
snippets.description: Adds a "Show on" setting to every classic widget, so you can limit it to the homepage, single posts, blog and archive pages, or everywhere except those.
snippets.notes: Works with classic widgets and the Legacy Widget block; block widgets do not get the setting.

snippets.title: Schedule Widgets With Start and End Dates
snippets.description: Adds "Show from" and "Show until" date fields to every classic widget, so a promotion, event notice or holiday message appears and disappears on its own.
snippets.notes: Times use the time zone in Settings > General; a page cache may keep showing a widget until the cache is cleared.

snippets.title: Most Discussed Posts Widget
snippets.description: Adds a "Most Discussed Posts" widget that lists the posts with the most comments, all-time or from the last few weeks, with optional comment counts.
snippets.notes: Add it under Appearance > Widgets (as a Legacy Widget in the block editor); results are cached for an hour.

snippets.title: About the Author Widget
snippets.description: Adds an "About the Author" sidebar widget that shows the current post author's photo, bio and a link to their other posts, and hides itself on other pages.
snippets.notes: The bio comes from Users > Profile > Biographical Info; the photo is the author's Gravatar or avatar.

snippets.title: Recent Posts Widget Includes Custom Post Types
snippets.description: Makes the Recent Posts widget list your custom post types, such as portfolio items, recipes or events, together with blog posts.
snippets.notes: Leave the list empty to include every public custom post type, or name the exact types to show.

snippets.title: Hide Pingbacks From the Recent Comments Widget
snippets.description: Leaves pingbacks and trackbacks out of the Recent Comments widget and the Latest Comments block, so they show only real conversations.
snippets.notes: Also filters out other special comment types, such as WooCommerce order notes.

snippets.title: Categories Widget: Top Level Only, Busiest First
snippets.description: Makes the Categories widget list only top-level categories and sorts them by number of posts, so a long category tree becomes a short list of your main sections.
snippets.notes: Switch either setting off at the top of the snippet; works for both the list and the dropdown version of the widget.

snippets.title: Link Widget Titles to a Page
snippets.description: Adds a "Title link" field to every classic widget, turning its title into a link, for example from "Latest News" to your news page.
snippets.notes: Core widgets show the link; third-party widgets that escape their own titles may show the title as plain text.

snippets.title: Social Profiles Widget
snippets.description: Adds a "Social Profiles" widget with links to your profiles on Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok, Bluesky, Mastodon and more, as an accessible list of text links.
snippets.notes: Leave a network empty to hide it; links carry rel="me" so Mastodon can verify your site.

snippets.title: Featured Post Widget
snippets.description: Adds a "Featured Post" widget that highlights one post or page you pick, shown as a card with its featured image, excerpt and a read-more link.
snippets.notes: The widget hides itself on the featured post's own page and when the post is unpublished.

snippets.title: Random Quote Widget
snippets.description: Adds a "Random Quote" widget that shows a different quote, tip or testimonial from your list on each page view, with the source shown below it.
snippets.notes: Write one quote per line as "Quote — Source"; with a page cache, the quote changes when the cache refreshes.

snippets.title: Widget Area Above the Footer
snippets.description: Registers an "Above the Footer" widget area and shows its widgets in a responsive row just above the site footer, in classic and block themes.
snippets.notes: Classic themes print it when they load footer.php; block themes get it before the footer template part.

snippets.title: Fix URLs With Double Slashes
snippets.description: Permanently redirects addresses that contain double slashes, such as /blog//my-post/, to the clean version, avoiding duplicate pages from broken links and badly built URLs.
snippets.notes: The query string is kept as it is.

snippets.title: Redirect Visitors by Country
snippets.description: Sends visitors from the countries you choose to a regional site or page, using the country header added by Cloudflare, CloudFront or your host, with search engine crawlers left alone.
snippets.notes: Off until you add countries. Needs a host or CDN that sends a country header; page caches must vary by country. Visitors can opt out with ?stay=1.

snippets.title: Smart App Download Link
snippets.description: Turns an address such as /app/ into one link for posters and QR codes: iPhone visitors go to the App Store, Android visitors to Google Play and everyone else to a page you choose.
snippets.notes: Off until you add your store links; without a desktop address, desktop visitors see the page at that address, if any.

snippets.title: Short /go/ Links for Affiliate and Partner URLs
snippets.description: Creates short links such as /go/amazon/ that redirect to long affiliate or partner URLs, so links in posts stay tidy and you can update a destination in one place.
snippets.notes: Uses temporary 307 redirects with noindex and a robots.txt rule; real pages at the same address always win.

snippets.title: Redirect Trashed Posts to Their Category
snippets.description: Remembers the address of each post or page you move to the trash and sends later visitors to its category, parent page or the blog page instead of a 404, even after the trash is emptied.
snippets.notes: Restoring a post removes its redirect; up to 500 addresses are remembered.

snippets.title: Redirect Missing Pages to the Nearest Parent Page
snippets.description: When an address like /services/old-offer/ no longer exists, sends visitors to the closest existing level above it, such as /services/, instead of a dead end.
snippets.notes: Needs pretty permalinks; missing files such as images are skipped. Set the status to 302 while you test.

snippets.title: Redirects From a CSV File
snippets.description: Reads redirect rules from a redirects.csv file in wp-content, one "old path, new address, status" line each, so you can manage hundreds of redirects in a spreadsheet without a plugin.
snippets.notes: Nothing happens until the file exists; it is re-read only when it changes. Supports 301, 302, 307, 308 and 410.

snippets.title: /latest/ Link to Your Newest Post
snippets.description: Makes /latest/ always open your newest post and /latest/category-name/ the newest post in that category, a link that never goes stale for social bios, emails and QR codes.
snippets.notes: Only used when no real page has that address; change the path at the top of the snippet.

snippets.title: Return 410 Gone for Removed Pages
snippets.description: Answers requests for pages you deleted on purpose with a "410 Gone" status instead of a 404, so search engines drop them from results faster.
snippets.notes: The list is empty by default; only addresses that are already missing get the 410, so live content is never hidden.

snippets.title: /random/ Link to a Random Post
snippets.description: Makes /random/ open a random published post, a fun "Surprise me" link for menus that keeps readers exploring your archive.
snippets.notes: Picks from your 500 newest posts by default; only used when no real page has that address.

snippets.title: Send Page Numbers Past the End to the Last Page
snippets.description: When someone opens a page number that no longer exists, such as /category/news/page/40/ after you deleted posts, sends them to the real last page instead of a 404.
snippets.notes: Works for the blog page, archives and search results.

snippets.title: Redirect Missing Resized Images to the Original
snippets.description: Sends requests for resized images that no longer exist, such as photo-300x200.jpg after a theme change, to the original upload, fixing broken images in old posts and on other sites.
snippets.notes: Only works when your web server passes missing upload files to WordPress, as the default Apache setup does.

snippets.title: Redirect Old AMP Addresses After Removing AMP
snippets.description: After you stop using an AMP plugin, permanently redirects the old /amp/ and ?amp=1 addresses to the normal pages, so search engines and shared links do not hit errors.
snippets.notes: Does nothing while an AMP plugin is active.

snippets.title: Show Pages Before Posts in Search Results
snippets.description: Lists matching pages first in search results, then blog posts, then other content, so key pages like pricing or contact are not buried under older posts.
snippets.notes: Change the order list to rank other types, such as product or docs, at the top.

snippets.title: Search Synonyms
snippets.description: Makes searches for one word also find posts that use another word with the same meaning, for example "sofa" also finds "couch", using groups you define.
snippets.notes: The list is empty by default; add groups of words. Searches with -exclusions or exact phrases are left to WordPress.

snippets.title: Category Dropdown in the Search Form
snippets.description: Adds a category dropdown to the site search form and the Search block, so visitors can search all content or only one category.
snippets.notes: Do not combine with the Search Within the Current Category snippet; both use the same field.

snippets.title: "Did You Mean" Suggestions for Empty Searches
snippets.description: When a search finds nothing, suggests a corrected spelling based on the words in your post titles, such as "Did you mean chocolate brownies?", with a link to search again.
snippets.notes: Works best for Latin-alphabet words; the word list is cached for a day and refreshed when you publish.

snippets.title: Content Type Labels in Search Results
snippets.description: Shows a small label such as "Page", "Post" or "Product" in front of each search result title, so visitors can tell results apart at a glance.
snippets.notes: Uses the singular name of each post type; works with themes that use the standard entry-title or Post Title block classes.

snippets.title: Include PDFs and Documents in Search Results
snippets.description: Lets the site search find PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files from the Media Library by their title, caption and description, alongside posts and pages.
snippets.notes: Files attached to unpublished content stay hidden. Add 'image/' to the type list to include images too.

snippets.title: Custom Stop Words for Site Search
snippets.description: Ignores filler words such as "can", "my" or "need" in multi-word searches, so "how can I reset my password" finds posts about resetting passwords.
snippets.notes: WordPress only drops stop words from searches with several words; list words that matter on your site under the keep list.

snippets.title: Search Posts by Author Name
snippets.description: Makes the site search also return posts written by authors whose name matches the search, so "maria" finds everything by Maria Lopez.
snippets.notes: Matches display names of users who have published posts, for searches of three characters or more.

snippets.title: Search Within the Current Category
snippets.description: On category pages, adds an "Only in [category]" checkbox to the search form and Search block, ticked by default, so visitors can search just that section.
snippets.notes: Do not combine with the Category Dropdown in the Search Form snippet; both use the same field.

snippets.title: Leave Noindexed Content Out of Site Search
snippets.description: Hides posts and pages that you set to noindex in Yoast SEO or Rank Math from your own site search, such as thank-you pages and thin landing pages.
snippets.notes: Uses each post's own robots setting; content type-wide noindex settings in the SEO plugin are not checked.

snippets.title: Only Recent Blog Posts in Search Results
snippets.description: Leaves blog posts older than three years out of search results, while pages and other content types stay searchable, which suits news sites and fast-moving topics.
snippets.notes: Change the number of months at the top; old posts remain reachable through archives and links.

snippets.title: Send Certain Searches Straight to a Page
snippets.description: Opens a chosen page directly when someone searches for an exact word or phrase, for example "contact" goes to your contact page and "returns" to your returns policy.
snippets.notes: The list is empty by default; matching ignores capital letters and extra spaces, and only whole searches match.

snippets.title: Author Bio at the Top of Author Archives
snippets.description: Shows the author's photo, name, number of posts, bio and website at the top of their author archive, turning it into a proper profile page.
snippets.notes: Classic themes get it above the first post, block themes after the archive title; it appears on the first page only.

snippets.title: Intro Text for Custom Post Type Archives
snippets.description: Adds an "Archive intros" section to Settings > Reading where you can write an introduction for each custom post type archive, such as Portfolio or Recipes, shown at the top of that archive.
snippets.notes: Only post types with an archive are listed. Classic themes need to show the archive description; block themes get it after the archive title.

snippets.title: 404 for Author Pages of Users Without Posts
snippets.description: Returns a 404 for the author archive of anyone who has never published, such as subscribers and customers, so their usernames and empty profile pages are not exposed.
snippets.notes: Authors get their archive back as soon as they publish something.

snippets.title: Oldest Posts First in Selected Categories
snippets.description: Lists posts in the categories you choose from oldest to newest, so serialized stories, courses and step-by-step series read in the right order.
snippets.notes: The category list is empty by default; add the slugs of your series categories.

snippets.title: Show Custom Post Types in Year and Month Archives
snippets.description: Makes yearly, monthly and daily archives also list custom post type entries, such as recipes or events, not just blog posts.
snippets.notes: Leave the list empty to include every public custom post type that has an archive, or name the exact types.

snippets.title: Sort Menu for Blog and Archive Pages
snippets.description: Adds a "Sort by" menu above the blog and archive lists so visitors can switch between newest, oldest, A to Z and most discussed posts.
snippets.notes: Sorted pages are marked noindex so search engines keep the default order; edit the list to offer other sorts.

snippets.title: Header Images for Categories
snippets.description: Adds an image picker to categories and shows the chosen image as a banner at the top of each category archive.
snippets.notes: Classic themes get it above the posts, block themes before the archive title; it shows on the first page only.

snippets.title: Visual Editor for Category and Tag Descriptions
snippets.description: Replaces the plain description box on the category and tag edit screens with the visual editor, and keeps headings, lists, images and links that WordPress would otherwise strip.
snippets.notes: Your theme must display term descriptions; add other taxonomies to the list at the top.

snippets.title: Subcategories Use Their Parent Category's Template
snippets.description: Makes subcategories use the parent category's custom template, such as category-news.php or a "category-news" block template, when they do not have their own.
snippets.notes: Also works for hierarchical custom taxonomies; the subcategory's own template still wins when it exists.

snippets.title: Year Headings in Blog and Archive Lists
snippets.description: Inserts a year heading such as "2024" between posts whenever the year changes on blog and archive pages, making long date-ordered lists easier to scan.
snippets.notes: For classic themes; lists sorted by something other than date get no headings.

snippets.title: "View All" Link on Paginated Archives
snippets.description: Adds a "View all 42 posts on one page" link under paginated category, tag and other archives that are not too large, for readers who prefer to scroll or search the page.
snippets.notes: Only shown for archives up to 150 posts; the single-page version is marked noindex.

snippets.title: Only Top-Level Items on Hierarchical Post Type Archives
snippets.description: Lists only parent items on the archive of hierarchical post types, such as services with sub-services, so child items do not crowd the overview.
snippets.notes: Leave the list empty to apply to every hierarchical post type archive, or name the exact types.

packs.title: Security hardening
packs.description: Close common attack surfaces: XML-RPC, version leaks, user enumeration, the file editors and login probing.

packs.title: Performance essentials
packs.description: Remove scripts and requests most sites do not need, and tune revisions and the Heartbeat API.

packs.title: Turn off comments
packs.description: Remove comments, pingbacks, trackbacks, comment feeds and comment emails everywhere.

packs.title: Clean, branded admin
packs.description: A calmer dashboard: no WordPress branding, default widgets or help tabs, with your own footer text and greeting.

packs.title: Client handoff
packs.description: Hand a site to a client safely: hide technical menus and update notices, block installs and editors, and label the environment.

packs.title: Branded login page
packs.description: Your logo, colors and link on the login page, a cleaner form and a remembered session.

packs.title: SEO basics
packs.description: Meta descriptions, social sharing tags, structured data and sensible noindex rules when you do not run an SEO plugin.

packs.title: WooCommerce cleanup
packs.description: Lighter WooCommerce: assets only on shop pages, no marketplace suggestions, simpler checkout and automatic completion of virtual orders.

packs.title: Better blog reading
packs.description: Last updated dates, related posts, an author box, a reading progress bar and external links in a new tab.

packs.title: Developer toolkit
packs.description: Template name in the admin bar, query counts in the page source, useful body classes and an environment badge.
